work_packages.title: FFmpeg 8.1.x shared-bundle CI build + `just ffmpeg-fetch`
work_packages.scope:
- Workflow + scripts (`ci/ffmpeg/build-{windows,macos,linux}.sh`) building the **pinned FFmpeg 8.1.x as shared libraries per OS** (win-x64, macOS arm64, Linux x64). **The Linux bundle is built in an Ubuntu 22.04 container (glibc 2.35)** to honour ADR-014. GPL build (`--enable-gpl --enable-version3`) with **required** libraries: `libx264, libx265, libsvtav1, libvpx, libopus, libmp3lame, libvidstab, libzimg, libsoxr, libass`; native encoders `prores_ks`, `dnxhd`, `gif` available; per-OS hwaccels: Windows `d3d11va, dxva2, nvdec/nvenc (ffnvcodec), amf, qsv(libvpl)`, macOS `videotoolbox`, Linux `vaapi, nvdec/nvenc (ffnvcodec), qsv(libvpl)`. Version, source tarball sha256 and the full `configure` line are recorded in `ci/ffmpeg/VERSION.toml`.
- Publishes each bundle (headers, import libs, shared libs, `configure.txt`, source tarball, license) as a GitHub Release asset with sha256 manifest `ci/ffmpeg/bundles.toml`; the source tarball and configure line are published alongside (GPL compliance, arch §21).
- `just ffmpeg-fetch` (delegates to `cargo xtask fetch-ffmpeg`): downloads the pinned bundle for the host OS into `.ffmpeg/`, verifies sha256, emits an env file setting `FFMPEG_DIR`; idempotent. Developers may instead use brew/distro `libav*-dev` for quick hacking (06-dev-process §2): documented, not CI-supported.
- CI jobs needing FFmpeg restore the bundle from a cache keyed on `bundles.toml`.
work_packages.interfaces: `bundles.toml` schema; `FFMPEG_DIR` contract consumed by 1D.01 and the S3 spike.
acceptance: The workflow produces bundles for 3 OSes; `ffmpeg -version` from each prints the pinned 8.1.x and `--enable-gpl`; after `just ffmpeg-fetch` on a clean machine of each OS a 10-line Rust build script links `avformat` successfully.

**Configure/encoder check (script, all 3 OS):** `configure.txt` contains every required `--enable-lib*` flag above, and `ffmpeg -hide_banner -encoders` lists `libx264 libx265 libsvtav1 libvpx-vp9 libopus libmp3lame prores_ks dnxhd gif`; `-filters` lists `vidstabdetect vidstabtransform zscale`; `-buildconf` shows `--enable-libsoxr --enable-libass`; hwaccel flags per OS are present (`-hwaccels`).
Release assets include the source tarball and `configure.txt` (script check).
`just setup && just check` is green on the 3 OSes using the fetched bundle.
Linux bundle `ldd`/`objdump` shows glibc requirement <= 2.35.
work_packages.out_of_scope: release signing, the P7 FFmpeg source-offer page, Flatpak ffmpeg-full.

work_packages.title: S1 build: Electron shell + Rust sidecar + SHM ring + napi reader
work_packages.scope:
- Rust sidecar generating synthetic 1080p60 frames (moving pattern with frame counter + embedded pts, NV12 and RGBA8 variants) via wgpu readback (software fine) into a **named shared-memory ring** per arch §10: 4–6 slots, header = atomic write index, per-slot `pts,w,h,format,rev,seq`, audio-clock word written continuously (fake clock).
- napi-rs v3 addon `bridge` mapping the ring and exposing slots as `ArrayBuffer`s (zero-copy) + `readHeader()`.
- **Transport (a):** the addon is loaded in a **non-sandboxed preload of the main editor window only** (`sandbox:false` for that preload; `contextIsolation:true`, `nodeIntegration:false`; narrow `contextBridge` API; content served from a local `app://` protocol only; strict CSP; plugin iframes get no preload). Rationale: Electron sandboxed preloads cannot load native modules. All other windows stay `sandbox:true`.
- Electron main spawns the sidecar and passes the token/ring name via the preload bridge only (never URL/DOM).
- (Transport (b) is WP-0C.06.)
- WS channel for transport commands (play/pause/seek) from renderer to sidecar.
acceptance: Transport (a) works with `contextIsolation:true`, `nodeIntegration:false`: a test asserts `typeof require === 'undefined'` and `typeof process === 'undefined'` in the renderer main world while `window.bridge.getLatestFrame()` returns frames, and that a second (sandboxed) `BrowserWindow` has no `window.bridge`.
On the dev machine, 60 s run produces frames with monotonically increasing `seq` and zero torn frames (checksum embedded in frame verified in renderer).
Sidecar crash (kill -9) is detected by main in < 1 s; ring is cleaned up (no leaked shm object on Linux/macOS; handle closed on Windows).
work_packages.tests: Rust unit test for ring writer/reader wrap-around; Node test for addon reader.

work_packages.title: S1 build: WebGPU canvas, DOM overlay, scrub bar, live resize
work_packages.scope:
- React/Vite renderer: WebGPU canvas presenting the newest slot with `pts ≤ audio clock` in `requestAnimationFrame`, via **both** upload paths behind a toggle: `queue.writeTexture` and `VideoFrame`→`importExternalTexture`.
- DOM overlay above canvas: draggable/resizable transform box (pointer events), safe-area guides, scrub bar sending seek requests (latest-wins).
- Live window resize: preview canvas pixel size changes are sent to the sidecar which re-renders at the new size (arch §10 step 1).
- Instrumentation: per-frame present timestamps, dropped-frame counter, scrub-to-pixel latency (seek sent → first frame with matching pts presented, using a pts-stamped glyph), CPU% of sidecar + main + renderer processes sampled every 1 s to a JSON log.
- Chromium flags required for WebGPU on Linux (Vulkan, Wayland ozone) documented in `spikes/s1-preview/FLAGS.md`.
work_packages.interfaces: metrics JSON schema `{ts, fps, dropped, scrub_ms[], cpu{engine,main,renderer}}`.
acceptance: Overlay box stays pixel-aligned over the canvas during resize and while playing (visual check + automated DOM-rect vs canvas-rect assertion every second).
Both upload paths run for 60 s on the dev machine and emit metrics JSON.
work_packages.tests: Playwright-Electron smoke launching the spike and asserting metrics file exists.

work_packages.title: S1 measure on all platforms + report
work_packages.executor_note: (operates hardware; agent assists with analysis script)
work_packages.depends_raw: WP-0C.02, WP-0C.03, WP-0C.06, WP-0I.04 (or developer machines meeting the 0I.02 definition)

- Evaluate each criterion: 60 fps sustained; dropped frames/min (< 2); scrub-to-pixel p95 (< 80 ms); transport CPU (< 15% of one core-equivalent, define in report); timeline ≥ 55 fps; overlay/z-order issues (none). Compare `writeTexture` vs `importExternalTexture`, **and transport (a) non-sandboxed-preload addon vs transport (b) utilityProcess + MessagePort** (frame-delivery latency, copy cost, CPU, jitter; security posture noted).
- Write `docs/spikes/S1-report.md`: raw tables per OS, verdict PASS/FAIL per criterion, recommended upload path, **recommended transport (a) or (b)**, required Chromium flags, known OS quirks, recommendation for ADR-001.
work_packages.interfaces: report is the evidence for ADR-001 (0J.02), which **records the transport choice** (a vs b), and `RING.md` for 1H.02/1H.03.
acceptance: Report contains a verdict line `S1: PASS | PASS-WITH-FALLBACK | FAIL` and a numeric cell for every criterion × every OS (16 cells + timeline).
If any criterion fails on any OS, a ticket/WP-0C.05 is activated (below) and the report says so explicitly.

work_packages.title: S1 build: transport (b) utilityProcess/main + MessagePort
work_packages.scope:
- Implement the alternative to transport (a): the napi addon runs in an Electron `utilityProcess` (or the main process); frames reach the sandboxed renderer through a transferred `MessagePort` (transferable `ArrayBuffer`s from a pre-allocated pool, or `SharedArrayBuffer` if cross-origin isolation can be enabled for the `app://` origin — measure both). All windows are `sandbox:true` with a **no-native-module** preload exposing only the port handoff.
- Same metrics output and same renderer present loop as 0C.02 so results are comparable; add an A/B switch `?transport=a|b`.
- Record copy count per frame, per-frame delivery latency (ring write → renderer receipt), and CPU of the utility process.
acceptance: Transport (b) runs 60 s at 1080p60 on the dev machine producing metrics JSON; a test proves the renderer is sandboxed (`process.sandboxed === true`) and has no native-module access.
A/B comparison table (a vs b) is generated by `cargo xtask bench-report`.

work_packages.title: S2 build: cpal mixer, stretch, loudness, clock-following video
work_packages.scope:
- cpal 0.18 output stream (256-sample buffer requested; record actual), 8 simultaneous decoded tracks (pre-decoded WAV/FLAC fixtures from 0I.01 or synthesized), per-track gain/pan, `rubato` resample 44.1k/96k → device rate, `signalsmith-stretch` at 0.5×, 1.0×, 2.0×, `ebur128` momentary/integrated loudness on master.
- Real-thread discipline: lock-free SPSC ring buffers from worker threads, no allocation/locks in the callback (verified with `assert_no_alloc` in debug).
- Master clock = samples played (+ device latency reported by cpal); minimal video window (winit or the S1 renderer) generating frames whose presentation follows the clock; test signal mode: video flashes white on frame N while audio plays a click at the same timeline time.
- Logging: callback underrun count, clock drift vs `Instant`, reported latency.
acceptance: 10-min run at 256-sample buffer on the dev machine: 0 underruns with 8 tracks + stretch 0.5×–2×.
`ebur128` integrated loudness of a −23 LUFS reference tone within ±0.1 LU.
Flash/click harness emits a capture file (for 0D.02).
work_packages.tests: unit tests for ring buffer; stretch ratio sanity (output length within 0.5% of expected).

work_packages.title: S2 measure (30-min drift, A/V offset) + report
work_packages.executor_note: (hardware; loopback/camera measurement) with sonnet-written analysis script
work_packages.depends_raw: WP-0D.01, WP-0I.04 (or developer machines meeting the 0I.02 definition)
work_packages.scope:
- Run 30-min soak on each reference machine/OS (Win11 WASAPI, macOS CoreAudio, Linux PulseAudio/PipeWire): drift = (audio clock − wall clock) at end; underruns; reported latency.
- A/V offset: measure flash→click offset with a phone high-speed camera + audio, or loopback (photodiode/mic) — procedure written in the report; accept ±1 frame@60 measurement error.
- If any criterion fails: retry with 512/1024 buffers + latency compensation (apply `cpal` reported latency) and with Rubber Band (GPL, via FFI) for stretch quality/CPU comparison; document.
- Report: verdict per OS, recommended default buffer size, latency-compensation rule, stretch library choice (signalsmith vs Rubber Band: CPU %, subjective artifacts at 0.5×/2×).
work_packages.interfaces: evidence for `cutweave-audio` design (1G.01/1G.02); no dedicated ADR (arch §23 has none for audio), verdict is recorded in the 0J.03 go/no-go review.
acceptance: report has numeric drift (frames/30 min), underrun count, A/V offset ms on each OS; verdict `PASS` or `PASS-WITH-FALLBACK (<setting>)`; fallback settings are reproducible via a documented flag.

work_packages.title: S3 build: ffmpeg-next decode, keyframe index, frame-exact seek
work_packages.scope:
- Use the pinned bundle from WP-0A.06 (`just ffmpeg-fetch`) when available, otherwise brew/distro libs for quick hacking (06-dev-process §2); document how `ffmpeg-sys-next` links them; record the working recipe per OS in `spikes/s3-decode/SETUP.md` (feeds 1D.01). Verify ffmpeg-next version/FFmpeg ABI compatibility; if broken try `ffmpeg-the-third` and report.
- Decode corpus items from 0I.01: H.264 4K30 long-GOP, HEVC 10-bit, ProRes, VFR phone clip (rotated).
- Build frame index (pts → keyframe/GOP map) by packet scan; frame-exact seek = keyframe seek + decode-forward to exact pts using the index; VFR handled through index (never constant fps).
- Ground truth via `ffprobe -show_frames` pts list; harness does 500 random seeks per file and compares returned frame pts and a CRC of the Y plane against `ffmpeg -vf select` reference output.
- Intra-codec proxy (ProRes Proxy / MJPEG) generated by script for the scrub comparison.
acceptance: Harness prints `frame-exact: 500/500` for every corpus file (CPU decode) on the dev machine.
Scrub benchmark prints p50/p95 for 4K long-GOP and proxy.
work_packages.tests: the harness itself (cargo test with `--ignored` flag for corpus-dependent tests).

work_packages.title: S3 build: HW decode (CPU upload) and zero-copy interop
work_packages.scope:
- (a) HW decode via FFmpeg hwaccel (D3D11VA on Windows, VideoToolbox on macOS, VA-API on Linux; NVDEC where present), `av_hwframe_transfer_data` to NV12/P010 in CPU memory, upload as wgpu textures and convert in a shader (reuse S4 shader if available, otherwise a minimal one). Fallback to SW decode when hwaccel init fails; frame-exactness re-verified on HW path (HW decoders can differ at bit level: compare pts, and PSNR > 50 dB vs SW frame).
- (b) zero-copy experiment behind a cargo feature: DX12 shared handle (Windows), IOSurface→Metal (macOS), dmabuf→Vulkan (Linux). Time-boxed to 4 agent-days; record "works / works-with-caveats / not viable" per OS with evidence.
- Metrics: per-frame decode→texture-ready latency, CPU%, GPU%.
acceptance: Path (a) decodes + uploads + renders H.264 4K30 and HEVC 10-bit on every OS available to the dev machine; failures produce clean SW fallback (test with hwaccel forced off).
Table of (b) status per OS is present with at least one measured number or a concrete blocker per OS.
work_packages.tests: harness extended; PSNR comparison HW vs SW.

work_packages.title: S3 measure on all platforms + report
work_packages.depends_raw: WP-0E.02, WP-0I.04 (or developer machines meeting the 0I.02 definition)
work_packages.scope:
- Run the harness on Win11, macOS arm64, Ubuntu 24.04 (X11 + Wayland where VA-API differs) reference machines; include an NVIDIA-equipped Windows machine if available.
- Verdict per criterion: 500/500 frame-exact (all files, all OS, SW and HW), 4K long-GOP scrub p95 < 150 ms, proxy p95 < 33 ms, path (a) works everywhere; zero-copy status per OS.
- Recommend ADR-003 text: FFmpeg via `ffmpeg-next` behind `MediaBackend`, CPU upload first; zero-copy deferred or scheduled, with FFmpeg acquisition recipe and ffmpeg-next vs ffmpeg-the-third verdict.
acceptance: numeric cells for each criterion × OS; verdict `PASS | PASS-WITH-FALLBACK (a-only)`; FFmpeg dev setup recipe linked for each OS.

work_packages.title: S4 build: render graph, linear compositor, LUT, tone-map, headless export
work_packages.scope:
- wgpu (pin 30.0.x) render graph (DAG of passes, simple cache keys) compositing **3 layers**, **2 blend modes** (normal, multiply), a **dissolve** transition, a `.cube` 3D **LUT** pass, in **linear light `Rgba16Float`**; YUV→RGB with matrix/range/transfer from tags; **PQ→SDR tone-map** (BT.2390-style) for HDR10 input frames.
- Headless mode (`--headless`) on software adapters (WARP, lavapipe) and real GPUs; reads back to PNG/EXR for comparison.
- Reference generation: independent CPU float implementation (Python/numpy script or Rust) of the same scene → reference images; PSNR and ΔE2000 comparison tool.
- GPU timing via timestamp queries; scene for timing = 1080p60, 3 layers + 2 effects (blur-lite + LUT) on iGPU.
- Headless export: render 300 frames, pipe raw frames to `ffmpeg` CLI to an MP4 (smoke only).
acceptance: Headless run produces reference-comparison output printing PSNR and ΔE for each test scene.
Timing table printed for each available adapter.
MP4 produced plays (ffprobe ok, 300 frames).
work_packages.tests: comparison tool unit tests (identical images → ∞ dB, ΔE = 0).

work_packages.title: S4 build: text — animated caption via MSDF atlas and Vello
work_packages.scope:
- `cosmic-text` shaping (Latin + one RTL + one CJK sample + emoji) → glyph runs → **MSDF atlas** renderer (own, msdfgen-compatible generation using `fdsm`/`msdfgen` crate or offline atlas) with fill, outline, shadow, per-word **pop** scale animation and **karaoke** highlight sweep; and a second path rendering glyphs via **Vello 0.12**.
- Scenes: (1) animated caption on 1080p; (2) same at 4K with 200 px glyphs for crispness; (3) 1000 animated glyphs (per-glyph transform/color) cost.
- Measure CPU time for layout+instance buffer build per frame, and GPU time per frame, for MSDF vs Vello.
- Crispness metric: render at 4K, compare against a supersampled (8×8) CPU rasterization reference; report SSIM + visual diff images.
acceptance: prints for both paths: 1000-animated-glyph per-frame CPU instance-build time (target < 1 ms) and GPU time; crispness SSIM ≥ 0.98 on the 4K scene for the chosen path; diff images saved.
work_packages.tests: snapshot test (`insta` image hash with tolerance) for caption frame.

work_packages.title: S4 measure on all platforms + report (+ skia fallback if failing)
work_packages.executor_note: (hardware runs) with opus-assisted analysis; skia-safe evaluation only if a criterion fails
work_packages.depends_raw: WP-0F.02, WP-0I.04 (or developer machines meeting the 0I.02 definition)
work_packages.scope:
- Run 0F.01/0F.02 on all reference machines including the iGPU reference (M1 and Intel Xe). Evaluate: GPU time < 8 ms (1080p60 scene) on iGPU; PSNR > 45 dB vs reference; ΔE < 2; 4K text crispness; 1000 glyphs < 1 ms.
- Decide text path for ADR-007: MSDF only / MSDF + Vello for large-complex glyphs / Vello only. If MSDF AND Vello both fail the glyph criteria, build a minimal skia-safe variant (time-box 3 days) and compare.
- Record wgpu behaviour deltas between WARP/lavapipe/real GPUs relevant to golden-frame tolerances (feeds 1O.01).
acceptance: table with numeric result per criterion × adapter; verdict `PASS | PASS-WITH-FALLBACK (<which>)`; documented tolerance recommendation (PSNR/FLIP thresholds) for software-vs-hardware golden frames.

work_packages.title: S4b build: oxc → rquickjs → scene graph → S4 compositor
work_packages.scope:
- Transpile the TSX lower-third from arch §12 (using a minimal scratch `@cutweave/compose` shim: `defineComposition`, `interpolate`, `spring`, `Group/Rect/Text`) with **oxc** (TS + JSX → JS; custom JSX factory emitting plain node objects) in-process.
- Run in **rquickjs** with: no `fetch`/`fs`/`require`/`import()` of external modules, `Date.now`/`Math.random`/`performance.now` removed or replaced (seeded PRNG from item id), memory limit and interrupt-handler time limit.
- `render({frame,fps,props,size})` → serializable scene description (JSON or compact binary) → drawn by the S4 compositor (rects, rounded rects, text via MSDF path).
- Props schema → JSON Schema extraction (`z`-like shim) just enough to prove the inspector/MCP path.
- Test scene with 200 nodes; adversarial scripts (infinite loop, huge alloc, attempt to touch `process`, `require('fs')`, `fetch`, `eval`, `new Function`).
acceptance: All adversarial scripts are contained: loop is interrupted within the time limit (default 50 ms/frame), alloc bomb fails with a catchable error, forbidden globals are `undefined`/throw; engine process survives (test asserts).
The lower-third renders on the S4 compositor to a PNG at frames 0, 60, 119.
work_packages.tests: Rust tests for each adversarial script and for determinism (below).
work_packages.out_of_scope: the full scene API, npm module resolution, hot reload.

work_packages.title: S4b measure + report (fallback decision)
work_packages.depends_raw: WP-0G.01, WP-0I.04 (or developer machines meeting the 0I.02 definition)
work_packages.scope:
- Measure on every reference machine: transpile time (cold + warm, median of 100) < 50 ms; scene eval time per frame for the 200-node scene (median/p99 of 10,000 frames) < 1 ms; determinism: render frames 0..239 three times in three separate processes → byte-identical scene JSON (hash compare); sandbox suite passes.
- Compare rquickjs vs Boa quickly on eval time (informational) and note oxc crate version/API stability.
- If failing: sketch the declarative JSON scene + expression fallback (expression grammar, node set) in the report, with an estimate of the lost capability.
acceptance: numeric cells for 3 thresholds × OS, determinism hash equality shown, verdict `PASS | PASS-WITH-FALLBACK (declarative)`.

work_packages.title: S5 build: `#[command]` macro, registry, schema + TS codegen
work_packages.scope:
- Proc-macro `#[command(name, summary, undoable, mcp="core|catalog|hidden", annotations(...))]` over a struct, per arch §5.1; generates `inventory`-style registration (linkme/inventory crate), a `CommandMeta` (name, summary, flags, input `schemars` schema, output schema), and a type-erased `invoke(json) -> Result<json, CmdError>`.
- 5 toy commands over a toy doc (`project.open`, `media.import`, `timeline.insert`, `clip.split`, `clip.trim`) + query `timeline.get` + query `render.frame` (returns PNG bytes); typed errors `NotFound/Invalid{path,msg}/Conflict`.
- Codegen binary emits `schema/commands.json` and TS types + typed client via **specta** (`specta-typescript`); implements the **decided** `Time` wire format (arch §4.1, ADR-015): JSON integer flicks, TS `number`, safe-integer validation at the boundary, timecode-string inputs accepted, specta type override so `i64` exports as `number`.
- `insta` snapshot tests of the JSON Schema and TS output.
acceptance: `cargo test` snapshot tests pass; changing a command field changes the snapshot and fails the test until reviewed.
Generated TS compiles under `tsc --strict` and a sample script calls `client.call("clip.split", {...})` with compile-time checked args (negative test with a wrong field fails `tsc`).
`Time` fields export as TS `number` (no `bigint`), a value above 2^53-1 is rejected with `Invalid` (test), and a timecode string input parses (test), per ADR-015.
work_packages.tests: snapshot + trybuild compile-fail test for a malformed `#[command]`.

work_packages.title: S5 build: rmcp server (stdio + HTTP) over the registry
work_packages.scope:
- Verify the current rmcp version; pin exact version. **Test BOTH MCP revisions, 2025-11-25 and 2026-07-28, via rmcp** (client and server negotiation, session handling, tool listing/calling, image content, structured output) and record in `docs/spikes/S5-report.md` which revision(s) rmcp supports, how negotiation resolves, and any gaps.
- Change notifications: implement whichever the negotiated revision supports (`resources/subscribe` + `notifications/resources/updated` on the older revision; `subscriptions/listen` on the newer) behind one internal `Notifier` abstraction. **Do not depend on `ping`** for liveness on the new revision.
- Tool profiles are selected **per endpoint** (`/mcp`, `/mcp/minimal`, `/mcp/full`) or by a `--profile` flag on stdio servers, never per connection; prototype `/mcp` and `/mcp/minimal`.
- rmcp server exposing the 5 commands as tools (annotations `readOnlyHint/destructiveHint/idempotentHint` from macro metadata) + generic `cutweave_search_commands`, `cutweave_describe_command`, `cutweave_execute(steps, dry_run?, expected_rev?)` and `render_frame` returning **image content** (JPEG ≤ 768 px, base64) + structured metadata.
- Transports: stdio and Streamable HTTP on `127.0.0.1` random port with bearer token + Host/Origin checks.
- Tool-list budget measurement (tool count and estimated tokens of `tools/list`) against the single-source budgets: **minimal <= 12 tools / <= 3k tokens; standard <= 36 tools / <= 8k tokens; full = standard + search-based long tail; P1 gate <= 19 tools / <= 5k tokens**.
acceptance: `npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector` connects over stdio and HTTP and lists tools, calls each, receives an image content block for `render_frame` (screenshots or CLI-mode transcript saved).
HTTP without token → 401; wrong Host header → 403.
The same test suite passes against both MCP revisions (or the report documents which fails and the fallback: pin to the older revision, adapter shim for the newer).
A change notification reaches a subscribed client under each revision's mechanism.
`tools/list` size recorded (target informational: < 6k tokens for 8 tools).
work_packages.tests: Rust integration test using rmcp client against the server (both transports).

work_packages.title: Corpus manifest + fetch script + license audit
work_packages.scope:
- `testdata/corpus.toml` manifest: for each item `id, description, sha256, size, license (CC0/CC-BY/self-generated), source_url or generator, tags`. Required items: H.264 4K30 long-GOP, H.264 1080p60, HEVC 10-bit SDR, HEVC 10-bit HDR10 (PQ), ProRes 422 HQ 1080p, **VFR phone clip** (rotated 90°), odd sample-rate audio (22.05k, 44.1k, 48k, 96k), 5.1 audio, image (PNG/JPEG), a truncated/broken MP4, a zero-audio-stream video, a variable-frame-size case. Generated items use `ffmpeg lavfi` recipes committed in `testdata/generate/*.sh` (so licensing is trivially clean); real-world items only CC0/CC-BY.
- `cargo xtask fetch-corpus [--tier small|full]` downloads to `testdata/.cache/` (gitignored) verifying sha256, resumable, offline-friendly (skips if present); `--tier small` < 50 MB for PR CI, `full` for nightly. Includes `xtask corpus-verify`.
- CI step caches `testdata/.cache` keyed on manifest hash.
- `testdata/README.md` with attribution table (CC-BY credits).
work_packages.interfaces: corpus ids referenced by tests (`corpus::path("h264_4k30_longgop")` helper in a tiny `cutweave-testutil` module under `xtask`, to be moved into a dev-crate in 1A).
acceptance: `cargo xtask fetch-corpus --tier small && cargo xtask corpus-verify` exits 0 on 3 OSes; corrupting a cached file makes verify fail.
Every manifest item has a license field; `xtask` rejects a manifest entry without one.
Generated items reproduce byte-identical sha256 across runs on the same ffmpeg version (record ffmpeg version in manifest) — or declare tolerance (`probe_hash` of stream properties) if not.
work_packages.tests: manifest parser unit tests; checksum mismatch test.
work_packages.out_of_scope: hosting the large files (document the chosen host in README: GitHub Releases assets of a `cutweave-testdata` repo).

work_packages.title: IDs, flicks time, frame-rate math
work_packages.scope:
- `Time(i64)` newtype in flicks (705,600,000/s) with checked arithmetic (`Add/Sub`, saturating variants explicit), `Duration`, `FrameRate{num,den}` (rational), `SampleRate`.
- Allowed conversions only: `frame_to_time`, `time_to_frame(Rounding::{Floor,Nearest})`, `snap_to_frame`, `samples_to_time`/`time_to_samples`.
- Parser/formatter for `"00:01:02:03"` (timecode at a given fps, drop-frame for 29.97/59.94), `"62.5s"`, and raw flicks integer; `Display` round-trips.
- Typed IDs: `MediaId/SequenceId/TrackId/ItemId` as UUIDv7 strings with prefix `med_/seq_/trk_/itm_`; `new()` (time-ordered), `FromStr` rejects wrong prefix; `IdGen` trait with `Uuid7Gen` (default) and `SeededGen(seed)` (deterministic, used by `--deterministic-ids`, see WP-1B.08).
- `serde` + `schemars` + `specta` derives; **wire format per arch §4.1 / ADR-015**: `Time` serializes as a JSON integer of flicks, exports to TS as `number` via specta type override, deserialization rejects non-safe integers (|v| > 2^53-1) and accepts timecode strings (`"00:01:02:03"`, `"62.5s"`) at API inputs; crate is `no_std`-friendly-ish: must pass `cargo xtask check-wasm`.
work_packages.interfaces: `cutweave_model::{Time, Duration, FrameRate, SampleRate, MediaId, SequenceId, TrackId, ItemId, IdGen}`.
acceptance: Exhaustive test over frame rates {23.976, 24, 25, 29.97, 30, 50, 59.94, 60, 120} and sample rates {44.1k, 48k, 96k}: `frame_to_time` / `time_to_frame` round-trip exactly for frames 0..1,000,000 and 1 flick = exact integer ratios (no float).
Overflow cases return `Err`, never wrap (test with `i64::MAX`).
`cargo nextest run -p cutweave-model` and `cargo xtask check-wasm` pass.

work_packages.title: Core traits, registry, `Tx` and patch ops
work_packages.scope:
- Traits per arch §5.1: `Command { type Output; fn apply(&self, &mut Tx) -> Result<Output, CmdError> }`, `Query { type Output; fn run(&self, &QueryCtx) -> Result<Output, CmdError> }`, `CommandMeta{name, summary, undoable, scope: Scope(Any|UiOnly), mcp: McpExposure(Core|Catalog|Hidden), annotations{destructive,idempotent,read_only}, input_schema, output_schema}`.
- `Registry` (static registration via `inventory`/`linkme` as chosen in S5) with `register`, `get(name)`, `list()`, `invoke_json(name, Value, &mut Tx)`.
- `CmdError` enum `{NotFound{kind,id}, Locked{item}, Conflict{current_rev}, Invalid{path,msg}, Unsupported, Internal}` each with machine `code()` and human `message()`, serializable.
- `Tx`: mutation API on the doc (`insert_item`, `remove_item`, `set_field(path, value)`, `insert_media`, …) that records **forward and inverse `PatchOp`s**, JSON-Pointer-addressed on the ID-based document (`/media/{id}`, `/sequences/{sid}/tracks/{tid}/items/{iid}/…`), ops: `Add{path,value}`, `Remove{path,old}`, `Replace{path,old,new}`, `Move`. `apply_patch(doc, ops)` pure function; `invert(ops)`.
- Semantic validation hook before apply (IDs exist, locks, ranges) returning `CmdError::Invalid`.
work_packages.interfaces: `cutweave_commands::{Command, Query, Registry, CommandMeta, CmdError, Tx, PatchOp, Patch}`; wasm-safe.
acceptance: For a hand-written test command, `apply_patch(apply_patch(doc, forward), invert(forward)) == doc`.
Registry rejects duplicate names at startup (test) and names not matching `^[a-z]+\.[a-z_]+$` (arch §5.1 naming).

work_packages.title: Single-writer document actor, snapshots, revisions, events
work_packages.scope:
- `DocActor` running on a dedicated thread (not tokio) with an mpsc command inbox; handle `DocHandle{ submit(cmd, actor, expected_rev) -> Future<Result<Applied>>, snapshot() -> Arc<DocSnapshot>, committed_snapshot() -> Arc<DocSnapshot>, subscribe() -> EventStream }`; `submit` also carries the originating `ConnId` (used by 1B.09 transaction ownership).
- `Arc` swap (e.g. `arc-swap`) of immutable `DocSnapshot{rev: u64, committed_rev: u64, doc: Project}` per revision; readers never lock. **`committed_snapshot()` is the last COMMITTED rev only** (excludes the live effects of an open gesture/proposal tx); saves, autosave and journaling use it exclusively.
- `expected_rev` check → `CmdError::Conflict{current_rev}`. `rev` increments per committed tx (not per command inside a tx).
- Events: `DocPatched{rev, actor, tx_id, ops}` broadcast to subscribers (bounded channel; slow subscriber gets `Lagged` and must resync via snapshot). `Actor` enum `{User, Agent(label), Plugin(id), System}`; **the actor is derived by the engine from the authenticated credential** (UI credential → `User`, agent token → `Agent(<token label>)`, plugin → `Plugin(<id>)`, internal jobs → `System`); `submit` takes a `Credential`/`ActorCtx`, never a client-asserted actor.
- **Idempotency (arch §5.1):** every submit carries a client-generated `request_id` (UUIDv7; the engine generates one for clients that omit it, e.g. CLI/MCP). The engine keeps a dedup table `request_id -> Applied` for a **10-minute window** (**wall-clock timestamps** via an injectable `Clock`, persisted per transaction in the journal so the window survives engine restarts); a repeat within the window returns the original result without re-applying and without bumping `rev`. The table is persisted via the journal (1C.02) so it survives restart.
- Panic in a command → tx rolled back, error returned, actor keeps running (catch_unwind), event `CmdPanicked` logged.
acceptance: Stress test: 8 threads submit 10,000 commands total; final doc equals sequential replay of the recorded order; no deadlock (test timeout 30 s); `loom` or `shuttle` model test on the submit/snapshot-swap path passes.
A reader holding an old snapshot sees no mutation after later commits.
While a gesture tx is open with uncommitted changes, `committed_snapshot()` still equals the pre-tx doc and `rev`/`committed_rev` diverge as specified (test).
Stale `expected_rev` returns `Conflict` with the correct current rev.
Submitting the same `request_id` twice (second after 9 min of fake time) applies once and returns identical output; after 11 min it is treated as new (test).
Round-trip latency for a no-op command on the actor p95 < 1 ms (criterion bench recorded; feeds arch §19 command RTT budget).

work_packages.title: Transactions, undo/redo, per-actor history
work_packages.scope:
- Transaction API: `edit.begin_tx{label}`, `edit.commit_tx`, `edit.cancel_tx` (rollback by applying inverse ops), implicit single-command tx otherwise; **tx kinds** (`edit.begin_tx{kind:"gesture"|"proposal", label}`): a `gesture` tx live-updates the doc (events emitted per update), collapses into one undo entry on commit, rolls back on cancel, and **auto-cancels after 30 s without activity**; a `proposal` tx (used by the copilot in P6) has no idle timeout, can be cancelled, and likewise commits as one undo entry. Ownership and soft-locks: WP-1B.09.
- Per-actor history stacks (`undo`/`redo`), commands `edit.undo{actor?}`, `edit.redo{actor?}`, query `edit.history{limit,cursor}`; undo of actor A's last tx applied only if it still applies cleanly: if later edits by another actor conflict, return `CmdError::Conflict` (documented rule), never corrupt the doc.
- New redo branch cleared on new edit by that actor.
- Undo/redo themselves produce `DocPatched` events with `actor` and `cause: Undo|Redo`.
- Checkpoints are **not** in P1 (see integrator note).
acceptance: Scenario tests: apply 50 random commands → undo all → doc equals initial; redo all → doc equals final (`Project` equality).

Gesture tx with 200 updates yields exactly 1 history entry; cancel restores pre-tx doc; `DocPatched` events were emitted for live updates; a gesture tx idle for 30 s (fake clock) is auto-cancelled and the doc restored.
Two actors interleave edits; each `edit.undo{actor}` reverts only its own last tx or returns `Conflict` (3 explicit scenarios).
work_packages.tests: unit + scenario; property tests live in 1B.07.
work_packages.out_of_scope: checkpoints, history persistence across restarts (journal replay reconstructs it in 1C.02).

work_packages.title: Transaction ownership, connection-drop rollback, minimal soft-lock
work_packages.scope:
- **A tx is owned by the connection (`ConnId`) that opened it.** Only the owner may add commands to, commit or cancel it (others get `CmdError::Locked{by}`); when the owning connection drops (WS close, MCP session end, stdio proxy exit) the engine **rolls the tx back** immediately (inverse ops, `DocPatched` event with `cause: Rollback`). Per-connection limit: one open tx.
- **Minimal soft-lock:** while a tx is open, items it has touched are soft-locked for other actors/connections: their commands on those items fail `Locked{item, by_actor, tx_id}` (non-blocking, no waiting); locks release on commit/cancel/rollback. Commands on untouched items proceed. Needed because UI gestures and an attached MCP agent coexist in P1.
- Tx kind behaviours from 1B.04 (gesture idle timeout 30 s using the injectable `Clock`; proposal: no timeout, explicit cancel) enforced here; `edit.cancel_tx` by owner only.
- Saves/autosave use `committed_snapshot()` (1B.03): an open tx never leaks into a save, and a crash with an open tx loses only the uncommitted tx (it is never journaled until commit).
- Events: `tx.opened{tx_id, kind, actor, items}`, `tx.closed{tx_id, outcome}` for UI "agent is editing" indicators.
acceptance: Test: connection A opens a gesture tx moving item X; connection B's `clip.trim` on X returns `Locked`, on Y succeeds; after A drops, X is restored to its pre-tx state and B's retry succeeds.
Save during an open gesture tx writes a document equal to the pre-tx committed doc (byte-compare) and journals nothing for the tx.
100 random open/commit/cancel/drop interleavings (proptest with 3 connections) never leave a dangling lock or a doc differing from a replay of committed txs.
work_packages.tests: unit + proptest + loom/shuttle for the ownership map.
work_packages.out_of_scope: CRDT merging, lock UI beyond the events, hard/blocking locks.

work_packages.title: Property-test harness: undo/redo identity, round-trip, invariants
work_packages.scope:
- Registry-driven generator: `arb_command_for(&Project) -> impl Strategy<(name, Value)>` producing valid-ish args (IDs drawn from the doc, times on frame grid) for **every registered non-view command** plus deliberately invalid args; adding a command without a strategy fails a test (`missing property strategy for <name>`).
- Properties (arch §20): (1) `undo(apply(doc)) == doc` for each successful command; (2) `redo(undo(apply)) == apply`; (3) failed commands leave doc and rev unchanged; (4) `serialize → deserialize` round-trip equality after random sequences of ≤ 100 commands; (5) invariants after every step: `Project::validate()` passes, no overlaps on tracks, linked groups intact; (6) patch events replayed on an empty-mirror reproduce the doc (the UI docStore contract).
- `PROPTEST_CASES` default 256 in CI, 4096 nightly; failing seeds persisted to `proptest-regressions/` (committed).
acceptance: `cargo nextest run -p cutweave-ops --features testing` passes with 256 cases; property (1) has been shown to catch a seeded bug (a mutation test in the PR: break the inverse of `clip.trim`, test fails, revert).
Strategy coverage report lists ≥ 95% of registered command names as exercised.

work_packages.title: Deterministic-ID test mode (`--deterministic-ids <seed>`)
work_packages.scope:
- `SeededGen(seed: u64)` `IdGen`: valid prefixed UUIDv7-shaped IDs from a counter-based PRNG (ChaCha8 from seed, fixed timestamp bits), one stream per engine. All ID creation in `cutweave-ops`/`Tx` goes through the injected `IdGen` (a grep-based test forbids direct `Uuid::now_v7()` outside `Uuid7Gen`).
- Engine/CLI flag `--deterministic-ids <seed>` (+ env `CUTWEAVE_DETERMINISTIC_IDS`) plumbed into `EngineConfig`; it also freezes `meta.created` and other timestamps written into project documents and the auto-generated `request_id`s, so two identical command scripts yield **byte-identical saved project documents** (arch §5.1).
- In `Gui` mode the flag is refused unless `--i-know-this-is-a-test` is passed.
- The journal records resulting IDs (1C.02), so replay is exact with or without the flag.
acceptance: The same script run in two fresh engines with seed 42 gives identical `.cutweave` bytes (sha256 equal); seed 43 gives different IDs but identical structure after ID normalization.
The grep test passes; `cargo nextest run -p cutweave-ops -p cutweave-commands`.

work_packages.title: Project folder format, atomic save/open, lock file
work_packages.scope:
- Folder layout per arch §17: `<Name>/<Name>.cutweave`, `generated/`, `compositions/`, `.cutweave/{journal,backups,lock}`.
- `save(path, &Project)` (called with `committed_snapshot()` only; an open tx's uncommitted effects are never persisted): write temp file in same dir → `fsync` file → atomic rename → `fsync` dir (Windows: `ReplaceFileW`/`MoveFileEx` with write-through); never leaves a partial `.cutweave` (test by failpoint injection at each step).
- `open(path)`: lock acquisition, `migrate_to_current`, `ReadOnly` handling, relative-path resolution of media (`path_rel` fallback when `path_abs` missing; report missing media in `OpenReport{missing_media[]}`; relink UI is P2).
- **Lock file** `.cutweave/lock` containing `{pid, host, started}`; stale-lock detection (pid dead on same host ⇒ steal with log; live pid ⇒ `CmdError::Locked`), released on clean close and via `Drop`; second open of the same project in another process fails with a clear error.
- Commands in `cutweave-ops` (thin): `project.open{path}`, `project.save{}`, `project.save_as{path}`, `project.close{}`; registered as non-undoable.
acceptance: Failpoint test: killing the process (simulated by aborting after each of 4 steps) leaves the previous `.cutweave` intact and loadable (4 cases).
Two processes: second `project.open` gets `Locked`; after `kill -9` of the first, the stale lock is reclaimed.
Round-trip: save → open equals original `Project`, on Windows paths with spaces and unicode.
work_packages.tests: unit + multi-process integration test (spawn helper bin).

work_packages.title: Command journal + replay + crash-recovery test
work_packages.scope:
- Append-only journal `.cutweave/journal/<base-rev>.jnl`: one record per **committed tx**: `{rev, tx_id, wall_clock_ts, actor, request_id (UUIDv7), label, commands:[{name,args}], result_ids, applied_output, crc32}` length-prefixed (`u32 len + payload + crc`); written by the doc actor **before** the tx is acked; write policy: `write()` to OS before ack, `fdatasync` group-commit every ≤ 50 ms and always on `project.save` (documented durability: survives process kill; ≤ 50 ms window on power loss).
- Gesture tx: only the final collapsed command list is journaled on commit; cancelled ones not.
- `view.*` commands are not journaled.
- On save: journal rotates (new base rev), old journal kept until the next successful save, then deleted.
- Recovery: `ProjectStore::open` detects non-empty journal newer than the `.cutweave` ⇒ returns `RecoveryAvailable{records, last_rev, last_ts}`; `recover()` replays commands (deterministic `IdGen` seeded from recorded IDs — the journal stores the **resulting IDs** in each record so replay is exact, see integrator note) through the real registry; torn/CRC-bad tail record is truncated with a warning; history stacks rebuilt so undo works after recovery.
- **Dedup after restart (arch §5.1):** recovery rebuilds the 10-minute `request_id -> Applied` table from the journal using each record's **persisted wall-clock timestamp** (a record is within the window if `now - ts <= 10 min`, so the window survives restart), so a client resending an unacknowledged request after an engine restart gets the original result and never a duplicate.
acceptance: **Crash-recovery test** (`cargo nextest run -p cutweave-engine --test crash_recovery`): helper process applies N=500 random ops via the registry, is `SIGKILL`ed/`TerminateProcess`ed at 20 random points; recovery reproduces a doc equal to "last acked rev" with **0 acked commands lost** across 20 trials, and ≤ 1 un-acked tx lost.
Truncating the journal mid-record at every byte offset of its final record (test loop) never causes a panic and recovers up to the previous record.
Undo after recovery reverts the last recovered tx.

**Resend test (exit 3):** in the 20 kill trials the helper also holds 5 in-flight (unacked) requests; after recovery they are re-submitted with the same `request_id`s and each is applied **exactly once** overall (acked-before-kill ones return the original result, unapplied ones apply once); final doc equals an uninterrupted run.
work_packages.tests: multi-process crash test, truncation fuzz loop, proptest(replay(journal) == live doc).

work_packages.title: Autosave, rotating backups, recovery API
work_packages.scope:
- Autosave timer: when doc dirty, save on idle (no commands for 2 s) and at least every 30 s (arch §17) via the atomic path; configurable in `settings.autosave{enabled, interval_s}`; runs on a background task, never blocks the actor (saves the **committed** snapshot only).
- `.cutweave/backups/`: keep last N=10 timestamped copies (rotate on autosave only when content hash changed).
- Events: `project.dirty{bool}`, `project.saved{rev,path}`, `project.recovery_available{…}` for UI.
- Dirty flag semantics defined: `last_saved_rev != committed_rev`.
work_packages.interfaces: `AutosaveService`, events above (registered in the event catalog for 1N).
acceptance: With a fake clock (tokio `pause`), autosave fires at 30 s of continuous edits and at 2 s idle; after 12 changed autosaves exactly 10 backups remain.
Autosave during a 500-command burst does not delay command acks by > 5 ms p95 (bench).

work_packages.title: `view` namespace commands and `ui-state.json` persistence
work_packages.scope:
- `view.set{patch}` (merge into `UiState{playhead, zoom, scroll, selection[], panel_layout (opaque JSON), preview_quality, master_gain}`) and query `view.get`; the transport commands of 1H.01 and `view.set_master_gain` (1G.02) belong to the same namespace. Not undoable, **not journaled**, no `rev` bump, no `doc.patched`; emits `view.changed` to other clients.
- Persistence in `<project>/.cutweave/ui-state.json` (atomic write, debounced 500 ms, also on close and with each save); loaded on `project.open` and returned by `view.get`; unknown keys preserved; a corrupt file is ignored with a warning and never blocks opening.
acceptance: After `view.set{playhead, selection}`, closing and reopening the project restores both (test); `edit.history` and the journal file size are unchanged by `view.*` calls (test).

work_packages.title: `MediaBackend` trait + FFmpeg build/link strategy
work_packages.scope:

work_packages.title: Probe, frame index, content hash
work_packages.scope:
- `probe`: streams, duration, fps/VFR detection (pts delta analysis), rotation (display matrix), color tags (primaries/transfer/matrix/range), audio rate/channels, codec profile; maps to `ProbeInfo` (1A.02). Errors on corrupt files are typed, never panic.
- **Frame index**: packet scan building `Vec<IndexEntry{pts, dts, is_key, pos}>` + GOP map; serialized into `cache.sqlite` (`rusqlite` bundled; schema versioned; table `frame_index(content_hash, stream, blob)`); VFR sources mapped through the index (arch §4.1).
- Content hash: BLAKE3 over first 1 MiB + last 1 MiB + size (documented fast-hash, used for relink in P2) with full-hash option; computed in the background.
- `CacheDb` struct in `cutweave-cache` (open, migrations, LRU size accounting stub).
acceptance: On the corpus: probe output matches `ffprobe -show_streams -of json` for duration (±1 frame), fps, rotation, color tags for every file (script-compared test); VFR clip flagged `vfr=true`; broken MP4 returns `MediaError::Corrupt` within 2 s.
Index for 4K30 long-GOP 60 s clip builds in < 3 s (recorded, not gating) and equals `ffprobe -show_packets` keyframe pts list (test).
work_packages.tests: corpus-driven integration tests (`--tier small`), unit tests with `FakeBackend`.

work_packages.title: Decoder: frame-exact seek, CPU path, decoder pool
work_packages.scope:

- CPU decode to `Nv12/P010/Yuv420p` planes (no conversion on CPU; GPU converts in 1F.02) with `ColorTags`; software scaler only for the fallback `Rgba8` path used by thumbnails.
- `DecoderPool` per media (bounded, LRU eviction, max 4 live decoders by default) with request cancellation tokens.
- `AudioDecoder::decode_range(start, dur) -> AudioChunk` resampled lazily by 1G.
acceptance: **500 random seeks per corpus video file (H.264 4K30, HEVC 10-bit, ProRes, VFR phone clip): 100% frame-exact** — returned pts equals the index pts for the requested time and Y-plane CRC equals ffmpeg reference — run as `cargo nextest run -p cutweave-media --test frame_exact -- --ignored` in nightly and `--tier small` subset (100 seeks) in PR CI.
4K long-GOP random seek p95 < 150 ms on a reference machine (bench recorded, non-gating on CI runners).
Cancelling a pending seek returns within 10 ms.

work_packages.title: Hardware decode (CPU-upload path) with fallback
work_packages.scope:

work_packages.title: Frame cache, thumbnails, filmstrips
work_packages.scope:
- In-RAM decoded **frame cache** (LRU by bytes; key `(content_hash, stream, pts)`; default budget 1 GiB or 25% RAM, configurable) used by scrub/preview.
- Thumbnail generator: `thumb(media, t, w) -> Jpeg/Webp bytes`; filmstrip: N tiles at even intervals → one sprite image + manifest `{tile_w, tile_h, count, interval}`; disk cache in the OS cache dir (`dirs`), content-hash addressed, size-capped LRU (default 2 GiB) tracked in `cache.sqlite`; ETag = content hash + params hash.
- Generated lazily and as a background job (1D.07) after import; cancellation supported.
acceptance: Second request for the same thumb performs 0 decodes (counter assertion); cache evicts oldest entries when over cap (unit test with 1 MB cap).
Filmstrip of a 60 s 1080p clip with 100 tiles generates in < 5 s on a dev machine (recorded).
Cache dir is outside the project folder; deleting it never breaks a project (test: delete, regenerate).

work_packages.title: Waveform pyramids
work_packages.scope:
- Decode audio once, compute min/max peak pyramid (levels of 256, 1024, 4096… samples per bin, i8/i16 pairs per channel mixed to mono + per-channel optional); store as a compact file in the disk cache; `waveform(media, lod, range) -> PeakData`; render-to-PNG helper (used by MCP `audio_waveform` later, P2).
- Runs as a job; progress events.
acceptance: Peaks for a synthetic −6 dBFS sine at 1 kHz are within ±1 LSB of the expected amplitude at every LOD (test); level N+1 bins are exactly the min/max of level N pairs (property test).
1 h of 48 kHz stereo audio computes in < 60 s (recorded).

work_packages.title: Job manager v0 and import job
work_packages.scope:
- `cutweave-jobs` v0: in-memory job registry persisted to `jobs` table in `cache.sqlite` for history only (resume across restarts is P5): `JobId`, `kind`, `state{Queued,Running,Succeeded,Failed,Cancelled}`, `progress{fraction,message}`, `CancelToken`; worker pool on tokio `spawn_blocking` with a **GPU/IO budget** semaphore (max concurrent decode jobs = cores/2; export = 1); event stream `job.progress`.
- Commands/queries: `job.status{id}` (q), `job.list` (q), `job.cancel{id}`.
- `media.import{paths[], dest?}` command: validates paths (exist, within allowed roots in headless/MCP mode), then **registers media synchronously**: probe each file (per-file timeout, default 5 s, up to 4 in parallel) + fast content hash, then `media.register` through the bus; returns `{media_ids[], failed[{path, error}]}` as soon as registration is done. Probe failure/timeout/corrupt file → entry in `failed[]` (no asset created).
- **Analysis is asynchronous:** after registration it spawns per-asset jobs (index → thumbnails (1D.05) → waveform (1D.06)) and returns their `job_ids[]`; emits `media.indexed{media_id}` when the index is ready. A failing stage sets `analysis_error` on the (already registered) asset so the UI shows a badge.
- Query `job.wait{job_id, timeout_ms}` (timeout capped at 60 s): returns the job's current/final state; returns early on completion, otherwise `{state:"running", progress}` at timeout. Exposed through RPC/CLI and, via 1J.01, as the MCP tool `job_wait`.
acceptance: `media.import` of 3 corpus clips returns 3 `media_ids` in < 2 s (synchronous registration; `media.list` immediately shows them with `probe` populated); thumbnails/waveforms are retrievable after `job.wait` on the returned job ids (< 10 s). Import of the broken MP4 returns it in `failed[]` (no asset in `media.list`); a probe that exceeds the timeout (fake slow backend) is reported in `failed[]` within timeout + 100 ms.
`job.wait{timeout_ms:100}` on a running job returns `state:"running"` after ~100 ms; on a finished job returns immediately (test).
Cancelling a running import stops decoding within 500 ms.
`media.import` of a path outside allowed roots (MCP/headless mode) returns `Invalid{path}` (path-allowlist test).

work_packages.title: Settings pages for this computer: Cache and storage, Performance and hardware
work_packages.area: `crates/cutweave-cache` (limits, usage, clear), `crates/cutweave-media` (decode policy), `crates/cutweave-engine` (`--cache-dir`, engine commands, UI-only scopes), `crates/cutweave-cli` (headless flag), generated schema and TS types, `apps/desktop` (launch flag from the preference), `packages/editor` (the two pages), `docs/reference/launch-protocol.md`, `docs/reference/settings.md`, `apps/desktop/e2e/flows`, `docs/user-flows.md`
work_packages.scope:
(product owner request, 2026-11-24: settings cover everything users can customize) the "This computer" pages of the settings catalog (`docs/reference/settings.md`) for the caches and hardware P1 already has. Values are machine preferences (WP-1M.11's `machine` group: never exported).
- **Cache and storage page:** the cache folder (folder picker; default the OS cache folder; main passes it as `--cache-dir` at engine start, so the row says "Applies the next time Cutweave starts" and the old folder is left for the person to delete); for thumbnails and filmstrips (2 GiB default, WP-1D.05) and waveforms (512 MiB default, now enforced with WP-1D.06's LRU) the usage and a limit; "Clear" per kind and "Clear all" (confirm). Clearing never touches projects or `generated/` media; caches rebuild on demand. Later WPs add their rows to this page: proxies (WP-2F.03), background renders (WP-2J.09).
- **Performance and hardware page:** hardware decoding Auto or Off (WP-1D.04's policy; applies to decoders opened after the change, and open pools reopen on their next seek); memory for decoded frames, Auto (the smaller of 1 GiB and a quarter of RAM) or 512 MiB / 1 / 2 / 4 GiB; read-only information: the GPU adapter in use and the hardware encoders found (`media.capabilities`). The hardware encoding default is on the Export page (WP-1M.13).
- **Engine surface:** query `media.cache_status` → `{folder, kinds:[{kind, bytes, limit_bytes, entries}], decode_hw, frame_cache_bytes}` (readable by agents); commands `media.set_cache_config{limits?, frame_cache_bytes?}`, `media.clear_cache{kinds}` and `media.set_decode_policy{hw: auto|off}`: engine commands, not undoable, not journaled, never dirty the project, and **UI-only scope** (ADR-0016; an agent token gets `forbidden`). A lower limit shrinks the cache at once (LRU). The editor applies the preferences after every handshake, like WP-1M.10.
- **Headless engines** take `--cache-dir` (and `CUTWEAVE_CACHE_DIR`) and the defaults; documented in the launch protocol and the CLI reference.

Integration: an agent token calling `media.set_cache_config`, `media.clear_cache` or `media.set_decode_policy` over RPC, MCP (`cutweave_execute`) and the CLI gets `forbidden`; `media.cache_status` answers agents.
With hardware decoding Off, a newly opened decoder is the CPU one (decoder-kind probe in the integration test).

**A user flow (ADR-0018, F23):** Settings > Cache and storage lists each cache kind with its usage and limit; after the bin has drawn thumbnails of the demo media (real decode), "Clear" on thumbnails drops their usage to zero; choose another cache folder (OS picker stubbed), relaunch: the page shows the new folder and the engine writes there. Performance and hardware shows the GPU name and the hardware decoding choice survives the relaunch.

work_packages.title: Software encode + MP4 mux (H.264 + AAC)
work_packages.scope:

- Progress callback, cancel token; partial file removed on cancel/failure.

Cancel mid-encode leaves no file; error paths tested (disk full simulated via failing writer).
Plays in `ffplay`/VLC and Chromium `<video>` (manual checklist item once per OS in PR; automated: `ffmpeg -v error -i out.mp4 -f null -` exits 0 with empty stderr).

work_packages.title: Hardware encoders with software fallback
work_packages.scope:
- H.264 HW encoders: NVENC, AMF, QSV (Windows/Linux), VideoToolbox (macOS), VA-API (Linux) via FFmpeg; capability probe by attempting to open a 256×256 test encode (cached per session); selection order per OS documented; `EncodeSpec.hw: Auto|Off|Force(name)`.

work_packages.title: Export pipeline, `export.start` command, offline audio mixdown
work_packages.scope:
- `export.start{sequence, path, range?: {in,out}, preset: "h264-mp4-1080p" | custom{width,height,fps,quality}, hw?}` command → returns `{job_id}`; export job: snapshot the doc at start (immutable; later edits don't affect it), for each frame `t = i / fps` render via `cutweave-render` (full quality, originals not proxies, headless wgpu — device shared with preview via a GPU-budget lock) → read back → `Encoder`; audio: offline mixdown (1G.02 `mixdown`) of the timeline range fed to AAC.
- Frame loop uses decode-ahead prefetch (decoder pool reuse, sequential decode — no per-frame seek) so 1080p simple timeline export ≥ 2× realtime with HW encode on reference machine.
- Progress events (`job.progress` with fps + ETA), cancel (stops within 1 s, deletes partial), error mapping (`Unsupported`, `Io`, `HwUnavailable` fallback).

Cancel at 50% → job state `Cancelled`, no output file.

**Preview matches export:** for 5 timestamps, the frame read back from the export pipeline before encoding is **bit-identical** to `render.frame` at full quality on the same adapter (tolerance policy).

Exporting twice from the same snapshot yields **frame-hash-identical** decoded output (decode both MP4s to raw and compare hashes) with threads fixed (x264 `threads=1` flag used in the determinism test only).

work_packages.title: Timeline evaluation → scene description
work_packages.scope:
- Pure function `evaluate(snapshot: &DocSnapshot, seq: SequenceId, t: Time, quality: Quality) -> Scene` where `Scene{size, background, layers: Vec<Layer{item, media, source_time: Time, transform, opacity, color_tags}>}` for visible video clips (top track last), mapping timeline time → source time (`source_in + (t - start)`), skipping disabled/hidden/muted-not-relevant items; for transitions/effects variants: not present.

work_packages.title: wgpu compositor: linear light, color conversion, transform/opacity
work_packages.scope:

work_packages.title: Quality ladder, frame readback, `render.frame` query
work_packages.scope:
- Preview quality ladder `Quality::{Full, Half, Quarter}` (scale applied at output size; decode at reduced size is future), `AutoQuality` controller (inputs: recent frame time, target fps; drop one level after 5 consecutive late frames, raise when paused → **refine to Full when paused**, arch §8).
- Readback: async buffer mapping (double-buffered staging buffers, no GPU stall on the render thread) producing `Rgba8`/`Nv12` for the SHM ring and `Jpeg/Png` for agents (JPEG via `jpeg-encoder`/`image`, default max 768 px long side, `max_size` param, quality 80).
- Query `render.frame{sequence, t, max_size?, fmt: "jpeg"|"png", quality?}` → `{image: bytes|resource, width, height, time, items_visible: [ItemId], rev}`; at `t` outside content returns the background frame, never an error.
