acceptance: `render.frame` of a 3-clip project at 3 distinct times returns correct frames (compared with golden refs via 1O.01 harness once available; before that against analytic expected colors of synthetic clips within ΔE < 2).
Auto-quality unit tests: simulated frame times drive ladder transitions exactly as specified (5 late → down, paused → Full).
1080p `render.frame` to 768 px JPEG end-to-end < 150 ms on dev machine with warm cache (recorded).

work_packages.title: Mixer graph and clip audio sources
work_packages.scope:
- Mixer graph v0: per-clip sources → per-track bus (gain, mute) → master (gain, hard-clip protection `tanh`-free soft limiter placeholder at 0 dBFS) → output; fixed 2-ch f32 output at the device rate.
- **Real-time thread discipline** (arch §9): lock-free SPSC ring buffers fed by decode workers (decode → `rubato` resample to device rate → ring); the callback does no allocation, no locks, no syscalls (verified by `assert_no_alloc` in tests).
- Prefetch policy: workers keep ≥ 500 ms ahead of the clock; seek flushes rings and refills; graph updates (doc changes) delivered via a lock-free command queue / double-buffered `Arc` swap of the segment list.
- `cutweave-audio` depends only on `MediaBackend`'s `AudioDecoder` trait — usable with `FakeBackend`.
- Offline renderer `mixdown(segments, range, rate) -> impl Iterator<AudioChunk>` using the **same graph code** (shared test: offline == realtime-render-to-buffer within 1e-6).
acceptance: Test with 4 overlapping tone clips mixed offline equals the analytical sum within 1e-5; clip boundaries are sample-accurate (impulse test: first sample of clip at exactly `time_to_samples(start)`).
10 min simulated realtime run using a mock sink at 256-sample buffers with 8 sources: 0 underruns, 0 allocations in the callback (assert_no_alloc).
Resampling 44.1k→48k of a 1 kHz sine has THD+N < −90 dB (test).
work_packages.tests: unit, property (offline==realtime), soak test (short in CI, long nightly).
work_packages.out_of_scope: time-stretch, pan, EQ, ducking, fades (P2), cpal (1G.02).

work_packages.title: cpal output, master clock, volume
work_packages.scope:
- `AudioOutput` over cpal 0.18: device enumeration, default device, buffer size request (256; fall back per S2 recommendation), sample-format negotiation, reconnect/default-device-change handling (restart stream; clock stays monotonic).
- **Master clock:** `AudioClock` atomics: `samples_played` (callback-updated), device output latency from cpal timestamps (`OutputCallbackInfo`), `position() -> Time` = timeline start + (samples_played − latency_samples)/rate; `is_running`; readable lock-free from any thread; used by 1H for A/V sync.
- Null/dummy device mode (`CUTWEAVE_AUDIO=null`) with a wall-clock-driven fake clock for CI and headless MCP (explicitly deterministic variant: `ManualClock` advanced by tests).
- Per-track volume (`audio_gain`) and mute applied; master volume as `view.set_master_gain` (`view` namespace: not undoable, not journaled; persisted via 1C.04).
- Meters: peak per bus published at 30 Hz via a lock-free ring (consumed by UI later).
acceptance: On a dev machine with an audio device: 10 min playback of the 8-source mix at 256-sample buffer reports 0 underruns, clock tracking error vs the device's sample progress < 2 ms over 10 min (the clock follows the device crystal by design, §9; drift vs `Instant` is reported, not gated: on the reference headset it is +11 ppm ≈ 6.6 ms/10 min, as Spike S2 measured).
Unplugging/changing the default device during playback (manual test on Windows + macOS, documented) restarts the stream within 2 s without crash.
Headless CI passes using null device; `AudioClock::position()` is monotonic non-decreasing (property test).
work_packages.tests: unit with null device; manual hardware checklist recorded in PR; soak nightly.

work_packages.title: Transport, A/V sync, scrub scheduler, JKL
work_packages.scope:
- Transport state machine `Stopped | Playing{rate} | Scrubbing` with commands in `view` namespace: `view.play`, `view.pause`, `view.seek{t}`, `view.set_rate{rate}` (JKL semantics: J = reverse step levels −1×/−2×/−4×… (**reverse playback = frame-step video, muted audio in P1**), K = pause, L = 1×/2×/4×; K+J/K+L = slow ±0.5× not required), `view.step{frames}`, `view.set_loop` (optional in/out not in P1), plus `playback.state{playing,rate,t,rev}` events at ≤ 30 Hz.
- Render loop thread: when Playing, follows the **audio clock** (`AudioClock::position`), picks target frame = floor to sequence frame grid, renders via `Renderer` with `AutoQuality`, skip-frames policy (drop late frames, never delay audio); prefetch of next N frames per active clip via decoder pool.
- **Latest-wins scrub scheduler:** seeks cancel in-flight render/decode (`CancelToken`), try frame cache first, emit low-res (Quarter) frame immediately then refine to Full when idle 100 ms (arch §10 step 5).
- Transport independent of UI: works headless (null audio clock) for MCP/CLI/tests.
- Playback state is not part of the document and not journaled (`view` namespace, arch §5.1); the playhead is persisted via 1C.04.
work_packages.interfaces: `Transport`, `PlaybackEngine::{attach(doc, renderer, audio, FrameSink)}`, `FrameSink` trait (SHM publisher or test sink), `view.*` commands.
acceptance: With `FakeBackend` + `ManualClock`: 10 s playback at 30 fps delivers exactly 300 frames in order, A/V offset (frame pts vs clock) ≤ 1 frame for 100% of frames; dropping a render artificially 3× slower than real time produces frame drops but never audio stalls (assert clock advanced steadily).
100 random seeks in 1 s intervals: no stale frame is ever delivered after a newer seek request (assert by seq numbers).
On a dev machine, 1080p30 single-layer playback of a corpus clip for 60 s with real audio: 0 dropped frames, A/V offset < 40 ms measured via the flash/click corpus clip and a timestamp log.
work_packages.tests: unit with fake clock; integration; nightly soak 10 min (full 30-min soak is P2/7D).
work_packages.out_of_scope: HW-measured budgets (arch §19 iGPU 3-layer), audio scrubbing, loop ranges.

work_packages.title: SHM ring publisher
work_packages.scope:
- Ring per `RING.md` from S1: named shared memory (Windows named file mapping; macOS/Linux POSIX `shm_open` or file in `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`/`/tmp` with 0600 perms via `memmap2`), name includes pid + random suffix, created by the engine, announced in the run-file (1I.01) and handshake; 4–6 slots; header `{magic, version, slot_count, slot_stride, write_idx: AtomicU64, audio_clock_flicks: AtomicI64, playing: AtomicBool}` and per-slot `{pts, w, h, format(NV12|RGBA8), rev, seq, size}`; seqlock-style slot publication (write `seq` odd → data → even) so readers detect torn reads.
- Publisher is a `FrameSink`: converts the rendered frame to RGBA8 (or NV12 if S1 showed benefit) at the **preview canvas size** reported by the UI (`view.set_preview_size{w,h}`), resizes the ring on size change with a generation counter.
- Audio clock word updated at ≥ 200 Hz from `AudioClock`.
- Cleanup on exit and stale-ring reaping at startup (rings from dead pids).
- Permission: object accessible only by the current user.
work_packages.interfaces: `ShmRing::{create, publish, set_clock}`, header layout in `crates/cutweave-playback/RING.md` (normative copy updated from S1).
acceptance: A Rust reader test (separate process) reading while the writer publishes 1080p60 for 60 s sees 0 torn frames (checksum in pixel data) and monotonic `seq`.
Writer overhead: publish of a 1080p RGBA frame (8 MB) p95 < 3 ms excluding render (bench).
After `kill -9` of the engine, the next engine start removes the stale ring (test).

work_packages.title: `cutweave-bridge` napi-rs addon (SHM reader)
work_packages.scope:
- napi-rs v3 addon exposing `openRing(name) -> Ring`, `Ring.header()`, `Ring.latestSlot(maxPtsFlicks?) -> {pts,w,h,format,rev,seq,buffer: ArrayBuffer}` (zero-copy external ArrayBuffer over the mapping, valid until the next call guarded by seqlock re-check), `Ring.audioClock()`, `Ring.close()`; plus `perfCounters()` stub.
- Prebuilt per-platform binaries built in CI (`@napi-rs/cli`, targets win32-x64, darwin-arm64, linux-x64-gnu), implementing **the transport chosen in ADR-001** (S1 report). Transport (a), the default: the addon is loaded by the **preload of the main editor window only, which runs with `sandbox:false`** (Electron sandboxed preloads cannot load native modules), `contextIsolation:true`, `nodeIntegration:false`, and is exposed to the page only through a narrow `contextBridge` API (`preview.getLatestFrame()`); the window loads local `app://` content only under the strict CSP of 1L.02; plugin iframes and all other windows get no preload and no addon. Transport (b), if ADR-001 chose it: the addon runs in a `utilityProcess` and frames are delivered over a transferred `MessagePort` to a fully sandboxed renderer.
- Failure modes: ring missing → typed JS error; version mismatch → error.
acceptance: Node test (Vitest, node environment) with a Rust-writer fixture binary: reader obtains ≥ 590 distinct frames in 10 s at 60 fps with 0 torn reads and buffer views are zero-copy (assert `buffer.byteLength === w*h*4` and no copy by checking `process.memoryUsage().arrayBuffers` growth < 20 MB).

Addon builds in CI on 3 OSes and loads in the **non-sandboxed main-window preload** (transport a) or the utilityProcess (transport b) per ADR-001 (smoke test in 1L.01 e2e); the renderer main world has no `require`/`process`, and a second window has no access to the addon (e2e).
work_packages.tests: Vitest + Rust fixture, CI build matrix.

work_packages.title: Source preview: play one media item outside any sequence
work_packages.area: `crates/cutweave-playback` (transport target, `view.*` transport commands, `playback.state`), `crates/cutweave-engine` (`full/preview.rs` and `full/audio.rs`: the source's frames and sound), generated schema and TS types, `docs/01-architecture.md` §10 (the decided paragraph), `docs/adr/0022-source-preview.md` (status once accepted)
work_packages.scope:
(product owner request, 2026-11-24: "I don't have a way to preview without adding to timeline") the preview transport plays a media asset on its own, as ADR-0022 decides (Accepted by the product owner, 2026-11-24).
- **One transport, two targets.** The document's `PlaybackEngine` plays either the active sequence (as today) or one media asset. `view.set_source{media?}` makes the asset the target; without `media` it returns to the sequence. Nothing touches the document: no item, no sequence, no undo step, no journal record, no unsaved state.
- **The source is a transient one-clip timeline** built from the probe: the asset's video and its audio, at its own frame rate (audio-only assets on a 30 fps grid over a blank picture), fitted into the preview size with the asset's aspect. It is indexed and rendered through the same `PreviewSource` path (compositor, quality ladder, hardware decode, proxies once WP-2F.02 lands) and its sound goes through the mixer on the master clock, so A/V sync, JKL, steps and scrubbing behave as on the sequence.
- **Playheads.** `view.play`, `view.pause`, `view.seek`, `view.step` and `view.set_rate` act on the current target, in its time. Each asset's source playhead is kept for the session; the sequence's playhead does not move while a source plays, and returning shows its frame exactly.
- **Events.** `playback.state` gains `source: {media, duration, fps} | null` (additive). After `view.set_source` returns, no frame of the old target reaches the ring (the transport's exact latest-wins rule), so the ring format does not change.
- **Ending.** Removing the asset, opening another project or `doc.reset` returns to the sequence with `source: null`. Timeline edits during a source session re-index the sequence as today and do not interrupt the source.
- **Agents and headless engines.** `view.set_source` is a `view` command (not undoable, not journaled, MCP catalog like the other `view` commands, not in `tools/list`); a headless engine plays into its null sink. Agents keep seeing media frames through `/media/{id}/thumb` and, in P2, `media_filmstrip`.
acceptance: With `FakeBackend` and `ManualClock`: a 10 s 25 fps asset plays 250 frames in order with A/V offset ≤ 1 frame; switching back mid-play shows the sequence's frame at its unchanged playhead; over 100 random switches and seeks, no frame of an old target is delivered after `view.set_source` returns.
The project stays clean, and `edit.history`, the journal and the saved document are byte-identical before and after a source session (test).
The engine's `preview_alloc` counting-allocator test passes with a source target (no per-frame allocation of our own).
Real media (corpus): an H.264 1080p30 and a HEVC 10-bit clip each play as a source for 10 s with 0 dropped frames on the dev machine (recorded); an audio-only asset plays its sound.
Removing the asset while it plays returns to the sequence (test).
work_packages.tests: unit with the fake clock, engine integration, alloc test, corpus.
work_packages.out_of_scope: the UI (WP-1M.15); in/out marks and inserting from a source (WP-2A.14); a second viewer playing at the same time (ADR-0022, option 2).

work_packages.title: axum server skeleton: auth, Host/Origin, run-file
work_packages.scope: - axum server bound to `127.0.0.1:` (`--port N`; `0` = random), tower middleware with **credential classes**: (1) the **UI credential**: a per-launch 256-bit token generated by Electron main and delivered to the engine **only over the spawn handshake pipe** (stdin), held in memory, **never written to disk or the run-file**, passed to the renderer through the preload bridge; (2) **agent tokens** (256-bit, labelled, e.g. `cli`, `mcp`) generated by the engine at start and stored in the run-file for CLI/MCP attach; (3) **internal** (in-process jobs). Presented as `Authorization: Bearer`; WS upgrade may use a subprotocol header. Media URLs for ``/`
work_packages.interfaces: `ApiServer::{start(config) -> RunningServer{port}}`, `Credential{Ui, Agent(label), Internal}`, `RunFile::{write, remove, discover()}`, `Scope::UiOnly` enforcement.
acceptance: Integration tests: no token → 401; wrong token → 401; right token + `Host: evil.com` → 403; right token + `Origin: https://evil.com` → 403; valid → 200 (≥ 8 cases).

Credential tests: the UI token never appears in the run-file, in logs, or on disk (grep of the engine's data dir after a session); an agent token invoking `test.ui_only` → `Forbidden`, the UI credential succeeds; the derived actor of a command is `user` / `agent:mcp` / `system` per credential (asserted via `doc.patched.actor`); a forged `_meta.actor` is ignored; a headless engine rejects any UI-credential handshake.
Run-file perms: on Unix `stat` mode is `0600`; on Windows the DACL grants only the current user (test via `icacls` parse).
`kill -9` leaves a stale run-file that `discover()` ignores (pid check) and startup cleans.

work_packages.title: JSON-RPC over WebSocket + event subscriptions
work_packages.scope:
- `ws://127.0.0.1:P/rpc`: JSON-RPC 2.0; methods = every registered command/query by name (`clip.split`, `timeline.get`, …) with `params` = command input; `request_id` (UUIDv7) is **required** on every mutating call from RPC clients (missing -> `Invalid`) and engine-generated for CLI/MCP; the engine dedupes per 1B.03 and a request resent after reconnect returns the original result; extra reserved methods `rpc.hello{client, version}` (returns `{engine_version, schema_hash, rev, shm?}`), `rpc.subscribe{events[]}`/`rpc.unsubscribe`, `project.snapshot` (full doc + rev; used for resync).
- Standard envelope extension: `params._meta{expected_rev, request_id, tx}` (**no client-asserted actor**: the actor is derived from the connection's credential, 1I.01); errors map `CmdError` → JSON-RPC error `{code, message, data{code,path,current_rev}}`.
- Events as notifications: `doc.patched{rev, actor, tx_id, ops}`, `playback.state`, `job.progress`, `media.indexed`, `project.dirty/saved/recovery_available`, with per-connection backpressure (bounded queue; on overflow drop the connection with close code 4001 `resync_required`).
- Rev-gap protocol: each `doc.patched` carries `prev_rev`; client detects gaps and calls `project.snapshot`.
- Concurrency: many connections; each request handled async but commands go through the single doc actor. Each WS connection has a `ConnId`; its closure triggers tx rollback (1B.09).
work_packages.interfaces: the RPC method namespace = registry; `RpcClientHello`, error code table in `docs/reference/rpc.md` (generated section in 1N).
acceptance: Test client issues `project.new`, `timeline.insert`, `clip.split`, `edit.undo` and receives the corresponding `doc.patched` events in order with consecutive revs; replaying events on an empty mirror equals `project.snapshot` (property test via `replay_events` from 1B.07).
The same `request_id` sent over two different connections returns the same result and `rev` increases once (test).
Stale `expected_rev` yields JSON-RPC error with `data.code="Conflict"` and the right `current_rev`.
Command round-trip over WS localhost p95 < 16 ms for `clip.trim` on a 400-item project (bench; arch §19 budget, recorded; gating threshold 25 ms on CI to allow noise).
50 concurrent connections issuing 100 commands each: no deadlock, final rev = total committed txs.

work_packages.title: Media HTTP endpoints
work_packages.scope:
- `GET /media/{id}/thumb?t=&w=`, `/media/{id}/filmstrip?w=&h=&count=`, `/media/{id}/waveform?lod=&start=&end=` (binary peaks or PNG via `fmt=png`), `/media/frame?seq=&t=&w=&h=&fmt=jpeg|png` (uses `render.frame`; the preview's JPEG fallback from WP-1M.04 calls it with `t` floored to the frame grid in integer flicks, even `w`/`h`, the token in `Authorization: Bearer`, and a CORS preflight from `app://cutweave` that must allow `authorization`); all authenticated (header or short-lived URL token param); validate params (bounds, `w` ≤ 4096); content-hash **ETag** + `Cache-Control: private, max-age=31536000, immutable` when keyed by content hash and `If-None-Match → 304`; range requests not needed.
- Concurrency limits (semaphore) and request cancellation when the client disconnects.
- 404 for unknown media; 422 with JSON error for bad params.
acceptance: Integration test with corpus: thumb returns decodable JPEG of requested width; repeated request with `If-None-Match` → 304 with 0 decodes; `/media/frame` for t=2 s returns the same bytes as `render.frame` query.
Disconnecting mid-request cancels the decode within 100 ms (test).
Requests without token → 401; `w=100000` → 422.

work_packages.title: `cutweave-engine` root: doc actor, project, jobs, API, launch protocol
work_packages.scope:
- `Engine::start(EngineConfig{mode: Gui|Headless|Oneshot, project?, port?, deterministic_ids?: u64, audio, gpu, allowed_roots, log})` wires the **core**: `DocActor` + registry (`cutweave-ops`), `ProjectStore` + journal + autosave, `JobManager`, `ApiServer` (1I.01, RPC 1I.02 mounts here). Media/render/audio/playback are attached by WP-1I.05 through a `Subsystems` extension point; without them the engine serves all document commands (enough for the UI and parity work to proceed in parallel).
- One engine = one open project (arch §14); session lifecycle `NoProject → Open → Closing`; `project.open/new/close` swap project state (cancel jobs, new journal). `Engine::shutdown()` flushes the journal, saves nothing implicitly, releases the lock, removes the run-file.
- **Launch protocol** (`docs/reference/launch-protocol.md`): CLI `--port N` (Electron main chooses the port on every (re)start); in `Gui` mode the UI credential arrives as the first line on stdin (never argv/env/disk); readiness line `{"event":"ready","port":P,"pid":N,"version":…}` on stdout (no tokens); orphan prevention (exit when stdin closes in `Gui` mode). Exit codes: 0 clean, 10 project-locked, 11 gpu-init-failed, 12 **port bind error** (so the supervisor can pick a new port), 13 bad handshake.
- `tracing` JSON logs to `~/.cutweave/logs/engine-<pid>.log` (rotation 5×10 MB), panic hook writes a crash marker, **no telemetry** (test asserts no outbound sockets during startup/shutdown).
work_packages.interfaces: `Engine`, `EngineConfig`, `Subsystems` trait, launch-protocol doc; `cutweave engine` (1K) wraps this.
acceptance: Integration test: start a `Headless` engine (core only), open a fixture project over RPC, run a command, `shutdown()`: run-file gone, lock released, thread count returns to baseline ±2.
Cold start to ready with an empty project < 1.0 s (core only; recorded).
Startup with a locked project exits 10 with a JSON error line; binding an occupied port exits 12.
In `Gui` mode with no handshake line within 5 s the engine exits 13.

work_packages.title: Engine subsystem wiring: media, render, audio, playback
work_packages.scope:
- Implement `Subsystems` for the full engine: `MediaBackend` + `DecoderPool` + caches (`FrameCache`, `ThumbCache`, `WaveformCache`), `Renderer`/`GpuContext` (software or real per `EngineConfig.gpu`), `AudioOutput`/null clock per `EngineConfig.audio`, `PlaybackEngine` + `ShmRing` publisher (Gui mode), registration of the `render.frame`, `export.start`, `view.*` transport commands and the media HTTP state for 1I.03.
- Lifecycle: ordered startup/shutdown (stop playback → join render/audio threads → close caches), device-lost propagation, per-project teardown on `project.close`; SHM ring name published in the run-file/handshake; GPU/audio failure degrade rules (audio fails → null clock + warning event; GPU fails → exit 11 in Gui mode, software fallback in headless).
- `EngineConfig.deterministic_ids` honoured end-to-end (1B.08).
acceptance: Full headless engine (null audio, software GPU) integration test: import corpus clip → insert → `render.frame` → play 2 s on a manual clock → export 1 s → shutdown with no leaked threads or SHM objects.
Cold start to ready with an empty project < 1.5 s on a dev machine (recorded; arch §19 start budget is 2.5 s for the whole app).
Forcing audio init failure yields a working engine with `engine.degraded` (test).
work_packages.out_of_scope: new features; this WP only composes existing crates.

work_packages.title: rmcp server: registry-derived tools, `cutweave_execute`, annotations
work_packages.depends_raw: WP-1I.01, WP-1B.09, WP-1B.06, WP-1D.07 (job status/wait provider), WP-1E.03 (`export.start`)
work_packages.scope:
- rmcp (version pinned per S5/ADR-009) server mounted on `/mcp` (Streamable HTTP) with the same token/Host/Origin middleware.
- **15 core tools (mcp="core")**: `project_open`, `project_info`, `media_import`, `media_list`, `timeline_get`, `timeline_insert`, `clip_split`, `clip_trim`, `clip_move`, `item_delete`, `edit_undo`, `export_start`, `job_status`, **`job_wait{job_id, timeout_ms}`**, and `render_frame` (implemented in 1J.02). Names derive from command names with `.`→`_`; descriptions, schemas and **annotations** (`readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint`, `idempotentHint`) are generated from `CommandMeta`. `edit_redo` and the rest of the registry are reachable through `cutweave_execute`/`cutweave_query`.
- `media_import` returns `media_ids` synchronously (1D.07); agents then call `job_wait` on the returned analysis job ids if they need thumbnails/index; `export_start` returns `job_id` and `job_wait` blocks up to `timeout_ms` (<= 60 s) so agents need no polling loops.
- **4 generic tools:** `cutweave_search_commands{query}` (fuzzy over name/summary), `cutweave_describe_command{name}` (full JSON Schema), `cutweave_execute{steps[{cmd,args}], dry_run?, expected_rev?}` — **transactional batch** (one tx → one undo step; `$ref` between steps like `{"$ref":"steps[0].output.left"}`; on any step error the whole tx rolls back and the error names the failing step index), `cutweave_query{name,args}`.
- Tool results: structured content (JSON) + short text summary; errors as MCP tool errors with `code`, `message`, `path`, `hint`.
- **Tool profiles are per endpoint, never per connection:** `/mcp` (standard = the 20 above in P1, R33), `/mcp/minimal` (<= 12 tools: `project_info`, `media_list`, `timeline_get`, `render_frame`, `job_wait`, `edit_undo` + the 4 generic tools), `/mcp/full` (standard + search-based long tail; identical to standard in P1); stdio servers take `--profile minimal|standard|full`.
- **Tool-list budgets (single source):** minimal <= 12 tools / <= 3k tokens; standard <= 36 tools / <= 8k tokens; full = standard + search-based long tail; **P1 gate: `/mcp` lists <= 20 tools and <= 5k tokens (R33)** (tokens estimated as ceil(bytes of compact `tools/list` JSON / 4), method documented). CI fails when exceeded.
- Transcripts/metadata strings in results wrapped `{"untrusted": true, ...}` per arch §14.
- Actor for MCP calls = `agent:<token label>` (credential-derived, 1I.01); MCP session end/disconnect rolls back that connection's open tx (1B.09).
acceptance: An rmcp client test on `/mcp` lists exactly the registry's core tools plus the 4 generic ones (18 here, as `render_frame` arrives with 1J.02, which raises the gate to 20, R33), within the 5k-token gate; `/mcp/minimal` lists <= 12 tools and <= 3k tokens; each core tool call returns the same output as the RPC call for the same args (spot-checked by 1O.02 parity).
`cutweave_execute` with 3 steps where step 3 fails leaves the doc and rev unchanged and returns `failed_step: 2`; with `dry_run: true` the doc is unchanged and the response lists predicted ops.
Tools have correct annotations: `clip_split` not read-only; `timeline_get` read-only (test per tool).
work_packages.tests: rmcp client integration (HTTP), snapshot of `tools/list` (insta) — becomes the committed MCP catalog snapshot.
work_packages.out_of_scope: resources (1J.02), prompts, tasks extension, elicitation, per-connection profiles.

work_packages.title: `render_frame` image content + resources
work_packages.scope:
- Tool `render_frame{sequence?, t, max_size?=768, fmt?="jpeg"}` returning an MCP **image content block** (base64 JPEG ≤ 768 px long side default) **plus** structured metadata `{time, rev, width, height, items_visible[], notes}`; never exceeds a 1 MB payload (re-encode at lower quality / reject with hint to lower `max_size`).
- Resources: `cutweave://project` (summary JSON), `cutweave://sequence/{id}/timeline` (paginated summary, first page ≤ 4 KB), `cutweave://catalog/commands` (command list); change notifications on `cutweave://project` use **whatever the negotiated MCP revision supports** (`resources/subscribe` + `notifications/resources/updated` on 2025-11-25; `subscriptions/listen` on 2026-07-28) behind one `Notifier` abstraction fed by `doc.patched`; nothing depends on `ping` for the newer revision.
- Large frames returned as resource links (`cutweave://frame/{rev}/{t}`) when requested `max_size` > 1568 (document threshold).
acceptance: MCP client test calls `render_frame` on the 3-clip fixture at t=2 s: result has exactly one image content block, valid JPEG ≤ 768 px, metadata `items_visible` contains the expected item ID.

Under **each** of the two MCP revisions (rmcp client configured per revision), subscribing to `cutweave://project` and then running `clip_split` produces an update notification within 200 ms; `tools/list` now has 20 tools (R33).

work_packages.title: stdio transports: `attach` proxy and `headless`
work_packages.scope:
- `cutweave mcp --headless [--project X] [--allow-root DIR…]`: in-process `Engine` (Headless, audio Null) serving MCP over stdio (rmcp stdio transport); stdout reserved strictly for protocol frames, logs to stderr/file.
- `cutweave mcp --attach [--run-file PATH|--pid N] [--profile minimal|standard|full]`: stdio proxy discovering the running GUI engine via the run-file (1I.01), connecting to `/mcp` (or `/mcp/<profile>`) over HTTP with an **agent token from the run-file** (never the UI credential), forwarding JSON-RPC both ways incl. notifications; multiple engines → error listing pids and require `--pid`; engine vanishes → proxy exits non-zero with a clear JSON-RPC error.
- Filesystem allowlist (arch §14/§18): headless mode allows project folder + `--allow-root`; `media.import`/`export.start` paths outside → error `Invalid` with hint.
- Documentation snippet `docs/reference/mcp-clients.md` with config JSON for Claude Desktop/Code stdio (`cutweave mcp --headless`).

work_packages.title: Agent targeting with several engines: list, choose by project, last-focused default
work_packages.scope:
(product owner request, 2026-11-24) when several engines run (the app plus headless engines from scripts, today; one per window later), an agent must be able to see them and pick one without a process id in its config.
- **The run-file says what a chooser needs:** the open project (name and path, or none), mode (GUI or headless), start time, and for GUI engines when its window last had focus. Main reports window focus to its engine; run-file writes stay atomic and stale files keep being ignored by the pid check.

If no GUI engine runs and several headless ones do, they fail with exit 3, listing the engines and how to choose.

work_packages.title: Electron security hardening (arch §18)
work_packages.scope:
- `webPreferences` (via one `createWindow()` factory): **main editor window**: `contextIsolation: true`, `nodeIntegration: false`, **`sandbox: false` for its preload only** (required to load the napi addon under transport (a) of ADR-001; if ADR-001 chose transport (b) this window is `sandbox: true` as well), preload minimal and audited, narrow `contextBridge`; **every other window** (dialogs, future plugin panels) and all iframes: `sandbox: true`, no preload, no addon; the factory rejects any other combination (unit test), `webSecurity: true`, `allowRunningInsecureContent: false`, `enableBlinkFeatures` none, `webviewTag: false`, `nodeIntegrationInSubFrames: false`; no `remote`.
- **Strict CSP** set via `session.webRequest.onHeadersReceived` and `<meta>`: `default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' (no 'unsafe-inline'; any exception must be justified in the checklist); img-src 'self' data: blob: http://127.0.0.1:<enginePort>; connect-src ws://127.0.0.1:<port> http://127.0.0.1:<port>; font-src 'self'; media-src blob: http://127.0.0.1:<port>; object-src 'none'; frame-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'` (**the port is chosen by Electron main at app launch** and passed to the engine with `--port` on every (re)start; the policy is built by one function `buildCsp(port)` with unit tests and **served by main's `app://` protocol handler as response headers**, so it can change without touching disk. If the engine's bind fails (exit 12) main picks a new port, restarts the engine and **reloads the renderer** with the updated CSP).
- **Validated IPC:** `ipcMain.handle` only for allowlisted channels, each with a **zod schema** for args, `event.senderFrame.url` origin check, no generic `invoke(channel, ...)` exposed — preload exposes only named functions through `contextBridge`.
- `setWindowOpenHandler` → deny all (external links via `shell.openExternal` only for `https:` and only through an allowlisted IPC); `will-navigate` blocked except app origin; `setPermissionRequestHandler`/`CheckHandler` deny all except none needed; `session.setCertificateVerifyProc` default; block `file://` navigation outside app bundle.
- Electron fuses flipped at package time (`@electron/fuses`): `RunAsNode=false`, `EnableNodeOptionsEnvironmentVariable=false`, `EnableNodeCliInspectArguments=false`, `EnableEmbeddedAsarIntegrityValidation=true`, `OnlyLoadAppFromAsar=true`.
- Credential handoff: main generates the **UI token**, sends it to the engine over the spawn handshake pipe (stdin; never argv/env/disk/run-file) and to the renderer only through the preload `contextBridge` getter (never URL, DOM, localStorage or logs). Agent tokens live in the engine's run-file and are never exposed to the renderer.
- Audit checklist `docs/security/electron-checklist.md` with each item and the test that proves it.
acceptance: Playwright security tests (all must pass): `window.require`/`process` are `undefined` in the renderer main world (main window has `sandbox:false` for the preload only); a second `BrowserWindow` created through the factory is `sandbox:true` and has no `window.cutweave.preview`; an iframe has no bridge; the window factory throws on `sandbox:false` for a non-main window; `fetch('http://example.com')` blocked by CSP; `fetch(engine /rpc)` without token returns 401; navigation to `https://example.com` is blocked; `window.open` returns null; unregistered IPC channel invocation rejected; an invalid-args IPC call rejected with a zod error.
`npx @electron/fuses read --app <packaged>` output matches the expected fuse state (test parses it).

Port-change test: force exit 12 on the first start (occupied port); main picks a new port, restarts, reloads the renderer, and the response CSP header (read via Playwright `response.headers()`) contains the new port and not the old.
Third-party scan with `electronegativity` (or equivalent) reports no High findings (CI step, allowlist file reviewed by human).
work_packages.tests: Playwright security suite; unit tests for CSP builder and IPC validator.

work_packages.title: Engine supervision, restart and UI resync
work_packages.scope:
- Main process `EngineSupervisor`: spawn `cutweave engine` with args/env per launch protocol (1I.04), parse readiness line (timeout 10 s), choose the port at launch (`--port`, pick a new free port on exit 12 and on every restart if the previous one is not free; reload the renderer with the new CSP per 1L.02), send the freshly generated **UI token over the spawn handshake pipe** (never written to disk), watch `exit`/`error`; states `starting → ready → crashed → restarting → failed`; exponential backoff restart (0.5 s, 1 s, 2 s; give up after 3 crashes in 60 s ⇒ `failed` with user-visible error dialog offering "Restart"/"Quit"), kill-on-quit (graceful `SIGTERM`/`rpc shutdown`, force kill after 3 s), orphan prevention (engine exits when parent pipe closes).
- On restart the engine re-opens the same project folder → journal recovery runs **automatically in "auto-recover" mode for supervised restarts** (replay journal; no prompt) — user-initiated cold open of a dirty project shows the restore/discard dialog (1M.07). Documented difference.
- Renderer connection layer (in `packages/protocol` client + `docStore`): on WS close → state `reconnecting`, queued **in-flight commands retained with `request_id`**, after new `ready` the client re-handshakes (`rpc.hello`), compares `schema_hash`, fetches `project.snapshot`, **re-sends un-acked commands** (idempotent via `request_id`: UUIDv7, 10-min dedup window per arch §5.1, engine dedupes through the journal; no duplicates, no losses), replays `view` state (playhead, selection kept client-side), SHM ring reopened.
- UI banner "Engine restarted — recovered" for 3 s; failure state blocks editing with a clear message.
- Test hooks: `CUTWEAVE_TEST_CRASH_AFTER=N` (engine aborts after N commands) and a Playwright helper `killEngine()`.
acceptance: Security: after a restart the engine accepts the fresh UI token main generates for the new engine process (a token is never reused across processes) and rejects the old agent token's UI-only calls; the UI token is absent from disk (grep of the temp HOME) and from the run-file.

Playwright test: edit (3 commands), `killEngine()` (SIGKILL), UI shows `reconnecting`, then recovers in < 5 s; `timeline_get` shows all 3 commands applied exactly once; a command fired **during** the outage is applied exactly once after recovery (**0 lost, 0 duplicated**, repeated 10×).
4 kills in 60 s → app enters `failed` with the dialog (test asserts state).

work_packages.title: Timeline interactions: select, move, trim, split, delete, snapping
work_packages.scope:
- Explicit **interaction state machine** (arch §16; XState-lite own implementation, pure & unit-testable): states `Idle → Hovering → Selecting | Moving | TrimmingStart | TrimmingEnd | ScrubbingRuler | DroppingMedia | Panning`; transitions emit **intents** `{kind: Move, item, to_track, at}` etc., which the editor layer converts into commands.
- Gestures use **gesture transactions** (arch §5.2): pointer-down on a clip begins `edit.begin_tx{kind:"gesture"}`; drag sends `clip.move`/`clip.trim` updates throttled to animation frames (engine applies live → preview updates); pointer-up `commit_tx`; Esc cancels (`cancel_tx`) restoring state; each gesture = exactly **one** undo step.
- Operations: click select (+shift multi-select, click empty deselect, marquee optional), move within and across same-kind tracks, trim edges, **split at playhead** (`S` key / toolbar button, applies to selected or clip under playhead), **delete** (`Delete/Backspace`), drop media from bin to timeline (`timeline.insert` at pointer time/track, snaps), playhead scrub on ruler.
- **Snapping** to playhead, clip edges and frame grid within 8 px (toggle `N`), computed client-side in flicks; commands always carry frame-aligned times.
- Engine errors (`Invalid` overlap/`Locked`) revert the gesture-tx state and show a toast; no client-side duplicate validation beyond snapping.
work_packages.interfaces: `@cutweave/timeline` state machine API `reduce(state, event) → {state, intents}`; editor `useTimelineIntents()`.
acceptance: State-machine Vitest suite ≥ 40 cases (every transition incl. Esc cancel, drag outside bounds, trim beyond media length).

Playwright e2e against a real engine: drag clip 100 px → doc shows moved start (frame-aligned), one undo entry (`edit.history` length +1), undo restores; trim, split-at-playhead, delete behave per `edit-semantics.md` (6 e2e tests).

work_packages.title: Schema emission + snapshot gate
work_packages.scope:
- `cargo xtask gen` builds a small `cutweave-gen` bin (in `xtask`, depending on `cutweave-ops`) that dumps: `schema/commands.json` and `schema/queries.json` (full catalog: name, summary, flags, mcp exposure, annotations, input/output JSON Schema, error codes), `schema/events.json` (event catalog from 1I.02/1C.03), `schema/patch-fixtures.json` (for 1M.02), `schema/mcp-tools.json` (core tool names/annotations as produced by 1J.01), and `docs/reference/commands.md` (human table).
- **Snapshot gate (arch §5.3):** `cargo xtask gen --check` regenerates into a temp dir and fails with a unified diff if committed files differ; plus `insta` snapshot tests for `schema/commands.json` in `cutweave-ops` so a diff requires `cargo insta review` approval. `schema_hash` (sha256 of commands.json) embedded in the engine (`rpc.hello`) and in `packages/protocol` generated constants.
- Deterministic output (sorted keys, stable formatting); CI job `schema-snapshot` (0A.03) calls `--check`.
acceptance: `cargo xtask gen --check` exits 0 on main; after adding a field to a command without regenerating, it exits non-zero printing the diff (verified in a negative test in `xtask` tests using a temp fixture crate or a feature flag).
Running `gen` twice yields byte-identical files; all registry commands appear (count equals `cutweave commands --json | jq length`).
work_packages.out_of_scope: TS output (1N.02), per-surface (CLI/MCP) docs beyond the above.

work_packages.title: TS protocol package: generated types and typed RPC client
work_packages.scope:
- `cargo xtask gen` additionally emits `packages/protocol/src/generated/{types.ts, commands.ts, events.ts, schema-hash.ts}` via **specta** (`specta-typescript`): all model types (`Project`, `Item`, `Time` as TS `number` per arch §4.1 / ADR-015, IDs as branded string types `MediaId = string & {__brand}`), command input/output maps `CommandMap = { "clip.split": {input: SplitItem, output: SplitOutput}, … }`, `EventMap`, and `CmdErrorCode` union. Header comment `// @generated — do not edit; run cargo xtask gen`.
- Hand-written (small) `packages/protocol/src/{rpc.ts, patch.ts, index.ts}`: typed `RpcClient.call<K extends keyof CommandMap>(name, input) => Promise<CommandMap[K]["output"]>` and `on<E extends keyof EventMap>`; `applyPatch` (1M.02 completes use).
- Biome ignores `generated/`; `tsc --strict` compiles; package builds ESM + d.ts via `tsup`.
- CI gate: the `schema-snapshot` job runs `cargo xtask gen --check` including TS files, so a Rust change without regenerated TS fails.
acceptance: `pnpm --filter @cutweave/protocol build && pnpm --filter @cutweave/protocol test` pass; a type test (`tsd`/`expectTypeOf`) proves `call("clip.split", {item, at})` typed and `call("clip.split", {item})` is a compile error; `call("nope")` is a compile error.
Changing `SplitItem` in Rust without regenerating makes `cargo xtask gen --check` fail (as in 1N.01).
Generated files contain no `any` (grep test) and no `bigint` anywhere (grep) and `Time` is `number` per ADR-015.

work_packages.title: Settings framework: tabbed pages, search, preferences store, reset, import and export
work_packages.area: `apps/desktop` (preferences store and IPC in main, values main needs before the window exists), `packages/editor` (settings dialog, page registry, theme migration), `packages/ui` (`SettingsLayout`, `SettingRow`; specs in `design/components/`), one preferences schema module that main and the editor both import (a small `packages/preferences` workspace package, or another single home; justify it in the PR), `docs/reference/settings.md`, `apps/desktop/e2e/flows`, `docs/user-flows.md`
work_packages.scope:
(product owner request, 2026-11-24: "tabbed with categories … everything that can be customizable, will be") turn the quick File > Settings… (one Theme row) into the frame that every settings page plugs into. The full inventory (every setting with its default, scope, storage, agent access and owning WP) is the catalog `docs/reference/settings.md`; this WP builds the frame and the pages whose features exist with no new engine work. The other P1 pages are WP-1M.13 (Export, Keyboard shortcuts), WP-1J.05 (Agents and MCP, Notifications) and WP-1D.08 (Cache and storage, Performance and hardware); later pages come with their features.
- **Three homes** (arch paragraph below): *app preferences* (the person's, every project), *this computer* (machine values: the same file, a `machine` group that export and import skip), and *project settings* (in the document, undoable, agents read and change them; edited in File > Project settings…, WP-2H.08, not in this dialog). Secrets never go in preferences: keys go to the keychain through write-only `ai.set_key` (arch §13).
- **Preferences store in main:** `<userData>/preferences.json` next to `recent-projects.json` and `window-state.json`. One versioned schema (keys, types, defaults, ranges); a damaged or partly invalid file never blocks startup (bad keys fall back to their defaults, the file is rewritten clean, a warning goes to the main log); atomic writes (temp file, fsync, rename); schema migrations like the project's. The renderer gets the snapshot before first paint and subscribes to changes; it writes one key at a time through new allowlisted, zod-validated IPC (`prefs:get`, `prefs:set`, `prefs:reset`, event `prefs:changed`), with a row in `SECURITY-MODEL.md`.
- **Apply plumbing:** each key says who applies it: the renderer, main, the engine through a UI-only command after each handshake and on change (WP-1M.10's pattern), or main at engine start (a flag). Rows that need the engine are disabled with "Needs the engine" while it is disconnected; rows that apply at the next start say so.
- **Moves what exists onto the store:** the theme (read once from the renderer's old `localStorage` value, then removed there) and WP-1M.10's Saving rows. Main reads the theme before it creates the window, so the window background and the title-bar overlay open in the right colors with no flash.
- **The frame:** a large modal dialog in the main window (other windows are sandboxed with no preload and cannot reach the engine, arch §2): a vertical side tab list of pages grouped as in the catalog (Preferences; Agents and AI; Extensions; Privacy and updates; This computer; Advanced), one page per category, and a search field above the tabs (focused on open). Each page is a list of `SettingRow`s: label, control, one-line description, and a reset button when the value differs from its default. Changes apply at once; "Done" closes. A page appears once it has a shipped row.
- **Page registry:** pages and rows are data (`{id, title, icon, group, order, rows: [{key, label, description, keywords, control, applies}]}`, controls: switch, segmented, select, number with unit, folder, list, action, custom). Later WPs register a page or a row with no change to the frame. A test checks that every registered key has a row in `docs/reference/settings.md`.
- **Search** across every page: matches labels, descriptions and keywords in the UI language, shows the matching rows grouped by page with the match marked, and "No settings match "x"" otherwise; Esc clears it and returns to the page that was open.
- **Reset:** per row; "Reset page"; "Reset all settings…" (confirmed) in Advanced. Resets never touch recent projects, window positions or keys.
- **Import and export** in Advanced: "Export settings…" writes App rows only (no machine values, keys, recent projects or window state) as JSON with the schema version; "Import settings…" validates every key, applies the valid ones and reports what it skipped. Also "Open settings folder" and "Open logs folder".
- **Deep links:** `openSettings(page, key?)` opens the dialog at a row (for example from the title bar's save-status tooltip to Saving and backups). The command palette (WP-2H.04) lists pages and rows through it.
- **Pages in this WP:**
  - General: on startup (open the last project or start with an empty project; the welcome screen option arrives with WP-3I.02); default folder for new projects (used by File > New project…); recent projects to list, and "Clear recent projects"; "Reset 'Don't ask again' choices" (the mechanism dialogs use to remember a choice).
  - Appearance: theme Dark / Light / Match system (`nativeTheme`, follows OS changes live).
  - Saving and backups: WP-1M.10's rows on the store.
  - Advanced: as above.
- **Placement:** File > Settings… (Ctrl+,) on Windows and Linux; Cutweave > Settings… (⌘,) in the macOS app menu (already wired); one dialog at a time.
- **Proposed arch paragraph** (§16 UI architecture, with a pointer from §17; for the integrator to place): "**Settings (WP-1M.11).** Settings have three homes. *App preferences* are the person's choices for every project (theme, startup, saving, editing defaults, shortcuts, agents' folders, AI routing); *this computer's settings* belong to the installation (cache folder and limits, hardware, audio devices). Both live in `preferences.json` in the app's user-data folder, owned by Electron main, which validates every write against one versioned schema shared with the editor and broadcasts changes; export and import carry app preferences only. *Project settings* live in the document (`project.settings`) and change only through undoable commands, so agents read and change them like any edit. Defaults for new projects are preferences that `project.new` copies into the document; after that the project's value rules. A preference that changes engine behaviour is applied by the app to its own engine, at spawn as a flag or after each handshake through an engine command in a UI-only scope (ADR-0016); headless engines take flags, environment variables and project settings instead. Agents read the effective values (`project.info`, `media.cache_status`) but never change preferences. No secret is stored in preferences: keys go to the OS keychain through write-only `ai.set_key` (§13). The catalog of every setting is `docs/reference/settings.md`."
acceptance: Unit (main): a damaged file, an unknown key, a wrong type and an out-of-range value each start with defaults for that key and a warning; writes are atomic (a kill between temp write and rename leaves the old file); a v0 fixture migrates.
Unit (IPC): unknown keys, wrong types and calls from another frame are rejected; export never contains `machine` values, recent projects or window state; import skips invalid keys and reports them.
The registry test: every registered key has a row in `docs/reference/settings.md`.

**A user flow (ADR-0018, F19):** open Settings with Ctrl+, and from File; type "auto" and the Saving and backups rows show; change the theme to Light and "On startup" to open the last project; reset the startup row and see its default; export to a file (OS save picker stubbed); Reset all; import the file: the theme comes back; relaunch: the values persist and the window opens in the chosen theme.
F16 keeps passing on the store; a profile holding only the old `localStorage` theme keeps that theme after the update.
axe: 0 violations; visual baselines of the dialog (General page, a search result, the empty search) in dark and light.
work_packages.tests: unit (store, migration, IPC), Vitest (registry, search, reset, dialog), visual, user flow.
work_packages.out_of_scope: project settings (WP-2H.08); the pages listed in the catalog for other WPs; settings sync between machines; per-workspace preferences.

work_packages.title: Find media in the bin: search, filters, sort
work_packages.area: `crates/cutweave-ops` (`media.list` filter and sort), generated schema and TS types, `packages/editor` (media panel), `packages/ui` (`SearchField`; spec in `design/components/`), `apps/desktop/e2e/flows`, `docs/user-flows.md`
work_packages.scope:
(product owner request, 2026-11-24) a fast way to find media by name, kind, length and use, the same way for people and agents. Tags, notes, ratings and saved searches stay in WP-2F.06; the folder scope arrives with WP-2F.08.
- **One filter, two implementations, one fixture.** `MediaFilter{text?, kinds?, min_duration?, max_duration?, used?, problems?}` and `MediaSort{by: imported|name|duration|kind, order: asc|desc}`.
  - `text`: every whitespace-separated term must occur in the asset's name (the file name until assets can be renamed, WP-2F.07), ignoring case and accents.
  - `used`: placed on a timeline of any sequence (or not).
  - `problems`: assets nothing can be read from (no streams; offline media joins with WP-2F.03). Analysis failures are events, not document state (arch §7), so they stay a badge, not a filter.
  - Durations are flicks; stills have none and match only when no duration bound is set. "Imported" order is ID order (UUIDv7 IDs are time-ordered).
  - The engine's `media.list` (a core MCP tool, so no new tool and no tool-list growth) gains optional `filter` and `sort`; paging keeps `cursor` = the last asset's ID, read in the requested order.
  - The editor filters its document mirror with the TS predicate, with no round trip per keystroke. A fixture file of documents, filters and expected IDs, generated by a Rust test, is checked by both implementations (as the timecode parser's fixtures are).
- **Search field** at the top of the Media tab ("Search media", a clear button): Esc clears, a second Esc leaves the field; ↓ moves to the first result; Ctrl/Cmd+F focuses it while the Assets panel has focus (rebindable with WP-2H.05).
- **Filters** button with a count badge, opening a popover: Kind (Video, Audio, Image), Duration (any, under 10 s, 10 s–1 min, 1–5 min, over 5 min), Use (any, on the timeline, not used), and "Only media with problems". Active filters show as removable chips under the field, with "Clear all".
- **Sort** menu: date imported (newest first, the default, or oldest first), name, duration, kind. Sort and filters persist with the panel's view state; the search text is kept for the session and cleared when another project opens.
- **Results** use the existing grid and list with "12 of 340" in the toolbar; arrow keys, Enter-to-insert and dragging to the timeline work on the results; a selected asset the filter hides stays selected.
- **Empty states:** no media yet (unchanged); "No media matches "x"" with "Clear search"; with filters on, "Clear filters" too.
work_packages.interfaces: `media.list{limit?, cursor?, filter?, sort?}` (additive, backward compatible); `MediaFilter`, `MediaSort`; `<SearchField>` in `packages/ui` (WP-1M.11 reuses it).
acceptance: The Rust and TS predicates agree on the shared fixture (at least 40 cases: accents, several terms, stills with duration bounds, used and unused across two sequences, every sort, paging under each sort).
Filtering 10,000 assets in the editor takes < 8 ms p95 per keystroke (Vitest bench); `media.list` with a filter over 10,000 assets < 20 ms p95 (Rust bench).
MCP: `media_list` with `filter.text` returns the IDs the bin shows for the same text (scripted client on the fixture).

**A user flow (ADR-0018, F21):** import the demo media; type part of a name: only matching cards remain and the count says so; add Kind = Audio, then Not used after placing one clip; sort by name; a search with no match shows the empty state and "Clear search" brings everything back; ↓ and Enter insert a result at the playhead.
axe: 0 violations; visual baselines of the toolbar with chips in dark and light.
work_packages.tests: Rust unit and fixture generation, Vitest (predicate, fixture, panel), benches, user flow.
work_packages.out_of_scope: tags, notes, ratings, saved searches and smart collections (WP-2F.06); the folder scope (WP-2F.08); transcript text (P3) and content search (P5); offline status (WP-2F.03).

work_packages.title: See media before placing it: hover-scrub on bin cards and a scrubbable picture in the Inspector
work_packages.area: `packages/editor` (media cards, the Inspector's media section, the Media and import settings row), `packages/ui` (a scrub-bar component if `design/components/` has none; spec added there), `packages/preferences` and `docs/reference/settings.md` (`media.hover_scrub`), `apps/desktop/e2e/flows`, `docs/user-flows.md`
work_packages.scope:
(product owner request, 2026-11-24: "We need both the asset item to be playable + preview inside inspector") the picture half, with no engine change: frames come from `/media/{id}/thumb?t=&w=` (WP-1I.03), which floors `t` to the media's frame grid and caches. Playing with sound is WP-1M.15.
- **Hover-scrub on bin cards:** moving the pointer across a video card shows the frame at that fraction of its duration, with a position line and the time; leaving restores the poster. Requests are latest-wins (a request in flight is aborted when a newer one starts), at most one per animation frame, at the card's width. Audio cards show a position line over their waveform. Settings > Media and import can turn it off (`media.hover_scrub`, on).
- **Inspector preview:** when a bin asset is selected, the Inspector's media section starts with a picture of the asset (its aspect, the panel's width) above the probe facts, and a scrub bar under it: click or drag to see any frame; ←/→ step one frame at the asset's rate and Home/End go to the ends while the bar has the focus; the time shows as timecode at the asset's rate. Audio-only assets show their waveform with the same bar.
- **Keyboard and screen readers:** the scrub bar is a slider (`aria-valuetext` in timecode); hover-scrub on cards is pointer-only, and the Inspector gives the keyboard path.
work_packages.interfaces: a media scrub component over the `ThumbnailSource` seam; preference `media.hover_scrub`.

work_packages.title: Spec: timeline edit semantics
work_packages.scope:
write the normative spec that 2A.02–2A.08 implement. It must define, each with ASCII before/after diagrams and a table of edge cases:
- **Track and placement rules:**
  - No two items overlap on one track, on any track kind (§4.3). Overlays are additional video tracks. Dropping or moving an item where it would overlap **auto-creates a new track above** (default `new_track`).
  - The main track is the first video track with `magnetic: true`. Exactly one magnetic track per sequence, which may be changed.
  - Placement has three modes: `insert` (ripple the rest of the track; default on the main track), `overwrite` (trim or split what is underneath) and `new_track` (default for any overlap on a non-main track).
- **Magnetic track:** gap-free after every command. Deleting or trimming closes the gap. Moving an item out of it ripples the tail left. Defined behaviour for the first item (always starts at `0`) and for an empty track.
- **Ripple scope:** ripple affects the target track plus tracks that contain items linked to shifted items. Other tracks are untouched unless the command takes `ripple_all_tracks: true` (NLE behaviour).
- **Linked clips:** `linked_group` semantics for move, trim, split, delete, copy. This covers both video+audio of one source and CapCut "attached to main clip" (child follows parent's start; parent trim does not move children unless they now fall outside, then clamp).
- **Trim family:**
  - Trim: change one edge, moves `source_in` accordingly, clamped to media bounds.
  - Ripple trim: trim, then shift the downstream items.
  - Roll: move the cut between two adjacent items, total duration is constant.
  - Slip: change `source_in` only.
  - Slide: move an item between neighbours by changing neighbours' trims.
  - Each has clamping rules and what it returns when clamped.
- **Locks:** locked track rejects mutation with `Locked`. A ripple that would shift a locked track fails atomically; list the exact rule. Hidden/muted/solo are non-structural.
- **Frame alignment:** every edit point snaps to the sequence frame grid. Audio-only tracks use sample-accurate times rounded to the nearest frame unless `fine: true`.
- **Gesture soft-locks (§5.2):** which items a gesture locks (all items the command may touch, including ripple-shifted downstream items and linked members), and the `Conflict{reason:"item_in_gesture", retry_after_ms}` rule for other actors.
- **Replace clip:** attributes kept (transform, keyframes, effects, audio settings, links), duration/in-point policy (`keep_duration` trims or pads with a warning; `keep_source_in`), what happens to speed/freeze.
- **Atomicity:** every command is all-or-nothing and returns the list of items it moved, trimmed, split or removed (`EditReport`). Agents depend on this.
- **Snapping** (pure function, specified here, used by UI only): candidates are playhead, item edges, markers, beat markers. Threshold is 8 px converted to time. Priority order and tie-break rules.
- **Selection** semantics: multi-select, linked-group selection (selecting a linked group selects members; `alt` selects one member).
work_packages.interfaces: the spec defines the signatures of the commands implemented later: `timeline.insert`, `timeline.overwrite`, `item.move`, `timeline.lift`, `timeline.extract`, `timeline.ripple_delete`, `item.delete`, `item.duplicate`, `clip.trim`, `clip.ripple_trim`, `clip.roll`, `clip.slip`, `clip.slide`, `clip.split`, `clip.replace`, `item.link`/`item.unlink`, and the `EditReport` type.
acceptance: Document reviewed and approved by a human maintainer (PR approval).
≥ 40 scenario fixtures in `docs/spec/fixtures/` as JSON `{before, command, after_expected | error}`, covering every command × {magnetic, free track, locked track, linked group, clamp}.
Every command in the spec lists its invariants as numbered statements `INV-n` that tests cite by id.
Includes an explicit "NOT supported in P2" list (multicam, nested compound clips, track targeting UI).

work_packages.title: Timeline interaction state machine
work_packages.scope:
- A framework-free, explicit finite state machine (XState-style hand-rolled reducer, no renderer dependency) consuming normalized pointer/keyboard events and emitting `Intent`s (`begin_tx`, `command(name,args)`, `update_tx`, `commit_tx`, `cancel_tx`, `set_selection`, `set_cursor`).
- States: `idle, hover, selecting(marquee), moving, trimming, ripple_trimming, rolling, slipping, sliding, razor, scrubbing, keyframe_dragging, panning, zooming`.
- Tool modes (select, razor, ripple, slip/slide, hand).
- Esc cancels and rolls back the `gesture` tx. Modifier semantics: Shift = additive selection / constrain axis, Alt = single member of linked group / duplicate-on-drag, Ctrl/Cmd = disable snapping.
- Auto-scroll at edges; drag across tracks with `new_track` preview; drop-on-gap and drop-on-clip insert-vs-overwrite per spec.
- Edge cases: pointer leaves window, command rejected mid-drag (shows clamped state, no error spam), an agent command touching a gesture's items fails with `Conflict{item_in_gesture}` (§5.2, engine side in 2A.12); the machine never retries on its own. If the engine auto-cancels the gesture after 30 s idle, the machine receives `gesture.cancelled` and returns to `idle` with the doc rolled back. A drag update rejected because another actor's gesture holds an item shows a locked cursor and does not abort.
work_packages.interfaces: `createTimelineMachine(deps) → {send(event), state, subscribe}`; Intent types exported; state chart documented in `packages/timeline/README.md` with a mermaid diagram.
acceptance: Vitest transcript tests (≥ 60) replay recorded event streams and assert the Intent sequence and final doc via a fake engine that wraps the real `cutweave-ops` through WASM or a recorded-command stub.

Property test (fast-check): for random event streams, the machine never reaches an undefined state, never leaves a `gesture` tx open after `pointerup/cancel/blur`, and every `begin_tx` is paired with exactly one `commit_tx` or `cancel_tx`.
A drag emits `update` intents at most once per animation frame (coalesced).
100% of states/transitions in the doc diagram are covered (coverage check script).

work_packages.title: Soft-lock extension: retry semantics, UI feedback and auto-cancel
work_packages.scope:
- **Extends** the minimal soft-lock shipped in P1 (E1B; decision B) rather than introducing it: P2 adds the full touched-set computation, retry semantics and UI feedback. An open `gesture` tx registers a soft lock on the set of items its commands touch (including items shifted by ripple and linked members, as defined in 2A.01). Another actor's command that touches a locked item fails fast, before any mutation, with `Conflict{reason:"item_in_gesture", holder, retry_after_ms}`. Commands on other items proceed.
- The holder's own later updates may extend the lock set. Commit and cancel release it. Undo of a gesture inverts only its own ops (valid because the locks guarantee disjointness).
- Auto-cancel applies to `gesture`-kind txs only: after 30 s without updates (timer on the doc actor, injectable clock for tests) it rolls back, releases locks, emits `gesture.cancelled{reason:"idle_timeout"}`. `proposal`-kind txs have no idle timeout and are cancellable explicitly; they soft-lock their touched items by the same rule.
- Retry semantics: `Conflict` carries `retry_after_ms` (hint from the holder's remaining idle budget; none for proposals) and the holder; MCP clients may retry after the hint, the UI never retries on its own. UI feedback: locked items show a non-blocking "in use by <actor>" indicator and a toast with the machine code.
- Saves persist only the last committed rev (an open gesture/proposal tx is never written to disk).
- A tx is owned by its connection: a dropped connection or engine restart rolls back that connection's open txs (gesture and proposal) and releases their locks.
- Same-actor commands are never blocked. MCP error text includes a retry hint. All error carries the machine code.
acceptance: Property test (proptest, interleaved actors A/B, random commands, random gesture begin/commit/cancel): history stays linear; B never mutates a locked item while A's gesture is open; commands on disjoint items always succeed; after A cancels, doc equals the state as if the gesture never happened plus B's disjoint edits; undo identity holds.
Fake-clock test: gesture idle for 30 s is cancelled and the doc is rolled back; activity every 29 s keeps it alive.
Rejected commands do not change the doc or the rev (byte-identical snapshot).
Lock check adds < 20 µs per command on a 5,000-item doc (criterion).
Parity test: identical error over RPC, MCP and CLI.

work_packages.title: Spec: keyframe and easing model
work_packages.scope:
define precisely, extending §4.2 `Animatable<T>`:
- **Time domain:** keyframe `t` is item-relative timeline time in flicks (not source time), so speed changes do not move keyframes. Behaviour on trim: keyframes outside the new range are kept (not deleted) unless a `prune` flag is set; behaviour on split (boundary value inserted into both halves so that both halves evaluate identically); on ripple (no change); on duplicate; on speed change (unchanged); on slip (unchanged, since it is item-relative).
- **Interpolation:** `hold | linear | bezier{x1,y1,x2,y2} | spring{stiffness,damping,mass}`; interpolation belongs to the segment *starting* at a keyframe. Easing presets (ease-in/out, in-out, back, expo, bounce, elastic) are named bezier or analytic curves stored as `bezier` or `spring` after expansion, with a `preset` hint. Out-of-range handles for bezier are allowed (overshoot) with x clamped to [0,1].
- **Value types and combine rules:** scalar, vec2 (per-component interpolation, linked handles optional), color (interpolated in linear light, premultiplied), angle (shortest-path off by default, accumulate for rotation), enum/bool (hold only).
- **Evaluation contract:** `eval(animatable, t) → T` pure and deterministic, sample-exact at keyframes, clamped before first and after last, uses f64 internally.
- **Animatable property registry:** the complete list for P2: position, scale (x,y linked option), rotation, anchor, crop (4 edges), opacity, flip (hold), volume, pan, and effect/composition params later.
- **Auto-key semantics** for `item.set_props` (when a property is already animated, a set at the playhead creates/updates a keyframe; otherwise sets the static value) and an explicit `keyframe.*` API.
acceptance: Human review approval. Test vectors file `docs/spec/keyframes-vectors.json` with ≥ 50 `(animatable, t, expected)` rows including overshoot, hold, and spring.
Every property in the registry names a type and its unit/range.

work_packages.title: Interpolation core
work_packages.scope:
- Implement `Animatable<T>` `eval`, a cubic-bezier solver (Newton with bisection fallback, error < 1e-6), analytic spring (critically/under/over-damped closed form), colour interpolation in linear light, a per-segment cache for monotonic playback queries (`Evaluator` with cursor) and batch evaluation `eval_range(t0,t1,n)` for curve drawing and the UI.
- Property types per the registry; `Animatable::sample_times()` for UI lane drawing; JSON schema derive.
- Stays free of non-wasm-safe dependencies so that 2C.06 can compile it into the shared wasm module (§16). The UI evaluates curves locally through that module; no per-frame RPC.

Bench: evaluating 10 animated props × 3 layers at one `t` < 20 µs; 50k keyframes lookup (binary search) < 1 µs.
`cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p cutweave-model` passes.

work_packages.title: Shared wasm module: keyframe, easing, time and snapping math
work_packages.area: crates/cutweave-wasm/ (new thin crate, wasm-bindgen), packages/protocol/wasm/, CI
work_packages.scope:
- A thin crate `cutweave-wasm` re-exporting from the wasm-safe crates: flicks/frame/timecode conversions (`frame_to_time`, `time_to_frame`, `snap_to_frame`, timecode parse/format), `Animatable` evaluation and easing (including bezier/spring sampling and `eval_range`), and the snapping API (2A.07 adds its exports). No new logic in this crate.
- Build with `wasm-pack`/`wasm-bindgen` (target `web`, `--release`, `wasm-opt`), size budget ≤ 150 KB gzipped (CI check). Published inside `packages/protocol` as `@cutweave/protocol/wasm` with generated TS typings, an async `initMath()` loader (also usable in Vitest/Node) and a synchronous API after init. Float/time marshalling uses i64 as BigInt only at the boundary with typed wrappers, bulk evaluation takes `Float64Array` to avoid per-call overhead.

work_packages.title: Layouts for several clips: side by side, top and bottom, picture in picture, grids
work_packages.area: crates/cutweave-ops/src/item/ (`item.apply_layout`, the layout table as data), generated schema and TS types, packages/editor (a Layout menu in the Inspector, the timeline's clip menu and the bin), apps/desktop/e2e/flows, docs/user-flows.md
work_packages.scope:
(product owner request, 2026-11-24: "if I want to place 2 videos side by side on the timeline, will it be possible?") Today this is possible by hand. A second clip dropped at the same time goes to a new track, then Scale 50 % and Position X ±480 in the Inspector. The clips are letterboxed, though, because P1 has no crop. Crop arrives with WP-2C.03, WP-2C.04 and WP-2H.03, and transform handles and snapping with WP-2H.06. This WP makes the arrangement one action.
- **`item.apply_layout{items[], layout, fill: crop|fit, gap?, order?}`** sets each item's transform and crop as ordinary `VisualProps` values in one undoable step. MCP catalog: agents arrange clips with the same command the UI uses, and the result is plain properties that anyone can adjust afterwards.
  - `crop` fills each cell with a centred crop; `fit` scales to fit inside the cell.
  - `gap` is a spacing in sequence pixels.
  - `order` lists the items for the cells; without it, the top track comes first.
  - A property that is already animated gets a keyframe at the playhead (2C.03's auto-key rule).
  - The cells come from the sequence's canvas size (WP-2B.01).
- **Layouts** (data, so packs can add more later):
  - two clips: side by side (left and right), top and bottom;
  - picture in picture: a small clip in any corner, 30 % of the width, inset by the title-safe margin;
  - three clips: three columns, one large and two small;
  - four clips: a 2 × 2 grid.
  - Too few or too many visual items give `Invalid`, with the counts the layout accepts.
- **UI:**
  - With 2–4 video clips selected, the Inspector shows a Layout row of small diagrams, and the timeline's clip menu has Layout ▸.
  - In the bin, selecting 2–4 video assets offers "Place side by side…", which inserts them at the playhead on new tracks and applies the layout in one undo step.
  - "Swap" reverses the order of a two-clip layout.

Parity: `item.apply_layout` through the CLI, MCP and RPC gives byte-identical documents (`--deterministic-ids`).
Golden frame: two colour-bar clips side by side with `crop` render each half filled, with no letterbox.

**A user flow (ADR-0018, F36):** select two clips in the bin, "Place side by side…": both are on the timeline at the playhead on two tracks, and the preview frame shows the two pictures filling the left and right halves; Swap reverses them; Ctrl+Z undoes the layout, then the insert; select both clips, choose Picture in picture in the Inspector: the second clip sits small in a corner.

work_packages.title: Speed model, reverse, freeze frame, source time mapping
work_packages.scope:
- Use `Speed::Constant(r)`, r in [0.1, 100], rational stored as `{num,den}` (not f64) to keep frame math exact; `reverse: bool`; `freeze: Option<{at_source}>`.
- Commands: `clip.set_speed{item, speed, keep: duration|in_point, ripple}`, `clip.reverse`, `clip.freeze_frame{item, at}` (splits the item and inserts a still-duration clip of the freeze frame per CapCut behaviour, default 3 s duration: configurable setting `freeze.default_duration`), `clip.reset_speed`.
- Source-time mapping function `source_time(item, t)` is the single canonical mapping used by render, audio, thumbnails and export. Frame-nearest sampling in v1 (no blending; blending arrives P4). Reverse requires decoder support for backwards GOP traversal: use GOP-cache decode-forward then reorder; for sources without proxy and long GOP a warning plus automatic proxy request (2F.01).
- Speed change on a magnetic track ripples; on a free track it keeps start and may be blocked by a neighbour (`Conflict`, with option `ripple`).
- MCP core: none (catalog `clip_set_speed`, `clip_freeze_frame`); note in the MCP map (2I.01).
acceptance: Unit test: 2× over a 10 s clip gives duration 5 s exactly in flicks; 1/3× is exact (rational), no drift over 1,000 round trips (`set_speed(a)` then `set_speed(1/a)` restores duration±0).
Frame-exact: preview/export at speed 0.5 shows source frame `floor(t*0.5*fps)` verified on the corpus clip with burned-in frame counter (golden OCR-free check via pixel-coded frame numbers).
Reverse playback of a 1080p H.264 long-GOP clip scrubs at p95 < 150 ms (§19) with proxy, and works (slower, documented) without.
Freeze frame creates exactly two splits + one still and keeps the track gapless on magnetic.
Undo identity and magnetic-gapless property tests extended with speed commands.
work_packages.tests: unit, proptest, golden frames, e2e via CLI.

work_packages.title: Audio for speed and reverse (pitch-preserving)
work_packages.scope:
- Time-stretch node using `signalsmith-stretch` for 0.1×–100× (above 4× or below 0.25× quality degrades; clamp the audio-preserve path to 0.25×–4×, and outside the range switch to resample (pitch-changing) with a flag in the report).
- `Clip.audio.preserve_pitch: bool` (default true). Reverse audio via block reversal with crossfaded joins (5 ms).
- Stretch runs on worker threads ahead of the real-time thread into ring buffers (§9) and survives seeks with < 50 ms re-prime. Mixer uses the same `source_time` as video.
- Offline render path (export) uses the same node deterministically (fixed block size).
acceptance: Test tone 440 Hz at 2× with preserve-pitch: measured fundamental 440 Hz ± 2 Hz (FFT test); without: 880 Hz ± 4.
A/V offset at 0.5× and 2× after 60 s: < 40 ms and drift < 1 frame / 30 min equivalent (the 2J.03 sync probe; this WP asserts offset < 20 ms in an offline test).
0 underruns at 256-sample buffer with 8 tracks all at 1.5× (audio soak 120 s).
Reverse of a 1 s sine yields the same energy (RMS ± 0.1 dB) and no clicks (max sample discontinuity < 0.05 at joins).
work_packages.tests: FFT unit tests, offline render comparison, soak.

work_packages.title: Fades, keyframed volume, pan
work_packages.scope:

- Commands: `audio.set_fade{item, in?, out?, curve?}`, `audio.set_volume{item, db, auto_key?}` / `audio.set_pan` (thin wrappers over `item.set_props`; same data), `audio.set_gain`. Fades clamp so that `fade_in + fade_out ≤ duration`.

No clicks: for a keyframed volume jump between adjacent keyframes (hold), max sample discontinuity after smoothing < 0.02.

work_packages.title: Auto-ducking (sidechain from voice tracks)
work_packages.scope:
- Sidechain ducker on a track bus: `audio.set_ducking{track, enabled, sources: [track_ids], threshold_db (-35), reduction_db (-12), attack_ms (50), release_ms (400), hold_ms (100), lookahead_ms (10)}`. The detector is a smoothed RMS/peak follower on the summed source tracks (post-fade, post-gain). Gain reduction is applied as a smooth dB ramp on the target bus (music/B-roll audio).
- Deterministic in preview and export (fixed block size, lookahead via delay compensation; no wall-clock). Runs on the audio thread with no allocation. The ducking curve is also computable offline for the timeline: `audio.get_duck_curve{track, from, to}` returns breakpoints so the UI can draw the gain-reduction shading on the music track.
- "Duck under voice" one-click: `audio.auto_duck{track}` picks sources as all tracks flagged `role=voice` (new `Track.role: voice|music|sfx|none`, settable via `track.set_role`, schema bump if not yet in 2A.02) and applies defaults.

- UI: ducking section on the track in the mixer (enable, sources, amount, attack/release) with live gain-reduction meter.
- MCP: `audio_set` gains a `ducking` variant (core), `audio.auto_duck` catalog.

work_packages.title: Proxy generation pipeline and policy
work_packages.scope:
- Proxy job: transcode to an intra-frame codec at ≤ 960 px on the long edge (ProRes Proxy via `prores_ks`/videotoolbox where present, DNxHR LB fallback, MJPEG last), audio copied to PCM. Keeps frame count and timestamps identical to the source (VFR sources are conformed through the media index to CFR with a stored `pts_map` so that proxy frame *n* equals source frame *n*, essential for frame-exact edits).
- Content-addressed in the global cache (`cache.sqlite` entry keyed by `content_hash + proxy_profile`), size-capped LRU, resumable job (partial files finalized atomically), progress events, cancel, concurrency limit (default 2; ≤ 1 while exporting), CPU/GPU niceness.
- Policy in `project.settings.proxy_policy`: `off | auto | all`. `auto` triggers on import for long-GOP codecs (H.264/HEVC) with long edge > 1920 px or fps > 60 or HEVC 10-bit (documented). Per-media `media.set_proxy_mode{auto|force|off}`.
- Commands: `media.generate_proxy{media[]}`, `media.delete_proxy`, `media.set_proxy_policy`, `media.proxy_status` query. Jobs resumed after engine restart.
- MCP: catalog; `media_import` reports `proxy: queued|none`.
acceptance: For the corpus 4K HEVC 10-min clip, proxy generation ≥ 1× realtime on the reference desktop; resumes after kill -9 and completes (test).
Frame mapping: for 500 random frame indices on VFR phone footage, the proxy decodes the same frame index as the source (verified by embedded frame-number burn-in clip): 100% match.
Cache cap respected: with a cap of 1 GB and 3 × 600 MB proxies, the least recently used one is evicted and its `ProxyRef` reports `evicted` (reverts to original).
Scrub p95 on proxy < 80 ms, on 4K long-GOP original with proxy off < 150 ms (§19; measured in 2J.03).
work_packages.tests: integration with corpus, kill/resume, cache eviction unit.
work_packages.out_of_scope: UI beyond a status query (2F.03), preview switching logic (2F.02).

- Setting `preview.use_proxies` (default on) toggle in the transport bar. The preview status chip shows "Proxy" or "Original".
- Missing/evicted proxy gracefully falls back to the original.

Hash is computed lazily with a fast partial hash (first/last/middle 1 MB + size) and full hash only on ambiguity. Path rewrite preserves `path_rel` when under the project folder.
- UI: a relink dialog on open ("N files missing"), per-asset badges in the bin, proxy status badges, and "Regenerate proxies" in the bin's context menu.

The machine values are applied through UI-only engine commands as in WP-1D.08; the project's own policy is edited in File > Project settings… (WP-2H.08).

work_packages.title: Collect and archive
work_packages.scope:
- `project.collect{dest, mode: copy_all|copy_external_only, include_generated, include_proxies, trim_unused: bool}` job. Copies referenced media into `<project>/media/` (or archive destination), rewrites `path_abs/path_rel` in the project doc copy, dedupes by content hash, preserves relative folder names with collision handling, verifies by hash after copy, reports progress, cancellable and resumable.
- `project.archive{dest, format: zip|folder}` bundles `.cutweave`, media, `generated/`, fonts/LUTs, and a manifest `archive.json` (hash list). Zip64 for > 4 GB; no recompression for media (stored). Excludes caches by default.
