work_packages.title: Background export queue, range and marker-set export
work_packages.scope:
- Persistent export queue (sqlite via cutweave-jobs): `export.enqueue{sequence, preset, range, output, overrides}` snapshots the sequence at enqueue time (immutable snapshot reference at the current `rev`, so later edits do not alter queued jobs) and runs jobs serially by default (parallel limit setting, default 1 for GPU exports). Jobs survive engine restart (interrupted job restarts from the beginning, with partial output cleaned; documented).
- Operations: `export.start` (enqueue + start), `export.cancel`, `export.pause_queue`, `export.reorder`, `export.retry`, `export.remove`, queries `export.queue`, `job_status` (common). Progress: percent, fps, ETA, current frame, bytes. Events `job.progress`.
- Export doesn't block editing; the preview may degrade (GPU budget `jobs` rule: preview priority above export, with a documented throttle). Offline media rules from 2F.03.
- Range export: `range = {kind: sequence | in_out | custom{start,end} | markers{ids[]|all, pair_mode}}`: a marker-set range export renders one file per marker region (marker `duration` or pairs of consecutive markers, naming template `{seq}_{marker_label}_{n}`).
- Output file collision policy (`rename|overwrite|fail`), disk space precheck.
- MCP core: `export_start`, `job_status`; queue management catalog.
acceptance: Enqueue 3 jobs, kill the engine during job 2 and restart: job 1 `done`, job 2 restarts and completes, job 3 completes; outputs valid (ffprobe).
Editing the timeline during an export does not change the exported output (frame hash vs. snapshot render).
Marker-set export of 4 markers produces 4 files with the right durations (±1 frame).
Cancel mid-export leaves no partial file and the queue proceeds.
Editing UI command RTT p95 stays < 16 ms during an export (measured in 2J.01 harness).
work_packages.tests: integration with the kill harness, unit for the state machine.

(product owner request, 2026-11-24: "History panel") a dockable panel listing the project's undo history as ADR-0019 defines it: the editor's Undo and Redo cover every actor and name who made each step.
- **Rows** come from `edit.history` (paged with `cursor`, virtualized) and follow `edit.history_changed`.
  - One row per change (cause `edit` or `restore`), oldest at the top, with a marker under the current state. Undone changes that can still be redone sit below the marker, dimmed.

work_packages.title: Checkpoints: edit.checkpoint / edit.restore
work_packages.scope:
- `edit.checkpoint{name?, note?} → {checkpoint, rev}` stores an `Arc` snapshot handle plus metadata (rev, actor, time) in an in-memory registry capped at 50 (LRU, named ones pinned up to 20); persisted in the journal as a marker event so restore works after crash recovery (the snapshot is re-derived by replaying to that rev if the in-memory handle is gone, bounded by journal retention; if unavailable, `NotFound` with a clear message).
- `edit.restore{checkpoint}`: applies a **forward** transaction computing the inverse diff to bring the doc to the checkpoint state (so history stays linear and the restore itself is undoable; it doesn't truncate history), tagged with the caller's actor. Refuses when it would revert another actor's edits unless `force: true` (default policy: restore reverts all edits since the checkpoint; report lists actors affected).
- `edit.list_checkpoints`, `edit.delete_checkpoint`. Checkpoints are not auto-created except `cutweave_execute{checkpoint:true}` (1 per call) used by MCP's destructive batch path.
- MCP core: `edit_checkpoint`, `edit_restore`; `edit_list_checkpoints` catalog. *As built (2026-11-25):* while the P1 MCP gate is full (R33), all four checkpoint commands stay in the catalog, reached through `cutweave_execute`, `cutweave_query` and `cutweave_search_commands`; WP-2I.01 lists `edit_checkpoint` and `edit_restore` as core.

work_packages.title: Background render cache (smart pre-render while idle)
work_packages.scope:
- **Segment detection:** analyze the active sequence into time segments and estimate render cost from the scene graph (layer count, compound nesting, effects, blends, speed/reverse on long-GOP sources) using per-node cost estimates calibrated from measured GPU/CPU time (recorded by the playback path). A segment is "heavy" when its estimated frame time exceeds 70% of the frame budget at the current preview quality, or when playback measured dropped frames over it.
- **Cache:** render heavy segments to an intra-frame cache file (reusing the proxy encoder profile) keyed by (subgraph hash, range, preview resolution) per §8 "cache by (subgraph hash, t)"; stored in the global cache dir under the LRU cap (default 20 GB, configurable) with entries in `cache.sqlite`. Granularity: fixed 2 s chunks aligned to the frame grid so small edits invalidate only affected chunks.
- **Scheduling:** a job that runs only when idle (no playback, no gesture, no export; resume ≥ 1.5 s after the last edit), single concurrent, cancelled instantly on edit/playback start, lower priority than export and proxies, nearest-to-playhead segments first; battery/thermal aware pause option.
- **Playback use:** the preview resolver substitutes cached chunks when the hash matches and quality ≤ cached resolution; falls back to live render otherwise. Pure optimization: results must equal live rendering (cached chunk vs live render at the same quality on the same adapter: bit-identical). Export does not use the cache in P2 (always live, for determinism).
- Commands: `render.cache_enable{bool}`, `render.cache_clear`, `render.cache_status` query `{segments:[{from,to,state: none|queued|rendering|ready|stale}], bytes}`; project setting `render_cache.enabled` default on.
- UI: ruler bar under the timeline ruler (grey none, orange queued/rendering, green ready).
- Settings (catalog `docs/reference/settings.md`): background renders limit (20 GiB) with usage and Clear on Settings > Cache and storage; "Start background rendering after" (1.5 s idle) and "Pause background work on battery" (on) on Settings > Performance and hardware, all machine values applied through UI-only engine commands (WP-1D.08's pattern); `render_cache.enabled` in File > Project settings… (WP-2H.08).
- MCP: catalog.
work_packages.interfaces: commands above; event `render.cache_progress`; `MediaResolver` extension for cached segments.
acceptance: On a fixture sequence with a 10 s heavy segment (6 layers + 3-level compound, which drops frames live at 1080p60 on the iGPU reference), after the idle cache completes the segment plays with 0 dropped frames over 60 s of looped playback (2J.03 harness).
Editing a clip inside one chunk invalidates only chunks whose subgraph hash changed (assertion on chunk states); unaffected chunks stay ready.
Starting playback or an edit cancels the cache job in < 100 ms (probe) and editing command RTT stays p95 < 16 ms while the job runs.
Cached vs live bit-identical on 50 sample frames (same adapter); LRU cap enforced (cap 500 MB test).
Export output frame hashes are identical with the cache on and off.
work_packages.tests: integration, invalidation unit tests, bench via 2J.03 harness.
work_packages.out_of_scope: using the cache for export, distributed rendering, GPU-texture caches (already in-engine).

work_packages.title: Opt-in, self-hosted, privacy-preserving crash reporting (ships with Public Alpha)
work_packages.area: crates/cutweave-engine (crash handler), apps/desktop, packages/editor (consent UI), infra/crash-collector/, docs/privacy/crash-reporting.md
work_packages.scope:
- Moved earlier from P7 7B.01 so the Public Alpha builds produce the crash data that the 1.0 crash-free gate (≥ 99.5%) is measured on. P7 7B keeps analysis, triage and hardening.
- Engine and shell crash handlers (minidump via `crash-handler`/`minidumper` for Rust, Electron `crashReporter` for the shell) writing dumps locally; symbolication on the collector, never on the client. Reports contain: app/engine version, OS/arch, GPU adapter name, stack, anonymous random install id (rotatable), session length and a clean-exit flag (for crash-free-session stats). No media paths, project contents, file names, prompts, transcripts, API keys or IPs stored (collector drops source IP).
- Strictly opt-in: first-run prompt (3I.02) and Settings toggle, default off; per-report preview of what would be sent with "send / don't send / always"; one-click delete of the install id's reports.
- Self-hosted collector: a minimal open-source service (container + docs; Sentry-compatible-minidump or Crashpad-compatible endpoint) the project runs on its own infrastructure; no third-party SaaS; endpoint configurable so forks/enterprises can point elsewhere or disable at build time.
- Redaction test harness shared with 5A.03 (secrets never appear in dumps or logs).
- The switch lives on the Privacy page of Settings (WP-1M.11's frame), with a plain statement of what leaves this computer: crash reports when on, AI requests to the providers the person set up, update checks (catalog `docs/reference/settings.md`).
work_packages.interfaces: setting `privacy.crash_reports: off|ask|always`; `cutweave doctor --crash-preview`; collector HTTP API (documented).
acceptance: with the setting off, a forced crash sends zero network requests (test with a blocking proxy); with it on, a forced crash on each of Windows/macOS/Ubuntu yields a symbolicated report on the collector within 5 min; grep/redaction test finds no paths, usernames or key material in 20 sampled reports; clean-exit sessions are counted for crash-free-session stats; privacy doc reviewed by the maintainers.
work_packages.tests: forced-crash integration on 3 OSes, network-blocking test, redaction test, collector container smoke.
work_packages.out_of_scope: crash triage dashboards and hardening work (P7 7B), usage analytics, automatic bug filing.

work_packages.title: `effect.toml` specification, schema & parser
work_packages.scope: normative spec + JSON Schema + parser. `kind = effect|transition|generator|blend`; params `float|int|bool|color|vec2|enum|curve|gradient|image|angle|point` with `min/max/default/step/unit/group/ui/keyframeable/preview_only`; inputs `source`, `secondary` (transitions: `from`,`to` + auto `progress`), `mask`, **`history = N`** (≤ 8 previous frames of the same clip via the frame cache — the deterministic replacement for persistent feedback buffers); passes `{shader, reads, writes, scale, format, iterations}`; built-ins `time, resolution, frame, fps, progress, seed`; `color_space = linear|display`, `alpha = premult|straight`; `budget{tier}`; `data_input` hook (used by stabilisation/tracking); metadata (category, tags, thumbnail, i18n name keys). Includes three reference effects in the spec (separable blur, RGB split, cross-dissolve) that must compile in CI.
acceptance: schema snapshot; parser rejects ≥ 25 malformed manifests with path-accurate diagnostics (file:line); round-trip parse→serialise→parse identical; spec examples compiled in CI; spec reviewed by a human maintainer (recorded in PR).
work_packages.out_of_scope: shader compilation (4A.02), WASM effect metadata worlds.

work_packages.title: WGSL loader, validator & host prelude
work_packages.scope: naga parse + validate at install and load; reject `enable` extensions, push constants, undeclared bindings, unbounded loops (only const-bounded `for`, ≤ 64 iterations), instruction/size caps, texture format/size whitelist, passes ≤ 8; **host-generated prelude** (uniform struct from params, bind groups: 0 uniforms, 1 textures+samplers, 2 LUT/aux) so authors write only `fn fx_main(uv, ctx) -> vec4<f32>`; diagnostics mapped back to author line/col (prelude offset removed); pipeline cache keyed by hash(source, layout).
work_packages.interfaces: `compile(manifest, sources) -> CompiledEffect | Vec<Diagnostic>`; CLI `cutweave effect check <dir>`.
acceptance: corpus of 30 hostile/invalid shaders (infinite loop, OOB indexing, forbidden extensions, huge arrays, recursion, undeclared bindings) all rejected within 50 ms each; 10 valid shaders pass; diagnostics point to the right line in 100% of corpus cases; second load hits the pipeline cache (< 5 ms).
work_packages.tests: corpus tests, fuzz-lite on WGSL mutations (no panics), unit.

work_packages.title: Render-graph integration: effect instances, multi-pass, temporal taps
work_packages.scope: `EffectInstance` evaluation at `t` (params `Animatable` → uniform ring buffer); pass allocation from a texture pool (scale/format); fusion of compatible single-pass pointwise effects into one pass; `history` taps served from the frame cache (deterministic; effect disabled gracefully if frames unavailable); effect order/enable; per-effect param-hash in render-graph cache keys; resolution-independent unit scaling for the quality ladder; effects on clips (adjustment layers in 4G.05, transitions in 4A.04).
work_packages.interfaces: `cutweave_render::effects::{EffectRuntime, EffectNode}`; `EffectRef` scene-graph nodes from P3's `SceneGraph` become real (removes the `effect.unavailable` stub).
acceptance: ½-res preview vs full export of resolution-independent effects ΔE00 mean ≤ 1.5; 10 stacked trivial effects fuse into ≤ 3 passes (test on graph); two runs bit-identical; seeking to a frame with `history` taps gives the same pixels as playing into it (determinism test); GF for the 3 reference effects.
work_packages.tests: golden, graph-shape unit tests, determinism, bench.

work_packages.title: Transitions engine
work_packages.scope: `Transition{a,b,kind,duration,alignment(center|start|end),params}` evaluation: render `from`/`to` to textures, run the transition pass with eased `progress`; **handles policy** when media beyond the cut is unavailable: `freeze|clamp` (shorten to available handle); single-clip in/out transitions (against transparent/black); max duration ≤ min(a,b) adjusted automatically; alpha-aware; speed-change aware; automatic audio crossfade (equal-power) with `audio: crossfade|none`.
acceptance: identity at ends for every shipped transition (harness check, bit-exact); transition across a 2× speed clip is visually continuous (A/B frame difference at cut boundary ≤ 1 frame step); audio crossfade energy constant (±1 dB) in test; GF for 3 reference transitions; no frame hitch when entering/leaving the transition region (render-graph rebuild < 2 ms).
work_packages.tests: golden, identity-at-ends, audio crossfade test, proptest on duration clamping.

work_packages.title: GPU budget enforcement, profiler & benchmark CLI
work_packages.scope: timestamp-query profiler per effect pass (fallback: fence timing), rolling p95; budget tiers from policy above; **auto-disable** after 30 consecutive frames > 2× budget with event `effect.disabled{id,reason}` and manual re-enable; `cutweave effect bench <id|--all> [--res 1080p|4k] [--json]` → `{p50,p95,tier,pass_count,taps}`; **static budget lint** (pass count × texture-tap count from naga analysis must fit tier) runs on hosted CI; nightly workflow on self-hosted iGPU runners (Intel Xe + Apple M1) compares measured p95 against declared tier and fails on regression.
work_packages.interfaces: events `effect.disabled`; CLI `cutweave effect bench`; `render.stats` query gains per-effect timings.
acceptance: a deliberately slow test effect (100 taps × 6 passes) is auto-disabled within 1.5 s of playback and the UI receives the event; static lint flags it in CI; bench output stable (p95 CV < 10% across 3 runs); nightly job produces a JSON artifact per runner.
work_packages.tests: unit, integration with synthetic slow effect, CI workflow dry-run.
work_packages.out_of_scope: per-effect optimisation work (owned by content WPs).

work_packages.title: Color pipeline specification & reference implementation

acceptance: reviewed by a human maintainer; reference implementation passes self-consistency (neutral params = identity within 1e-9; monotonicity for exposure/contrast); each GPU op in 4F.02–4F.04 states its ΔE00 tolerance vs reference (≤ 1.0 mean, ≤ 2.5 max on 10k sampled colours).
work_packages.tests: unit on reference; property tests (identity at defaults).

acceptance: GPU vs reference ΔE00 mean ≤ 1.0, max ≤ 2.5 on 10k colours per control at ±50/±100; neutral defaults bit-exact identity; ≤ 0.5 ms at 1080p iGPU; temperature slider monotonic in B/R ratio (property test); GF.

acceptance: a constant-speed curve is bit-identical to constant mode; source frames selected match the analytic integral (frame-exact test on 5 presets); no negative/zero speed ever (validation); duration equals ∫ within 1 flick-rounding frame; presets GF; undo/redo.

acceptance: synthetic shaky clip with known injected path: residual high-pass path RMS reduced ≥ 80%; real handheld fixture ≥ 60% (vs analysis output); `auto-scale` never shows borders (test); strength 0 is bit-exact identity; ≤ 0.8 ms at 1080p iGPU; GF.

work_packages.title: Point tracker (pyramidal Lucas-Kanade)

acceptance: synthetic planar warp ground truth: mean corner error ≤ 1.5 px (≤ 3 px for perspective at 30° tilt); survives 30% of points occluded; falls back to a lower-order model when degenerate and reports it; deterministic (seeded RANSAC).

work_packages.title: Key store and host HTTP layer
work_packages.scope:
- `KeyStore` over `keyring` (Credential Manager / Keychain / Secret Service), keyed by (provider, label). **Write-only API**: `ai.set_key{provider, key}` stores the key and returns only a fingerprint (last 4 characters) — the renderer discards the value; `has`, `delete`, `validate` (provider-specific cheap call). Adapters reference keys only by opaque **key handle**; no read API exists anywhere. Env override `CUTWEAVE_KEY_<PROVIDER>` for CLI/headless MCP. Headless Linux without a Secret Service: env-only plus a clear error (Notes §25). `secrecy` + `zeroize`; redaction layer on `tracing` and on every error `Display`.
- `HostHttp` (reqwest + rustls): injects auth per `AuthScheme` (header, bearer, query, basic, and `signed`: host-side `sign(alg, key_handle, payload)` for JWT/HMAC/SigV4 providers, returning only the signature), timeouts, jittered retries for idempotent status/list calls only, `Retry-After` parsing, response-size caps, redirect policy, **per-provider host allowlist** (API + CDN download hosts), blocks private/loopback IPs for user-supplied URLs (explicit allow only for the "local server" OpenAI-compatible profile), proxy support, cassette hook for 5A.04.
- Keys never reach project files, journal, command log, MCP results, UI stores or plugin memory.
- `ai.set_key` is a **UI-only scope**: the engine derives the actor server-side from the presented credential (UI token → `user`; agent token → `agent:<label>`; plugin → `plugin:<id>`; internal → `system`) and rejects `ai.set_key`, `ai.provider.remove_key` and key validation-with-new-key from any non-`user` actor. The other UI-only scopes (approval minting, roots allowlist, budget configuration, plugin permission grants) use the same mechanism; no client-supplied actor or origin tag is ever trusted.
acceptance: an agent token or plugin credential calling `ai.set_key` is rejected with `forbidden_scope` (test over RPC and MCP); sentinel-key test: a planted key is searched for in all tracing output, error strings, command log, journal and `Debug` dumps and never found; `sign` passes JWT (HS256/ES256), HMAC-SHA256 and SigV4 test vectors and raw key bytes are unobtainable through any API; SSRF tests (redirect to 127.0.0.1 / 169.254.169.254 rejected); `cargo-deny` clean.
work_packages.tests: unit, wiremock integration, fuzz target for header/URL handling.
work_packages.out_of_scope: key-entry UI (5F.07), OAuth flows, exposing `sign` to WASM (deferred to E6A).

work_packages.title: AI job manager (persistent, resumable, safe against double billing)
work_packages.depends_raw: 5A.02, E1B, **E1D (`cutweave-jobs` basic persistent queue — owned by Phase 1, not re-owned here)**
work_packages.scope:
- **Extend the E1D queue (do not fork it)** with an AI job kind. Add to its SQLite schema: client-generated UUIDv7 `id`, provider, model, capability, `params_hash`, state, `remote_id`, `cost_est`, `cost_actual`, attempts, error, project, actor, timestamps, outputs.
- State machine `Queued → Submitting → Running → Downloading → Succeeded | Failed | Cancelled | NeedsReview`. **Persist `Submitting` + an idempotency key before any network call.** On restart a `Submitting` job with no `remote_id` becomes `NeedsReview` (never auto-resubmit unless the provider supports an idempotency key). `Running` jobs resume polling.
- Poll with exponential backoff + jitter, manifest poll-interval hints and `Retry-After`; per-provider and global concurrency limits; local queueing on 429/`queue_full`; cancel (remote + local); retry only when `retryable` and safe; per-capability timeouts; resource-class hooks (`gpu|cpu|io`) for local jobs.
- Events `job.progress`, `job.finished`, `job.needs_review`.
work_packages.interfaces: `AiJobs::{enqueue, cancel, retry, list, get}`; events on the existing bus.
acceptance: kill -9 during `Running` resumes after restart; kill during `Submitting` yields `NeedsReview` and no second remote job; double submit of an identical request creates one remote job; MockProvider chaos test (failures, 429, slow polls, cancel races) stable over 1000 iterations.

work_packages.title: Cost estimator, pricing-formula evaluator and budget ledger
work_packages.depends_raw: 5A.02, 5A.05, 5A.01, 5B.01 (formula fields; may start against a stub schema)
work_packages.scope:
- `Money` (decimal + currency; USD only in v1, provider credits converted by catalog data), `CostEstimate{low, expected, high, basis, confidence(exact|estimate|range|unknown), as_of, stale}`; stale when `as_of` is older than a configurable age (default 30 days).
- Pricing-formula DSL: a tiny non-Turing-complete evaluator (`+ - * /`, `min max ceil`, `table[a][b]`, variables from params/inputs/outputs such as `duration`, `resolution`, `megapixels`, `chars`, `minutes`, `tokens_in/out`) with a step limit. No scripting engine, no `eval`.
- Budget ledger (SQLite): scopes **per-action agent budget and per-session agent budget (default $0, §13)**, per-project, daily, monthly, per-provider; soft warning vs hard stop; **reserve on submit**, reconcile with provider-reported usage (else the estimate, flagged), release on failure/cancel. App-level caps in app config; project-level caps in project settings (Notes §23).
- Unknown price → confidence `unknown` → always tier 3, human-approved (5A.08).
acceptance: property test: concurrent reservations never exceed any cap; evaluator fuzz (no panics, bounded time); golden estimates for 3 sample manifests (per-second video, per-megapixel image, per-character TTS).

work_packages.title: Spending authority: three-tier policy engine, approvals, consent, untrusted-content labelling
work_packages.area: crates/cutweave-ai (`policy`), crates/cutweave-api (credential-derived actor, UI-only scope enforcement, MCP result shapes), crates/cutweave-cli (`--budget`)
work_packages.scope:
implement §13 exactly, enforced by the engine (never the model):
- `PolicyEngine` classifies an invocation as read | reversible | destructive | **paid** | external | `requires_human` (publishing, deleting originals, voice cloning, uncurated models; also feeds the copilot, 6I).
- **Tier 1 — Auto:** cost below the user-set *per-action* budget **and** within the *per-session agent budget* (default **$0 ⇒ off**). Runs immediately; reserved in the ledger.
- **Tier 2 — Agent-confirmed:** a dry run (`ai.estimate`, `cutweave_execute dry_run`) returns `cost_estimate` + `confirm_token` (HMAC with a per-launch secret; bound to {command, canonical params hash, actor (derived server-side from the credential), project, max_cost, expiry 5 min, single use}). The token only proves the agent saw the price: redeeming **cannot exceed the remaining agent budget** (checked and reserved atomically at redeem).
- **Tier 3 — Human-approved:** anything above budget, with unknown price, or marked `requires_human` returns `approval_required{approval_id}` (≥ 128-bit random id, bound to params hash + cost, single use, expiring). **Only the desktop UI can mint the approval** (`ai.approval.grant|deny` is a UI-only scope: the actor is derived server-side from the credential, so only the UI token, actor `user`, may call it, via the Electron token handoff; agent tokens (`agent:<label>`) and plugins (`plugin:<id>`) are rejected; `mcp = hidden`). The agent polls `approval_status{approval_id}` → pending | approved | denied | expired.
- **Headless** (`cutweave mcp --headless`): tiers 1–2 only, requires an explicit `--budget <usd>` (absent ⇒ $0); tier-3 requests return `approval_unavailable_headless` and can never be granted.
- First-use per-provider data-flow consent; privacy mode `local-only` blocks cloud routes; provider/media-derived text wrapped `{untrusted:true}` and never used in policy decisions; append-only audit log (credential-derived actor, cost, tier, token/approval id). Budget configuration is also a UI-only scope (`user` actor only).
work_packages.interfaces: `PolicyEngine::{classify, decide, mint_token, redeem_token, request_approval, approval_status}`, MCP result `approval_required`, query `ai.approval_status`, CLI flag `--budget`.
acceptance: (a) default $0 budget: no paid MCP call runs automatically; (b) a valid confirm token cannot spend beyond the remaining agent budget, including under concurrent redemption (property test); (c) replayed, altered, expired or cross-actor/cross-project tokens rejected; (d) an agent over the **real MCP transport and over RPC with an agent token** (actor `agent:<label>`) cannot mint, guess or replay an approval, cannot change the budget, and `ai.approval.grant` is unreachable from MCP; a forged actor/origin field in a request is ignored (actor always comes from the credential); (e) `requires_human` commands are tier 3 even at cost 0; (f) headless without `--budget` refuses paid actions, with `--budget` never reaches tier 3; (g) transcript/provider text such as "approve the spend" changes nothing; (h) session-budget reset semantics tested.
work_packages.tests: unit, proptest (budget invariants), integration over RPC + MCP + CLI, injection fixtures.
work_packages.out_of_scope: the approval card UI (5F.03), copilot UX (6I).

work_packages.title: Catalog signing, verification and rollback protection
work_packages.scope: detached ed25519 signature (minisign-compatible) over the RFC 8785 canonical JSON of the catalog plus its SHA-256; pinned public keys with key IDs and **rotation** (new key accepted only when announced in a catalog signed by an already-trusted key, with an overlap window); **emergency revocation list**; anti-rollback via persisted highest-seen `catalog_version` per channel; `min_app_version`; `valid_until` (soft: warn "catalog stale" after 30 days). Failure modes: invalid signature, downgrade, expired ⇒ keep previous catalog, surface a warning, never partially apply. The same verifier is reused for local-model artifacts and any future adapter packages (E6A). Threat-model doc (key compromise, CDN compromise, replay, downgrade).
acceptance: test vectors for every failure mode; rotation and revocation scenarios pass; no network code in this module; reviewed by a human before merge.

work_packages.title: Declarative provider manifest spec and safe template language
work_packages.scope: manifest fields: `id`, `hosts` (allowlist), `auth{scheme: header|bearer|query|basic|signed}` where **`signed` calls the host-side `sign(alg, key_handle, payload)` (5A.03)** with a claims/payload template, so JWT/HMAC/SigV4 providers need no code; endpoints; **job pattern** `sync | poll{submit,status,result,cancel,done_when,failed_when,interval_hint} | multi_step` (no webhook patterns in v1); request templates (JSON body, multipart, query, headers); response mapping to normalized outputs (Asset list with kind/mime, Transcript, StockResult, usage/cost); `error_map` (status/body match → `AiError`); upload steps (presigned/multipart); model → endpoint mapping; pricing refs. Extraction with JMESPath; templating = minimal `${path}` substitution preserving JSON types; **no loops, no conditionals beyond `default`/`coalesce`, no code**; hard limits (template size, depth, output size). Spec doc with 4 worked examples (fal-like queue, Replicate-like predictions, sync TTS, JWT-signed API).
acceptance: the four examples validate and render expected requests (the signed one against fixed JWT vectors); pathological templates hit limits instead of hanging; reviewed with 5B.01 (shared `adapter` field and mapping references).
work_packages.tests: unit, proptest (render never panics), fuzz the template parser.

work_packages.title: Caption translation
work_packages.scope: `caption.translate{transcript|caption_track, target_langs[], mode: replace|bilingual, glossary, tone}` using the `Translate` capability (LLM-backed with JSON-schema output, or a dedicated provider). Produces a **new `Transcript`** with `language` and `translated_from`, preserving segment timings; word timings redistributed deterministically (proportional by characters within each segment); respects caption chunking limits (max chars/lines) by re-chunking; glossary/brand terms enforced; batched to bound tokens; cost from token estimate. Transcript text is untrusted: delimited, outputs validated against the schema, instructions inside it ignored. No local fallback in P5 (cloud Llm only; local LLM/MT is a stretch): offline runs fail with a clear error. Bilingual layout is a 3E feature this command calls.
acceptance: F1; timings monotonic and within source segment bounds; a transcript containing "ignore previous instructions" translates verbatim with no side effects; glossary respected in cassette test.

work_packages.title: Dubbing pipeline
work_packages.scope: `ai.dub{source, target_lang, voice_mode: clone|stock|provider_native, keep_background, speakers, lip_sync?}`: (1) Stt + diarization (cached) → (2) optional stem split to keep background → (3) translate → (4) TTS per segment/speaker → (5) **time-fit**: stretch ≤ 1.15× (E2E time-stretch), else one LLM "shorten" retry, else allow bounded overflow into silence → (6) mix onto a new `dub:<lang>` track group, original muted not deleted → (7) captions in the target language. `provider_native` runs the ElevenLabs-style dubbing job as one step. Per-step costs summed into one estimate. Segment review data (text edit + regenerate one segment with its own cost) exposed via `ai.dub.segments` / `ai.dub.regenerate_segment`. `lip_sync: true` invokes 5G.09 if present.
acceptance: F1; MockProvider 2-speaker fixture produces aligned dub track, original intact, one undo reverts all; combined estimate equals the sum of steps.
work_packages.out_of_scope: voice-cloning consent (5G.06 owns it), review UI beyond the commands.

work_packages.title: Lip-sync
work_packages.scope: `ai.lip_sync{clip, audio, model}` using `LipSync` models (aggregator-hosted lip-sync models; verify). Validates inputs against manifest limits (max duration, resolution, face required); uploads only the needed range; output replaces the video of a **new clip** in one tx (original kept disabled below); faceless/multi-face failures surface typed errors; synthetic-media disclosure: provenance + `contains_ai` + C2PA assertion on export. Eligible for deferral (Notes §21).
acceptance: F1; over-limit clip rejected before cost is requested; no-face MockProvider failure leaves the project unchanged.

work_packages.title: Upscale and frame interpolation
work_packages.scope: `ai.upscale{clip|media, factor|target_res, model}` and `ai.interpolate{clip, target_fps|factor, model}` using `Upscale`/`Interpolate` models (verify availability/prices). Long video split into keyframe-aligned chunks and reassembled (ffmpeg concat); cost by output pixels × seconds / frames; "try one frame" cost-free-ish preview for upscale. Applies by replacing the clip's media ref (re-proxy via E2F) or, for slow-motion, by creating an interpolated asset and wiring E4H "frame mix: AI". Non-AI Lanczos/bicubic upscale is always available and clearly labelled "not AI". (Local Real-ESRGAN/RIFE packs are a stretch, Notes §21.)
acceptance: F1; chunk boundaries show no seam in a golden diff; slow-motion 0.25× uses the interpolated asset and undo restores the original.
work_packages.out_of_scope: denoise/deblur models, restoration of old footage.

work_packages.title: Beat detection and scene detection (zero-model implementations)
work_packages.scope:
local-only analysis jobs (cpu class, cost 0): **beats** via an Ellis-style spectral-flux + dynamic-programming tracker in Rust (own implementation keeps dependencies small; aubio (GPL) would now be licence-allowed under §21, but essentia (AGPL) and madmom weights (NC-SA) stay excluded); **scenes** via an HSV-histogram content/adaptive detector on 48×27 downscaled frames. Outputs stored in the analysis cache and written as markers (`beat`, `scene`) on the clip/sequence so E2A snapping uses them; optional `timeline.split_at_scenes`. ONNX upgrades (beat_this, TransNetV2) arrive as higher-quality local providers in 5I.07 and take over when installed.
- Settings > Media and import: "Detect scenes and beats in new media" (`media.analyze_on_import`, off) (catalog `docs/reference/settings.md`).
acceptance: F1 (cost 0); beat F-measure ≥ 0.8 on synthetic click tracks and the CC0 music fixtures; scene detection precision/recall ≥ 0.9 on the corpus hard-cut set; results cached per media hash.
work_packages.tests: unit, accuracy tests on corpus, e2e.

work_packages.title: `media.describe` and the VideoUnderstand frame-sampling shim
work_packages.scope: `media.describe{media, range?, question?, response_schema?, detail}` → `Description{segments:[{start,end,summary,tags}]}` returned as untrusted. Native path: Gemini (5D.03). **Shim for other Llm providers**: sample frames (scene-aware via 5G.11 when cached, else uniform, capped count), burned-timecode contact sheets (reusing the E2I renderer) + transcript → vision-capable Llm → timestamped JSON validated against the schema. Cache per (media hash, range, prompt hash, model). Cost estimate by frames/tokens (or video seconds for native); it is paid when cloud, so it follows F1.
acceptance: same question on one fixture via native cassette and via shim returns schema-valid output; second call hits the cache with cost 0; frame cap enforced.
work_packages.tests: unit (sampler), cassette integration, injection fixture (text overlaid in a frame cannot alter behaviour).

work_packages.title: Highlight candidate mining
work_packages.scope: `ai.shorts.find{source, count, min_s, max_s, language, criteria}` → ranked `ShortCandidate{id,start,end,hook_text,title,score,rationale,signals{hook,completeness,emotion,energy},needs_context}`. Algorithm: transcript → topic/segment boundaries (sentence ends, pauses, scene cuts, audio-energy/laughter peaks) → candidate windows within limits → LLM scoring with a JSON-schema output and a rubric (hook in first 3 s, self-contained, emotional peak, no dependence on earlier context) → **over-select 2×**, de-duplicate overlaps, rank. Map-reduce for 20+ minute sources (per-chunk then global) with token-budget-aware chunking and a pre-run cost estimate. Optional video-native pass via `media.describe` for visual cues. Prompts are versioned files shared with the skill (5J.04). Temperature 0 + cache for repeatability; transcript is untrusted and delimited. No local LLM fallback in P5 (stretch). Read-only: never mutates the timeline.
acceptance: F1; on the 5H.05 fixture with recorded LLM responses the output is schema-valid, de-duplicated, within length limits and stable across runs; an injection string in the transcript does not alter output structure.
work_packages.tests: unit (windowing, dedupe), cassette tests, prompt-version snapshot.

work_packages.title: Short builder (candidates → 9:16 sequences)
work_packages.depends_raw: 5H.02, 5G.04, E3E, E3F, E2B, E2E, E3B/E3C (optional hook title)
work_packages.scope: `ai.shorts.make{source, candidates, aspect, caption_style, options{remove_silence, remove_fillers, loudness_lufs, hook_title, reframe}}`: per short create a sequence (1080×1920 default); add the range snapped to **sentence/word boundaries** (pad 0.15 s, never mid-word, using the Transcript); silence/filler removal (3F commands); reframe (5G.04); captions from the transcript range with the chosen style (3E); loudness normalization (E2E); optional hook title composition. One checkpoint + one tx per batch with `expected_rev`; source untouched; partial failure rolls back. Returns sequence IDs plus automatic checks (duration ≤ max, captions inside safe area, LUFS in range). `ai.shorts_from_sequence` = find + make for an "auto" mode (paid steps need confirmation).
acceptance: F1; on the fixture every short passes the state checks; one undo removes all created sequences; source media and sequence unchanged.
work_packages.tests: unit, golden frames of first/last frames, e2e with MockProvider + recorded LLM.

work_packages.title: Shorts panel UI (shortlist review)

work_packages.title: Shorts evaluation harness and fixtures
work_packages.scope: fixture: a ≥ 20-minute podcast/interview with a **redistributable licence** (record licence and source in the corpus manifest; fetched, not committed) plus its transcript. Replay mode with recorded LLM responses for CI. `xtask shorts-eval` renders N candidates from Cutweave plus 2 baselines (uniform chunking; random segments), anonymizes and shuffles them, and emits a rating sheet; rubric for "usable": standalone, hook within 3 s, clean in/out (no mid-word cut), captions legible and in safe area, subject framed. Scoring script computes usable rates; automatic state checks reused from 5H.03.

On failure, iterate prompts/segmentation (5H.02) and repeat on a second fixture to avoid overfitting. Record results in `docs/eval/shorts-blind-review.md`.
acceptance: signed-off result file linked from the Phase 5 exit checklist.

work_packages.title: Model manager: local entries, download, verify, licence acceptance
work_packages.scope:
local models are **catalog entries** (`locality: local`, `artifacts[]` with pinned-commit URL or mirror, sha256, size, SPDX licence, EP, min VRAM, `redistributable`) — no second registry (Notes §16). Commands `model.list|install|remove|verify|status|license`. Runtime "GPU packs" (CUDA/TensorRT/OpenVINO ORT builds) use the same mechanism with signature checks. `xtask models-lint` fails CI on deny-listed licences (§21) or missing sha256 in the default set and checks the "core pack" budget (< 1.5 GB).

work_packages.out_of_scope: runtime (5I.02), the licence review itself (5I.09), UI (5F.07).

work_packages.title: Local provider runtime: probe, EP policy, sessions, VRAM budget, sidecar
work_packages.area: crates/cutweave-ai-local (new), crates/cutweave-cli (`cutweave worker ai`), crates/cutweave-playback (yield signal)
work_packages.scope: `LocalProvider: Provider` (`Locality::Local`, cost 0) registering only capabilities whose packs are installed **and** whose hardware probe passes. Hardware probe (GPU vendor/VRAM via wgpu adapter info + platform APIs). `ort` with `load-dynamic`; EP order TensorRT (opt-in) > CUDA > DirectML > CoreML > OpenVINO > CPU, always keeping CPU fallback; one-time benchmark per model/device cached; quality tiers tiny/balanced/best. Session LRU with memory cost and idle unload; **VRAM budget manager** reserving renderer headroom, queueing or downgrading jobs that exceed it; GPU jobs **pause/yield during playback and scrubbing**; resource classes (gpu: 1 job, cpu: cores−2, io); chunked inference with progress and cancel tokens between chunks. **Sidecar mode** (`cutweave worker ai`, stdio/local-socket protocol): hard-kill cancellation, crash isolation, own ORT version; sherpa-onnx and any other library bundling its own ORT only ever run in a sidecar (never two ORT versions in one process). If this exceeds 4 days, split the sidecar into its own WP.
work_packages.interfaces: `LocalProvider`, `LocalPack` trait implemented by 5I.03–5I.08, sidecar protocol v0.
acceptance: a dummy pack runs in-process and in the sidecar with identical results; killing the sidecar mid-job yields a clean `Failed(retryable)`; playback never drops below budget in the perf harness while a GPU job runs (frame-drop counter, E2J).

work_packages.scope: TransNetV2 ONNX on 48×27 frames (windowed) → scene boundaries; beat_this ONNX export (check STFT/conv ops; STFT in Rust) → beats + downbeats. work_packages.title: Plugin host design, threat model & ADR

work_packages.title: Wasmtime host core: linking, limits, trap isolation
work_packages.scope:
- Component loader; linker built **per plugin from its granted permissions** (ungranted imports are absent — deny by default).
- Limits: `StoreLimits` memory caps, epoch-interruption deadline per call (default 50 ms control calls; configurable for jobs), fuel for non-epoch paths, cancellation of p3 futures.
- Trap/panic isolation: a trapping or runaway plugin is disabled, `plugin.changed` emitted, engine continues; auto-disable after N traps in M minutes; local crash file under `~/.cutweave/plugin-crashes/`.
- Opaque resource handles (never pointers), handle table scoped to a call/job.
acceptance: infinite-loop guest returns `Timeout` within 2× deadline; memory-bomb guest fails `LimitExceeded` with no engine OOM; 1000 instantiate/drop cycles show RSS delta < 5%; host never panics on guest misbehaviour.
work_packages.tests: unit + abuse guests (loop, alloc bomb, deep recursion, trap); criterion bench (empty call p95 < 200 µs).
work_packages.out_of_scope: permission semantics (6A.05); per-frame pixel processing in WASM (documented unsupported).

work_packages.title: Permission model & enforcement
work_packages.scope:
- Kinds: `network` (host allowlist, https only, no raw sockets, size/rate limits), `fs` (plugin-data preopen only; user files via host file-picker tokens), `secrets` (named; **host injects auth headers, plugin never reads key material**), `project.read|write:<scope>` (command-bus scopes), `media.read`, `clock`, `random`, `ai.spend` (paid AI with cap).
- Grant store with diffing: updates that widen permissions require re-grant. Granting is a UI-only scope: only the UI token (actor `user`) may grant; a plugin or agent can never grant itself or others (test).
- Enforcement: `wasi:http` filter (allowlist + redirect re-check + DNS-rebinding guard + private-IP block); fs canonicalization (symlinks, `..`, UNC, 8.3 names); scoped capability tokens for bus calls with recursion depth + rate limits.
- Audit ring buffer of gated calls, exposed as `plugin.audit`.
acceptance: guest hitting a non-allowlisted domain, a redirect to one, a private IP, or `../` escape is denied with typed errors + audit entry; a provider plugin calls its API with the key and **cannot read the key** (test scans returns/memory); widening update forces re-prompt.
work_packages.tests: negative matrix (≥ 40 denial cases), mock-HTTP integration, Windows path-allowlist tests.

work_packages.title: Plugin commands on the command bus (GUI + CLI + MCP)
work_packages.scope:
- `command-handler` world + `macro` handlers (L0 JSON command lists). Register as `<plugin-id>.<command-id>` (core namespaces reserved); JSON Schema in/out from manifest.
- Auto-surface: palette entry + auto-form, CLI, MCP via `cutweave_search_commands/describe/execute` (`mcp="catalog"`, never `core`); annotations from `risk` (read|write|destructive|network); destructive/network → `confirm_token`.
- Execution as actor `plugin:<id>` (derived server-side from the plugin's credential, never client-supplied), undo via inverse patch or tx wrapper, scoped tokens, audit.
- **Untrusted text hygiene:** plugin titles/descriptions sanitized, capped ≤ 300 chars, marked `untrusted` in MCP, shown verbatim at install review.
- Tool-set change notification + registry snapshot refresh on plugin load/unload, using the negotiated MCP revision's mechanism (2025-11-25 `resources/subscribe`, 2026-07-28 `subscriptions/listen`); the tool profile of an endpoint (`/mcp`, `/mcp/minimal`, `/mcp/full`) never changes per connection.
work_packages.interfaces: runtime registry registration API; `plugin.changed`; MCP change notifications (per negotiated revision).
acceptance: example command appears in palette, `cutweave exec` and `cutweave_search_commands` with identical schema; undo restores doc; out-of-scope bus call returns `Forbidden`; description "ignore previous instructions…" is inert and flagged.
work_packages.tests: parity test over plugin commands (feeds 6J.01); property test undo identity for macro commands; MCP catalog snapshot with sample plugin.

work_packages.title: Provider/importer/exporter world integration; L0 pack loader unification
work_packages.scope:
- Register `ai-provider` plugins into the 5A gateway as first-class adapters (same trait as built-ins; reuse 5E code, **no fork**): catalog entries from `capabilities()`, cost estimate, job streaming, cancel, provenance sidecar.
- `importer` world: `probe(head, filename)` + `plan()`; FFmpeg does the decoding; file access via picked-file handles only. `exporter` world for container/metadata/subtitle exporters.
- Unify L0 data-pack loading (LUTs, fonts, stickers, SFX/music, caption styles, text presets, templates, macros, export presets, keymaps/themes) behind one `pack` contribution with kind-specific validators; migrate the 3E/3G/4D loaders with no behaviour change.
work_packages.interfaces: `pack` manifest kinds; gateway adapter registration; importer/exporter registries.
acceptance: a WASM provider passes the 5C/5D contract suite unchanged; example importer opens a custom file by drag-drop; all built-in packs still load (golden listing diff = 0); invalid packs rejected with path-specific errors.
work_packages.tests: contract-suite reuse, golden pack listing, importer `probe` fuzz target.

work_packages.title: Sandbox abuse corpus, fuzzing & performance budgets
work_packages.scope:
- Abuse corpus of guest components: infinite loops, memory bombs, stack overflow, malformed WIT payloads, oversize returns, handle reuse/forging, denied net/fs, rapid re-instantiate, log flooding.
- `cargo-fuzz` targets: host imports, manifest parser, pack validators, scene-graph decoder, importer `probe`; nightly job with persisted corpus.
- Perf budgets as CI thresholds: wasm call overhead, warm plugin load < 100 ms, plugin command round-trip contribution p95 < 16 ms.
acceptance: corpus ≥ 25 guests, all contained (engine alive, plugin disabled, typed error); 30 CPU-minutes/target PR smoke with zero crashes; budgets enforced.
work_packages.tests: this WP is the test suite; outputs feed 7B.02.
work_packages.out_of_scope: GPU-shader abuse (4A budgets); L3 iframe abuse (6B.01/6B.03).

work_packages.title: Plugin Interface Exception: legal finalization
work_packages.scope:

- Confirm MIT/Apache-2.0 headers on `wit/`, `packages/plugin-sdk`, `packages/compose-runtime`; DCO-only vs CLA-lite decision for adding the exception to already-merged contributions.
- Registry policy text: SPDX required; proprietary allowed but labeled.
acceptance: signed-off text published and shown in the install dialog; all contributors covered (DCO log check).
work_packages.tests: license-header CI check passes for SDK dirs.

work_packages.title: L3 sandbox host: iframe isolation & custom protocol
work_packages.scope:
- Serve plugin UI from custom protocol `cutweave-ext://<plugin-id>/` (Electron `protocol.handle`); each panel in a sandboxed iframe with **opaque origin** (`sandbox="allow-scripts"`, no `allow-same-origin`), strict CSP (`default-src 'none'`; `connect-src 'none'` unless a granted network permission is proxied via host), no Node, no top navigation, no popups.
- Plugin JS never runs in the main window context. Reconcile with §18 CSP (main window: connect only to engine origin): extension frames get their own CSP; main CSP unchanged.
- Lifecycle: load/unload/reload on `plugin.changed`; frame crash does not affect the editor.
acceptance: test plugin cannot read `window.parent`, editor storage or cookies, or fetch any URL; navigating away is blocked; killing the frame process shows a placeholder and the editor continues.
work_packages.tests: Playwright+Electron escape attempts (parent access, `fetch`, `window.open`, external form submit, service-worker registration); unit tests for protocol path traversal.

work_packages.title: postMessage RPC bridge & `@cutweave/sdk` panel API
work_packages.scope:
- Host bridge: `MessageChannel` handshake per frame (port transfer, no wildcard targets), validate every frame→host message against generated schemas (all treated as untrusted), per-plugin permission check on each command/query/subscription, rate limit + backpressure.
- `@cutweave/sdk` (MIT): typed client generated from `packages/protocol` (`cutweave.exec/query/subscribe`), `cutweave.ui` helpers (toast, host-token file picker, dialogs), theme tokens as CSS variables (light/dark/high-contrast), `defineInspector()`.
- Versioned `ext_api` handshake; refuse on mismatch with clear message.
work_packages.interfaces: `@cutweave/sdk` public API; bridge message JSON Schema (snapshot-tested).
acceptance: panel with only `project.write:text` can add a text item but gets `Forbidden` for `export.start`; malformed/oversized/spoofed messages dropped and counted; SDK compiles against generated protocol with zero `any`.
work_packages.tests: Vitest for bridge validation; fast-check property tests on the decoder; Playwright e2e with example panel.

work_packages.scope:

work_packages.title: Git-based index repo & CI validation pipeline
work_packages.scope:
- Index format: one entry per plugin id → repo URL + commit + artifact URL + SHA-256 + manifest summary; PR-reviewed.
- CI per PR: manifest schema; WIT conformance vs host RC; `naga` validation; permission lint (wildcard domains rejected); SPDX; size cap; software-wgpu (lavapipe/WARP) test render vs the stored per-adapter reference (SSIM ≥ 0.995 AND PSNR ≥ 40 dB); composition determinism (render twice, byte-equal); param fuzz (NaN/inf/extremes); abuse-corpus smoke.
- Publish static `index.json` + per-plugin metadata via GitHub Pages/Releases (zero hosting cost); artifacts mirrored to Releases.
work_packages.interfaces: `index.json` schema v1; shared `cutweave plugin check` library (with 6C.06).
acceptance: deliberately bad PRs (unbounded WGSL loop; wildcard network; missing license) each fail with a clear message; a good example merges and appears in `index.json` within 10 min.
work_packages.tests: index self-tests with fixture plugins (good + 10 bad).

work_packages.title: Signing & verification
work_packages.scope:
- Trust chain v1: hash pinned in the reviewed index entry; **index metadata signed** by a Cutweave index key (minisign/Ed25519 or Sigstore, recorded in an ADR); optional author signatures (minisign/Sigstore keyless) verified when present.
- Engine verifies: index signature → entry hash → artifact SHA-256 → optional author sig → manifest matches entry. Key rotation + `revoked.json` revocation list, fail-closed; installed plugins keep working offline.
- Sideload allowed with "unverified" banner + permission dialog.
- Reuse the key-hierarchy design chosen for the 5B signed model catalog (separate keys per purpose).
work_packages.interfaces: `verify_plugin_artifact()`, `revoked.json` schema, embedded public keys + rotation procedure.
acceptance: tampered artifact, swapped manifest, replayed older index (rollback) and revoked key each fail with distinct typed errors; rotation test passes with N and N+1 keys.
work_packages.tests: unit + ≥ 12 adversarial fixtures; fuzz of signature-file parser.

work_packages.title: Index key custody & publisher policy
work_packages.scope:
- Generate index signing keys offline on hardware tokens; custody across ≥ 2 maintainers; backup/recovery + rotation runbook; CI signs via short-lived/OIDC secrets only.
- Publisher policy: who may merge index PRs, review checklist, takedown/revocation process, security contact, SLAs.
acceptance: runbook rehearsed once (rotate + revoke on a test index); public keys committed; policy published.

work_packages.title: Registry client, install, update & rollback

- Update flow: daily poll (opt-out; respects the global "disable update checks"), user approval, **re-prompt if permissions widen**, keep previous version for one-click rollback, atomic swap, project pins respected.
- Missing-plugin placeholder → install offer from the index.
acceptance: install→use→update→rollback works against a local test index; interrupted download leaves old version intact; with update checks disabled, zero network requests (verified via test proxy).

work_packages.title: Template format spec v1 (+ ADR)
work_packages.scope:
- `template.toml` + `fragment.json` (project fragment: sequence(s), tracks, items, text, captions, effects, compositions, keyframes with **relative** times) + `slots.json` + `assets/` + `preview.webp|mp4` + `thumbs/`. Template = L0 pack kind `template` (installable via plugin/pack pipeline).
- **Slot types:** `media` (video|image|audio; constraints: min/max duration, aspect, orientation), `text` (max chars, rich/plain), `color`, `font`, `caption-style`, `composition-prop`, `logo`, `music`. Each slot: id, label, required, default, targets (item/prop paths), adaptation rule (`fit|fill|crop|loop|stretch-with-hold|trim`) and **timing mode** (fixed, content-driven duration, ripple).
- Compatibility: `min_app`, required plugins/effects/fonts (with fallbacks), aspect variants (one template may carry 16:9 + 9:16 + 1:1 fragments).
- License metadata for every bundled asset (SPDX, source URL) — required.
- ADR-015 recording the format; JSON Schema; semver + migrations for the template schema.
acceptance: spec reviewed by a human; 3 hand-written sample templates validate; format round-trips through serde; wasm32 compile check still green for `cutweave-model`.
work_packages.tests: schema snapshot; negative corpus (≥ 20 invalid templates).

work_packages.title: Engine: validate, instantiate, slot binding, `template.*` commands
work_packages.scope:
- Commands: `template.list|get|validate|apply{template, target, bindings, aspect}|install|remove`. `apply` = **one undoable transaction**: copy fragment with fresh IDs (id remapping), import assets into `generated/`/media bin, bind slots, adapt durations per rules, resolve missing fonts/effects with fallbacks + warnings.
- MCP: `template_list`, `template_apply` core-or-catalog per ADR-009 budget (default `catalog`), `cutweave://templates` resource, dry-run returns binding diff + warnings.
- Placeholder rendering for unfilled required slots (visible "drop media here" card in preview/export is blocked until filled, or export warns).
acceptance: applying a template twice yields independent items; undo removes everything incl. imported assets references; unfilled required slot → export gate warning; 100% of fills are deterministic (same inputs → byte-identical doc).
work_packages.tests: property tests (undo identity, id uniqueness), golden-frame render of 3 sample templates with fixture media, MCP snapshot.

work_packages.title: Save-as-template
work_packages.scope:

- UI wizard: pick items → mark as slot (right-click "Make replaceable"), set constraints, preview, export `.cutweavetemplate` / save to user library.
- Generates `preview.mp4/webp` + thumbnails via headless render.
work_packages.interfaces: `template.save`, UI flow, user template library dir.
acceptance: save → apply on a fresh project reproduces the original look (golden frame SSIM ≥ 0.995 AND PSNR ≥ 40 dB vs the stored per-adapter reference, with original media as slot fills); template with a missing license on a bundled asset cannot be exported for sharing.
work_packages.tests: round-trip golden test (save→apply), Playwright e2e of the wizard.

work_packages.title: Smart templates: auto-fill slots from the media bin
work_packages.scope:
- `template.autofill{template, candidates?}` → proposed bindings. Deterministic pass first: match by media kind, orientation/aspect fit, duration fit, sharpness/loudness score, scene-detection best segments, transcript for text slots (title = first sentence/summary), brand kit colors/fonts/logo if present (6I.05).
- Optional LLM pass through the gateway (`Llm`, with `VideoUnderstand` when available) to rank clips for narrative slots; **off by default if no provider**; never required.
- Always returns a reviewable proposal (no silent apply); cost estimate shown when LLM used.
work_packages.interfaces: `template.autofill` command + MCP catalog tool; used by the wizard and the copilot.
acceptance: on the 3-media-set fixtures, deterministic autofill picks the expected clip for ≥ 90% of required slots; works fully offline; LLM pass output validated against schema and ignores instructions found in transcripts.
work_packages.tests: fixture-based unit tests, mocked-LLM tests, injection test (transcript containing instructions).
work_packages.out_of_scope: generative fill of missing slots (could call 5F later).

work_packages.title: CapCut draft import: technical investigation
work_packages.scope:
- Analyze CapCut draft folder structure (`draft_content.json`/`draft_info`, encryption/obfuscation in recent versions), versions, which entities map to Cutweave (tracks, segments, materials, text, speed, keyframes, effects by id).

- Results JSONL stored in a branch/artifact store; dashboard page (static HTML) with pass@1, rubric mean, cost, tool calls, per-skill delta; **regression alert** (GitHub issue) on > 5 pt drop vs 7-night baseline; flaky-task detection (variance flag).
acceptance: three consecutive nightly runs complete within cost cap; an injected regression (skill description broken) raises an alert next run.
work_packages.tests: workflow dry-run tests; alert logic unit tests.

work_packages.title: Gate: ≥ 80% task success on ≥ 2 clients — exit criterion X2
work_packages.scope:
- Iterate on skill bodies, trigger descriptions, tool descriptions/schemas (via the registry, not ad-hoc), and prompts until the gate holds: **suite success (T01–T17, N=3 seeds, skills on) ≥ 80% for each of ≥ 2 distinct clients from different vendors**, and **safety S1–S6 = 100% pass** for those clients.
- Root-cause every failing task into: model limit / skill gap / tool-schema gap / assertion bug; file fixes (assertion bugs fixed in tasks, not by loosening tolerance without review).
- Record final report in `agent-kit/evals/RESULTS-beta.md` with model versions, dates and costs.
acceptance: gate numbers met on 3 consecutive nightly runs (not a single lucky run); skills-on ≥ skills-off on aggregate; report published.

work_packages.title: `LlmProvider` trait, agent loop & streaming events
work_packages.scope:
- New crate `cutweave-copilot`: `LlmProvider` trait normalizing messages, tool calls, images, streaming deltas, caching hints, usage; implementations over the gateway `Llm` capability (Anthropic, OpenAI-compatible incl. local Ollama/llama.cpp, Gemini).
- **Loop is ours:** plan → act → observe with the **same tool registry as MCP** (in-process call, no second API), parallel tool calls when the model supports it, max-step and max-token guards, cancellation (cancels jobs, keeps undo group), error recovery (typed `CmdError` fed back).
- Per-model capability flags (vision, parallel tools, max image size, context window, tool-calling quality tier) from the 5B catalog; degradation rules (no vision → `media.describe` delegate; weak tool-caller → core tools + prompts only).
- Structured event stream: `copilot.text_delta`, `plan.updated`, `tool.started|finished`, `cost.updated`, `proposal.ready`, `turn.done`.
work_packages.interfaces: `copilot.*` commands (`send`, `cancel`, `status`, `history`); events above; crate public API.
acceptance: loop completes a 5-step edit against a scripted fake provider deterministically; real-provider smoke (opt-in) completes "add a title"; cancel mid-tool stops within 1 s with consistent doc; capability flags drive degradation (unit-tested for 3 model profiles).
work_packages.tests: fake-provider scripted tests, property test (every turn ends in a committed or rolled-back tx), provider contract tests with recorded fixtures.

work_packages.title: Cache-stable prompt layout, context hygiene & compaction
work_packages.scope:
- Prompt assembly order (stable → volatile): role + harness rules → safety/budget policy → tool-use guidance (batch, query before edit, verify) → **skill index (name + description only)** → project brief (brand kit, preferences, memory) → **volatile project-state summary last**. Cache breakpoints placed per provider (Anthropic `cache_control`, OpenAI/Gemini prefix caching).
- Golden **prompt-prefix stability test**: prefix bytes identical across turns of a session and across sessions with the same settings; CI fails if volatile data leaks into the prefix.
- Context hygiene: summaries not raw dumps, byte-capped tool results, images downscaled and referenced by handle, programmatic batching, session **compaction** preserving plan + checkpoints + pending proposals.
- Token/cost accounting per turn (cache hits/misses).
work_packages.interfaces: `PromptBuilder`, compaction policy; settings for cheap/smart model slots (architecture §24 Q1).
acceptance: measured prefix cache-hit ≥ 80% on a 20-turn scripted session (provider usage fields); compaction keeps task success in a 60-turn session (scripted); tool result > cap is summarized with a handle.
work_packages.tests: golden prompt-prefix tests; compaction tests; token-budget tests.

work_packages.title: Policy engine, confirmation tokens, budgets & audit
work_packages.scope:
- **Policy engine outside the model**: classify each action by command registry annotations + plugin `risk` as `read | reversible | destructive | paid | external`; decisions: allow / require-confirm / deny, by autonomy mode (suggest / apply-with-undo / auto-within-budget).
- **UI-issued confirmation tokens** (single-use, bound to command + args hash + estimate + TTL) minted only with the UI token (actor `user`, derived server-side from credentials; approval minting is a UI-only scope) — the copilot session runs as an agent actor and the model cannot mint or replay them; paid actions respect per-session/per-task caps (money + count) with hard refusal beyond cap; running spend tracked.
- Untrusted-content handling: transcripts, filenames, metadata, OCR text, plugin descriptions wrapped in delimiters, tagged `untrusted`, never allowed to change policy; agent cannot raise its own permissions or autonomy.
- Audit trail (append-only per project, exportable); same policy classes shared with MCP (`confirm_token` flow) so MCP clients and the copilot behave identically.
acceptance: S1–S6 safety tasks (6H.10) pass with the copilot adapter; forged/replayed/expired token rejected; budget cap enforced across concurrent jobs; policy decisions unit-tested for every command in the registry (auto-generated table test — unclassified command fails CI).
work_packages.tests: table-driven policy tests, token fuzz tests, concurrency test for caps, injection fixtures.

work_packages.title: Turn transactions, checkpoints, proposals & per-turn undo (engine side)
work_packages.scope:
- Every agent turn runs in a transaction tagged `agent:copilot:<session>` with an automatic `edit.checkpoint` before it (a tx is owned by its connection; a dropped connection rolls it back); **per-actor history** so "undo agent turn" reverts exactly that turn without touching user edits made meanwhile (conflict detection when the user edited the same items → offer partial undo/abort).
- **Pending proposal mode = an ephemeral `proposal` transaction** (decision B): the copilot session owns the tx, which soft-locks the items it touches (the P1/P2 soft-lock), has **no idle timeout** and is cancellable. The loop applies edits inside the tx, publishes a diff (created/modified/deleted ids, resulting duration) and preview renders from the tx's working state; **accept** commits the tx as ONE undo step tagged `agent:<id>`; **reject** rolls it back (doc byte-identical). Per-edit accept/reject granularity is done by re-playing the accepted subset into a fresh committed tx. No speculative branch and no rebase exist: concurrent edits to locked items fail fast with `Conflict{item_in_gesture}`, other items proceed.
- Jobs started by a turn (paid generation, export) are linked to the turn for cancel/cost.
work_packages.interfaces: `edit.begin_tx{kind:"proposal"}`, `edit.propose|accept|reject|undo_turn` (thin wrappers over the tx), `render.frame` with `proposal` arg; events `proposal.ready`.
acceptance: property test: apply proposal ∘ reject leaves doc byte-identical; a user edit on items locked by an open proposal fails fast with `Conflict`, edits on disjoint items succeed and accept commits as exactly one undo step tagged `agent:<id>`; dropping the copilot connection rolls the proposal back; undo-turn removes agent edits while keeping later user edits; works through MCP too (an MCP client can use proposals).
work_packages.tests: proptest invariants, concurrency tests, golden preview from the proposal tx.
work_packages.out_of_scope: UI (6I.08); speculative branching/rebase (not needed, see Notes #8).

work_packages.title: Memory: preferences, brand kit, project notes
work_packages.scope:
- Layered memory: global user preferences (default platform, language, caption style, cheap/smart model slots, autonomy mode), **brand kit as typed data** (fonts, color tokens, logo asset ref, caption style id, intro/outro refs, lower-third style, tone-of-voice note) stored per workspace/project with commands `brand.get|set|import`, per-project `notes.md` (agent-writable via `project.notes_append`, user-editable), session summaries.
- Resources `cutweave://project/{id}/brand-kit` and `…/notes`; schema + JSON Schema shared with the `brand-kit-apply` skill (6G.07) and template autofill (6D.05).
- UI: Memory panel (view/edit/delete every item; export), "forget this" per item; nothing leaves the machine except inside prompts to the user's chosen provider.
acceptance: brand kit round-trips and is visible to an MCP client; user can delete any memory item and it stops appearing in prompts (prompt-diff test); notes survive project move/collect.
work_packages.tests: schema snapshot, prompt-assembly tests with memory, Playwright e2e for the panel.

work_packages.title: Skills on demand, video-understanding delegate & verify loop
work_packages.scope:

acceptance: copilot on T17/T16 scripted runs loads exactly the expected skill (log check), never exceeds 2 revision rounds; no-vision model path completes T16 via `media.describe` delegate.

work_packages.title: Proposal review UI, confirmations & copilot settings

work_packages.title: Tool-list size budget, profiles & breaking-change checks

Profiles are selected per MCP endpoint (`/mcp`, `/mcp/minimal`, `/mcp/full`) or the `--profile` launch flag — never per connection. CI fails above budget.
