work_packages.title: Crash analysis, crash-free-session metric & hardening
work_packages.depends_raw: WP-3I.05 (crash reporting collection, shipped with the Public Alpha), E1L (supervision), WP-6B.04 (error UX pattern)
work_packages.scope:
- Crash **collection** (opt-in, self-hosted, privacy-preserving) moved earlier to **WP-3I.05**; this WP does not re-implement it. It consumes those reports and clean-exit session counts.
- Analysis: symbolication/grouping pipeline tuning (dedupe by stack signature), weekly triage report, P0/P1 labelling rules, top-N crash signatures burn-down with owners.
- **Crash-free metric:** daily aggregate of opt-in sessions (clean-exit flag from 3I.05); dashboard computes the crash-free session rate with a Wilson 95% interval over the final-14-day window, shows n, and evaluates **both** G3 variants: primary (≥ 99.5%, n ≥ 2,000) and fallback (n < 2,000: ≥ 99.5% over ≥ 500 sessions + 72 h soak with zero crashes + zero data-loss bugs, evidence from 7B.03).
- Hardening: add GPU-device-lost and hang detection (watchdog) coverage where 3I.05 left gaps, recovery-UI improvements for the top crash classes, regression tests for every fixed signature.
acceptance: dashboard reproduces the crash-free rate and CI from a seeded synthetic dataset (unit-tested, both G3 variants); every P0/P1 signature has an owner or fix; forced engine panic, renderer crash, GPU loss and hang each group under the correct signature; no PII appears in the analysed dataset (scrub audit on 50 sampled reports).
work_packages.tests: dashboard unit tests on synthetic sessions, signature-grouping tests, scrub audit.
work_packages.out_of_scope: the collection client/endpoint (3I.05), automated issue filing.

work_packages.title: Fuzzing campaign & triage gate
work_packages.scope:
- Ensure `cargo-fuzz` targets with seed corpora for: project load + every migration, command JSON (schema-aware), OTIO/EDL/FCPXML importers, SRT/VTT/ASS parsers, plugin manifest + pack validators + importer `probe` + host imports, template loader, scene-graph decoder, MCP JSON-RPC input, WS RPC frames, effect.toml/WGSL front-end, media probe wrappers (FFmpeg with a sanitizer build where feasible).
- Nightly fuzz on CI/dedicated runner with corpus persistence; apply to OSS-Fuzz (optional) ; ASAN/UBSAN builds.
- **Campaign gate:** ≥ 24 CPU-hours per target (≥ 100 CPU-hours for project-load and importers) over the final two weeks with **zero open crashes/hangs/OOMs**; each found bug gets a regression test in the corpus.
acceptance: ≥ 14 targets live; gate numbers met and report committed; all findings fixed with regression tests (list in report).
work_packages.tests: nightly fuzz job; corpus replay in PR CI (fast).

work_packages.title: Soak-test matrix & forced-crash campaign
work_packages.scope:
- **Soak scenarios** (scripted via MCP/RPC + UI e2e): (1) 4-hour randomized editing session (proptest-driven commands, undo/redo, save/reload) on a 1 h/400-item project; (2) 30-min A/V playback drift nightly (existing) extended to 2 h weekly; (3) 8 h idle with project open; (4) 50-job export queue incl. cancels; (5) plugin load/unload/crash loops ×1000; (6) AI mock-provider jobs ×500 with cancel/resume; (7) repeated open/close of 100 projects.
- Each scenario reports RSS/VRAM/handle/thread growth, dropped frames, errors; thresholds: RSS growth < 10% over 4 h after warm-up, 0 handle leaks, 0 unhandled errors, A/V drift < 1 frame/30 min, 0 underruns at 256 samples.
- **Forced-crash campaign:** 100 forced kills (SIGKILL/TerminateProcess, power-loss simulation via fs-sync fault injection) at randomized points (mid-command, mid-save, mid-export, mid-autosave) → recovery UI → compare doc to journal truth: **0 lost committed commands, 0 corrupted projects** (extends the 20-crash Phase 2 check).
- Matrix: 3 OS × reference machines; weekly full run, nightly subset.
work_packages.interfaces: `cutweave debug kill-at <point>`; soak reports in CI artifacts.
acceptance: all scenarios green on 3 consecutive weekly runs before RC; 100/100 crash recoveries lossless; regression issues filed for any threshold breach.
work_packages.out_of_scope: hardware-specific GPU driver bugs (tracked as known issues).

work_packages.title: Automated a11y checks, keyboard access, focus & screen-reader labels
work_packages.scope:
- Scope doc + checklist mapped to WCAG 2.2 AA success criteria (incl. new 2.4.11 focus not obscured, 2.5.7 dragging alternatives, 2.5.8 target size ≥ 24 px, 3.2.6 consistent help, 3.3.7 redundant entry, 3.3.8 accessible authentication N/A).
- axe-core in Playwright across every in-scope screen/state (light/dark/high-contrast); CI blocks on serious/critical; `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y`.
- Remediate: tab order, visible focus, focus traps/returns in dialogs, dockview panel keyboard nav, command palette semantics, form labels/errors, `aria-live` regions for jobs/toasts/copilot streaming, names/roles on all icon buttons, keyboard-only operation of every non-timeline feature.
- Keyboard-only e2e: import → edit via palette/shortcuts → export without a mouse.
acceptance: axe: 0 serious/critical on all scoped screens in 3 themes; keyboard-only e2e passes; every interactive element has an accessible name (script check).

work_packages.title: Accessible timeline & visual-criteria remediation
work_packages.scope:
- **Timeline (Canvas2D) alternative:** a parallel accessible representation (virtualized ARIA tree/grid "Timeline outline": tracks → items with name, start, duration, selected state) kept in sync with selection; full keyboard editing (move/trim/split/delete/snap by arrow keys with step sizes, announce results via live region); satisfies 2.5.7 (every drag has a non-drag alternative: nudge/command/inspector fields).
- Visual criteria: contrast ≥ 4.5:1 text / 3:1 UI components in all themes (token audit script), high-contrast theme, `prefers-reduced-motion` and `prefers-contrast`, 200% zoom/reflow of dialogs, 24 px minimum targets, no color-only meaning (e.g. track colors, error states), caption-style preview not relied upon for UI.
- Performance guard: accessible tree must not regress timeline budget (≥ 55 fps at 5k items — virtualized to visible region).
- The high-contrast theme is a third option of Settings > Appearance > Theme (WP-1M.11).
acceptance: a user can perform select/move/trim/split/delete with keyboard only and hear/read results in NVDA, VoiceOver and Orca; token contrast script reports 0 failures; timeline benchmark unchanged (±5%).
work_packages.tests: Playwright keyboard e2e on timeline; contrast script in CI; benchmark guard.

work_packages.title: External accessibility audit & sign-off (human)
work_packages.scope: engage an accessibility auditor (or qualified contributor with AT expertise) to test in-scope screens with NVDA (Win), VoiceOver (mac), Orca (Linux), keyboard-only and zoom/high-contrast; produce a report mapped to WCAG 2.2 AA; triage findings into fix WPs (tracked here, fixed by sonnet agents); re-test; publish an Accessibility Conformance Report (VPAT-style) with known limitations (Canvas preview).
acceptance: **no open AA-level failures** in scope; any exceptions explicitly listed with rationale and approved; sign-off recorded by named reviewer.

work_packages.title: i18n infrastructure, RTL support & pseudo-localization
work_packages.scope:
- ICU MessageFormat (plurals, select, gender), string extraction + CI (fail on hard-coded UI strings, missing keys, unused keys, unbalanced placeholders), pseudo-locale (accents + 40% expansion + RTL pseudo) used in visual regression to catch truncation.
- Locale-aware date/time/number/duration formatting; engine error **codes** → localized messages in UI (engine never ships display strings the UI cannot translate); locale switch without restart; CJK/Arabic/Hebrew/Devanagari font fallback in chrome.
- **RTL:** logical CSS properties throughout, mirrored icons list, `dir` handling in dialogs/panels; **timeline time axis stays LTR** (documented decision; Notes #8), transport controls not mirrored; bidi text in inspector/text fields; captions/text engine bidi verified via 3A (shaping tests with Arabic/Hebrew samples).
- Settings > General gains "Language" (default: the OS language when Cutweave has it, else English), applied without a restart, main's menus included (catalog `docs/reference/settings.md`).
acceptance: pseudo-locale and RTL-pseudo e2e screenshots show no clipped/overlapping text in the 12 core screens (visual diff review recorded); string-lint passes; Arabic text renders shaped (no disconnected letters) in the Text tool preview and export golden.
work_packages.tests: string lint, visual regression in pseudo/RTL locales, text-engine bidi golden tests.

work_packages.title: Language packs: es, pt-BR, fr, de, ja, zh-Hans, ar
work_packages.scope:
- Machine-first translation (LLM with glossary: video-editing terms consistent with CapCut/Premiere-localized equivalents, "do not translate" list: Cutweave, MCP, WGSL, FFmpeg…) of ~all UI strings (+ templates names, error messages, plugin manager) for **6 shipped languages + Arabic** (RTL check pack).
- Glossary per language; length-budgeted strings; plural forms per CLDR.
- Ships as `core` locale packs (L0); community contribution workflow documented (Weblate/Crowdin decision in Notes #8).
- Human review step is tracked in 7C.06.
acceptance: 100% key coverage per language; lint passes (placeholders, plurals); screenshot pass of 12 core screens per language with no overflow (visual regression); app starts and switches language live.
work_packages.tests: i18n lint, visual regression per locale.

work_packages.title: Native-speaker review & RTL sign-off (human)
work_packages.scope: one native/fluent reviewer per language spot-checks ≥ 150 strings each (timeline/inspector/export/errors prioritised) and rejects mistranslations; an Arabic-reading reviewer signs off RTL layout across the 12 core screens.
acceptance: each language: ≥ 95% of sampled strings approved, rest fixed; RTL checklist signed.

work_packages.title: §19 budget dashboard & CI gates
work_packages.scope:
- Map each of the 10 §19 rows to a named benchmark id, scenario fixture (generated projects: empty, 1 h/400 items, 5k items, 4K long-GOP, 1080p60 3-layer + 2 effects + animated captions), reference machine (P0 definitions incl. iGPU M1 / Intel Xe) and threshold = the budget; nightly job writes JSON; static dashboard (green/red per budget, 30-day trend); **PR gate** on regressions > 5% vs baseline for criterion benches; release gate = all rows green.
- Runner strategy: self-hosted reference runners for GPU/HW-encode rows (hosted runners only for software-adapter checks); noise control (CPU governor, repeat N=5, median/p95 rules per row).
- Rows (copied): app start → editable project < 2.5 s; open 1 h/400-item project < 2 s; command RTT p95 < 16 ms; scrub p95 < 80 ms (proxy/intra) and < 150 ms (4K long-GOP no proxy); playback 1080p60 (3 video layers + 2 effects + animated captions, iGPU) 0 dropped frames over 60 s; timeline pan/zoom 5,000 items ≥ 55 fps; A/V offset < 40 ms and drift < 1 frame/30 min; export 1080p H.264 (HW) ≥ 2× realtime; idle memory 1 h 1080p project < 1.5 GB.
work_packages.interfaces: `tools/perf/budgets.toml` (single source of truth), dashboard artifact, CI job `perf-gate`.
acceptance: all 10 rows measured automatically on all reference machines; each row shows current value vs budget; seeded 20% regression flips the relevant row red and fails the PR gate.
work_packages.tests: self-test of the gate with a synthetic regression.

work_packages.title: Startup, project-open & memory budgets burn-down
work_packages.scope: profile (tracing, samply/Instruments/WPR) and fix until green: **app start → editable empty project < 2.5 s**, **open 1-hour/400-item project < 2 s to interactive** (lazy thumbnail/waveform loading, snapshot build cost, sqlite index warm-up), **idle memory < 1.5 GB** with a 1 h 1080p project (frame-cache sizing policy, thumbnail pyramid caps, no leaks per 7B.03); heap profiling (dhat/heaptrack) report; cold vs warm start distinction documented (budget applies to warm start on reference machine; cold start reported).
acceptance: the three rows green on all reference machines for 7 consecutive nightly runs; heap report shows no unbounded growth over a 1 h idle + edit loop.

work_packages.title: Playback, scrub & A/V sync budgets burn-down
work_packages.scope: fix until green: scrub p95 < 80 ms (proxy/intra) and < 150 ms (4K long-GOP no proxy); 1080p60 playback with 3 video layers + 2 effects + animated captions on iGPU (M1/Intel Xe) with **0 dropped frames over 60 s**; A/V offset < 40 ms and drift < 1 frame/30 min (nightly 30-min and weekly 2-h checks). Typical levers: quality-ladder policy, decode-ahead tuning, GPU buffer pooling, shader pass merging, HW decode defaults, audio buffer sizing. Also verify third-party/first-party effect GPU budgets (4A) still hold under the combined load.
acceptance: rows green on all reference machines (Win11, macOS arm64, Ubuntu 24.04) for 7 consecutive nightly runs; no regression in golden frames (vs the stored per-adapter reference: SSIM ≥ 0.995 AND PSNR ≥ 40 dB; preview vs pre-encode export on the same adapter bit-identical).
work_packages.tests: playback/scrub/sync benchmarks and the nightly 30-min sync soak.
work_packages.out_of_scope: new features; HDR; zero-copy interop beyond what Spike 3 delivered.

work_packages.title: Timeline, command RTT & export-speed budgets burn-down
work_packages.scope: fix until green: timeline pan/zoom with 5,000 items ≥ 55 fps (with accessible tree from 7C.02 and proposal layer from 6I.08 active); command round-trip UI→engine→patch→UI p95 < 16 ms (including when a plugin handler or the copilot is active); export 1080p H.264 simple timeline with HW encode ≥ 2× realtime on each OS (NVENC/QSV/AMF, VideoToolbox, VA-API) with the software fallback measured and documented.
acceptance: rows green for 7 consecutive nightly runs; HW-encode availability matrix documented (which GPUs verified).

work_packages.title: Third-party notices generation & license audit
work_packages.scope:
- Build-time generation: `cargo-about` (Rust), JS license collector (pnpm/electron-builder deps), bundled FFmpeg + codec libs (from the FFmpeg build manifest), bundled fonts, LUTs, sticker/music/SFX packs, templates, caption styles, effect packs and the Agent Kit — each with license text and attribution (CC-BY credits included).
- Outputs: `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt` + HTML in the installer and **About → Licenses** screen (searchable); machine-readable `licenses.json` in the release.
- CI: `cargo-deny` + JS equivalent fail on unknown/forbidden licenses (GPL-incompatible, non-redistributable, "nonfree"), and on any bundled asset without an SPDX entry; SPDX header + DCO + LICENSE-file audit: `LICENSE` (GPL-3.0), plugin exception, MIT/Apache headers on `wit/`, `packages/plugin-sdk`, `packages/compose-runtime`.
acceptance: installer contains the notices file and the About screen renders ≥ 99% entries of the SBOM (script compares to SBOM, 7A.01); CI fails on a seeded GPL-incompatible dependency and on an unlicensed asset; license-header audit script passes.
work_packages.tests: CI checks; unit tests for collector; e2e About screen.

work_packages.title: FFmpeg build, source offer & GPL compliance
work_packages.scope:
- Pinned, reproducible FFmpeg build scripts for all OSes (GPL build with x264/x265/etc. as allowed by §21; no `--enable-nonfree`; HW APIs per OS), producing shared libs bundled in the app; versions and configure flags recorded.
- **Per-release source offer:** publish alongside each release: exact FFmpeg source tarball (or git commit + verified mirror), all patches, build scripts, full `configure` line, third-party codec library sources/versions; a **written offer** (≥ 3 years) in the installer, About screen and docs; `ffmpeg -version`/`-buildconf` output embedded and compared with the published configure flags by CI.
- Flatpak variant documented (uses codecs extension; Notes #9).
- Source mirror is retained for ≥ 3 years (release assets, not only upstream).
acceptance: CI verifies that the bundled library build-flags (read from the shipped binaries) equal `ffmpeg-build-info.json` and that the source tarball hash is listed in the release; rebuilding from the published source + scripts reproduces the library hash (or documented diffs); `--enable-nonfree` absent (scripted check).
work_packages.out_of_scope: FFmpeg upstream patches; codec patent licensing (7F.03).

work_packages.title: Codec patent posture review (human/legal)
work_packages.scope: counsel review of distributing H.264/HEVC/AAC-capable software and bundled encoders/decoders in target jurisdictions; decide and document the posture: prefer OS/HW codecs where available, default export presets (consider AV1/VP9/H.264-HW first; HEVC off by default or HW-only), whether x264/x265 ship in the base build or a separate "codec pack" (research/03 §8.4 suggests an optional pack; architecture §21 allows GPL build — **needs decision**, Notes #9), Flatpak codec extension handling, user-facing disclosure text, region notes; no patent-grant claims anywhere.
work_packages.interfaces: `docs/legal/codec-posture.md`; in-app Export dialog disclosure text; installer/EULA-free notice text.
acceptance: written counsel (or maintainer-with-counsel) sign-off recorded; build config matches the decision (CI check on encoder list); disclosure text shipped.
work_packages.tests: CI check of `ffmpeg -encoders` vs the decision.

work_packages.title: Model-license display & privacy/egress audit
work_packages.scope:
- **Model licenses:** every on-demand downloadable local model (Whisper, ONNX matting/denoise/scene/beat…) shows license, source, size, restrictions (non-commercial?) **before** download and in Settings → AI → Models; hash verification on download; weights never bundled silently (§21). Cloud catalog entries show provider terms link and data-retention note where known.
- **Privacy/egress audit:** automated e2e with a recording proxy and no keys configured, telemetry/crash opt-in off: **only allowed outbound requests** are (a) update check (if enabled) and (b) plugin index fetch (if enabled), both disable-able; with them disabled → zero requests. Keys never appear in logs/crash reports/MCP output/plugin memory (secret-scan test). Provenance sidecars contain no machine-identifying data.
- Privacy statement page (docs) generated from the allowlist of destinations.
acceptance: license dialog shown for 100% of downloadable models (list check vs `models.toml`); egress test passes in 3 configurations (default, all-off, AI-keyed mock); statement matches allowlist exactly (generated).
work_packages.tests: e2e egress audit; secret-scan test; unit tests for hash verification.

work_packages.title: Security review: local API (human-led)
work_packages.scope: human security reviewer (or external firm), assisted by an opus-generated pre-review checklist and automated tooling, tests the engine's local surfaces: token auth entropy/rotation and run-file permissions (`~/.cutweave/run/<pid>.json`), localhost binding and Host/Origin checks (DNS rebinding, CSWSH on `/rpc`), MCP HTTP auth (401/403), CORS, path allowlist (symlinks, `..`, UNC, 8.3 names, junctions), media endpoints (SSRF-like, traversal), confirm-token forgery/replay, `cutweave_execute` abuse (resource exhaustion), job/export file writes, SHM ring permissions, Windows loopback/firewall prompt behaviour, update channel trust. Report severity-rated findings; fixes tracked as follow-up WPs; re-test.
acceptance: **0 open High/Critical** findings; Medium findings fixed or accepted with written rationale; re-test evidence attached.
work_packages.tests: regression tests added for every fixed finding.

work_packages.title: Security review: plugin sandbox & supply chain (human-led)
work_packages.scope: review wasmtime host configuration and version (known CVEs, p2/p3 features enabled), permission enforcement bypass attempts (network allowlist redirect/DNS tricks, fs escapes, secret exfiltration through logs/errors/timing), command-bus scope escapes and recursion, L3 iframe sandbox escapes (CSP, protocol handler traversal, postMessage spoofing), plugin-supplied-text injection into MCP/copilot, GPU shader DoS handling, index/signing chain (rollback, key rotation, revoked keys), OAuth token isolation (6F.01), update path. Includes a time-boxed red-team exercise with the abuse corpus extended by the reviewer.
acceptance: **0 open High/Critical**; accepted-risk register for residual GPU DoS documented honestly in the plugin docs; re-test evidence.
work_packages.tests: regression tests/corpus additions for each finding.

work_packages.title: Electron hardening verification & supply-chain gates
work_packages.scope:
- Verify §18 hardening with automated checks: `contextIsolation`, `sandbox: true`, no `nodeIntegration`, strict CSP (connect only to engine origin), validated IPC (schema per channel), Electron **fuses** set (disable `runAsNode`, `nodeCliInspect`, enable ASAR integrity/only-load-from-asar), `webSecurity` on, navigation/new-window denial, permission request handler default-deny (mic only on user action), no remote content; run Electronegativity (or equivalent) and fix findings.
- Supply chain: `cargo-deny` (advisories, bans, licenses), `cargo-audit`, `pnpm audit` (high+ blocking, with reviewed ignore list), lockfile integrity, GitHub Actions pinned by SHA, least-privilege tokens, SBOM vulnerability scan (grype/osv) in the release workflow, provenance attestations verified; Dependabot/Renovate policy for security updates with SLA.
acceptance: automated checks assert every setting (fail on deliberate regression); release SBOM scan shows 0 known High/Critical vulnerabilities (or documented, time-boxed ignores); all workflow actions pinned.

work_packages.title: Release candidates, bug bash & 1.0 go/no-go (human)
work_packages.scope:
- Feature freeze, RC builds (`rc.1…`) through beta channel; structured **bug bash** (maintainers + volunteers across 3 OSes; checklist of core flows, plugin install, templates, AI Studio mock/live, copilot, MCP clients, upgrade from last beta, project migration from earlier alphas/betas) with severity triage; burn-down of P0/P1 (fix WPs created as needed — a contingency budget of ~10 agent-days is reserved).
